0NVY: Sati Namu = He whose Name is 'Sati'. The Sanskrit form of the word 'sati' is 'satya', and its meaning is 'the one who exists'. Its root (dhatu) is 'as', which means 'to be'. So 'Satinam' means: 'that One Oankar, whose Name is: the One who exists'. Purakhu = in Sanskrit, according to etymology, this word has been explained thus: 'puri shete iti purushah', that is, 'the one who lies within the body'. The commonly current Sanskrit meaning is 'man'. In the Bhagavad Gita, 'purakh' is used in the sense of 'atma'. In the Raghuvansh this word occurs in the sense of 'the universe, or the Self', and likewise in the work 'Shishupal Vadh'. In Sri Guru Granth Sahib, 'Purakh' means 'that Oankar who pervades the entire world, that Spirit which is permeating the whole creation'. In the senses 'man' and 'soul' too this word occurs in several places. Akal Murati = the word 'murati' is feminine gender; 'akal' is its adjective, and it too has been written in feminine form. If the word 'akal' stood alone as an attribute-word of Ik Oankar, like 'purakhu', 'nirbhau', 'nirvairu', it would be in masculine form; then it would carry an aunkar (u) at its end. The word 'muratu' (with aunkar) is the Sanskrit word 'muhurat'. Words such as chasa and muhurat are used in the division of time; those words are masculine. {Note: it is essential to know the distinction between 'murati' and 'muratu'. 'Murati' is always written with a sihari (i) and is feminine gender. Its meaning is 'sarup' (form). It is a Sanskrit word.} Ajuni = free of the wombs, who does not come into birth. Saibhan = svayambhu (sv = svayam; bhan = bhu), the one who comes into being from his own self, whose light has arisen from himself. Gur Prasadi = by the Guru's prasad, by the Guru's grace — that is, the above 'Ik Oankar' (is attained) by the Guru's grace.

Akal Purakh is One, whose Name is 'the One who exists' (hond vala), who is the Creator of the creation, who pervades all, is free of fear, free of enmity, whose form is beyond time (that is, whose being is imperishable), who does not come into the wombs (does not take birth), whose light has come into being from His own self, and who is met through the grace of the Satguru.
One Universal Creator God. The Name Is Truth. Creative Being Personified. No Fear. No Hatred. Image Of The Undying, Beyond Birth, Self-Existent. By Guru's Grace ~
There is but one God. True is His Name, creative His personality and immortal His form. He is without fear sans enmity, unborn and self-illumined. By the Guru's grace He is obtained.

In the Vedas' own teaching, the numeral 'One' (ek) is not stated before 'Om' at the beginning; here it has been stated. The purport of this is so that it may become evident to all that the settled principle (siddhant) is that Reality is non-dual (advait), not dual — hence jiv and Ishvar are of one form, not two as in the doctrine of the dualists (bhed-vadis). Some give this reason for stating the numeral 'One' at the beginning: that this teaching is common to men and women alike; whereas in the Vedas, apart from the men of the three varnas, all women, and the men of the remaining varnas, have no sanction to utter 'Om' with the mouth. So — in order both to give a teaching common to all, and also to keep intact His own injunction stated earlier in the Vedas — with this consideration Parmeshvar placed a veil (parda) before 'Om', so that all might speak it from behind the veil; in speaking it veiled there is no fault. Understanding this same point, the rishis instructed Valmiki with the reverse of the 'Ram' mantra, teaching him 'Mara'. The meaning of the veil is this: rendering the recitation in a manner other than the original reading. On this view too the meaning of 'One' is the same as stated before. As for the meaning of 'Om': the grammarians, from the mere taking of the name, call it Parmeshvar, 'the One who protects'; they form it from the root 'av', and the meaning of 'av' is 'protection' — hence the name of the Protector is said to be 'Om'. And those of the other granths (take) 'a' + 'u' + 'm', these three (letters — source breaks off here).
RBP6: Japu = the name of this entire bani is 'Japu'.
'Japu' is the name of the bani.

From the saying of the word 'Jap' at this place, the name of this bani is indeed called 'Japu'. The Parmatma whose Name's jap has been enjoined — of what kind is that Parmatma? On this it is said: (Karta) He is the cause of the entire world. The sense is this: so long as the defining mark (lachhan) of a thing has not been stated, until then the establishing (siddhi) of that thing does not take place. Therefore, of that Ishvar whose Name's jap has been stated, His defining mark too ought to be stated; otherwise His establishing will not take place. Now, the defining mark is of two kinds: one the svarup-lachhan (the mark of the thing's own nature) and one the tatasth-lachhan (the incidental mark). There, the attribute which — through being not different from the thing's own nature, that is, through being the thing's very nature — is invariable (avibhichari), and makes the thing known as distinct from others, is the svarup-lachhan. As when someone asked, 'Which is Devdatt's house?', and he replied, 'The one that is highest of all and has an upper storey — that is Devdatt's house'. This is a svarup-lachhan, because being-highest-of-all and possessing-an-upper-storey, both being of the very nature of the thing that is Devdatt's house, are invariable, and they make that house known as distinct from other houses. And the attribute which, through being different from the thing's own nature, is variable (vibhichari), and yet makes the thing known as distinct from others — that is the tatasth-lachhan. As in: 'the one with the crow is Devdatt's house', because the crow's (source breaks off here).
J92N: Adi = from the very beginning. Sachu = the one who exists. The word 'sachu' is the Prakrit of the Sanskrit 'satya', whose root is 'as'; 'as' means 'to be'. Jugadi = from the beginning of the ages. Hai = that is, He exists at this present time as well.
Akal Purakh has existed from the very beginning; He has been present from the beginning of the ages.
True In The Primal Beginning. True Throughout The Ages.
True in the prime, True in the beginning of ages,

'Adi' means: even before the creation of all, that Purakh was Sach (existent) alone. When the subtle and gross expanse (prapanch) had come into being, but the dharma of Satjug and the other ages had not yet been extended — the name of that period is 'Jugadi' — in that period too He was Sach alone.
K0U6: Nanak = O Nanak! Hosi = will be, will remain. ||1||
O Nanak! He is present at this time as well, and in the time to come too He will remain the One who exists. ||1||
True Here And Now. O Nanak, Forever And Ever True. ||1||
True He is even now and True He truly, shall be, O Nanak!

'Hai bhi sachu' — now, in the period of the whole world's subsistence too, He is Sach. Sri Guru Nanak Ji says: 'hosi bhi sachu' — in the future, even in the period of the whole world's dissolution (pralaya), He will be Sach alone. ||1|| Then, for the easy understanding of seekers, condensing it, they state the meaning of this Mantra (the Mool Mantar): the One who is 'Om', the Parmatma of auspicious form. He is 'Sati' — free of destruction in all three times. 'Namu' means the nam-rup which is the world; of that He is the 'Karta' (maker). 'Purakhu' — He is seated within all the bodies, which are the puris (dwellings). 'Nirbhau' — He is free of fear; and 'Nirvairu' — He has enmity with no one. Further, 'Akal Murati' means: His form is free of death. They state the reason for His being free of death: that Hari is 'Ajuni' — He is not received into a mother's womb; and 'Saibhan' — He is of self-effulgent form. Such a Parmeshvar, 'Gurprasadi', is known through the Gurus' grace, or through their being pleased. 'Japu' — O Angad Ji! Recite this Mantra. By implication, causing others to recite is also included: come, recite. It is in connection with this very word that the name of the Mantra too came to be 'Japu'. Question: the Sat Brahm who exists in all three times — is His attainment achieved by purification (soch), or by keeping silent, or by staying hungry, or by exercising cleverness? Kindly tell us. Answer:
BL70: Sochai = by keeping purity, by maintaining cleanness. Sochi = suchi, purity, cleanness. Na hovai = cannot come about. Sochi = were I to keep purity.
Even if I keep (bodily) purity a hundred thousand times (through bathing and the like), (even so, by) keeping purity in this way, purity (of the mind) cannot come about.
By thinking, He cannot be reduced to thought, even by thinking hundreds of thousands of times.
By pondering on God, man cannot have a conception of Him, even though he may ponder over lacs of times.

By 'soch', the performing of purification, the antahkaran (inner faculty) does not become pure — free of rag and dvesh (attachment and aversion) — even if purification be performed hundreds of thousands of times. Or: atam-vichar (reflection upon the Self) is not attained through performing purification, even if one performs purification hundreds of thousands of times. The sense is this: outer purification is the cause of the body's cleanness; the inner filth of rag, dvesh and the rest is removed through maitri (friendliness) and the other virtues. When rag and dvesh have been removed, then through vichar, by means of gyan, the attainment of the True Reality takes place.
GJW9: Chupai = by remaining silent. Chup = stillness, the mind's silence, the mind's settledness. Lai raha = were I to keep applied. Liv tar = the cord of liv, the string of absorption, unbroken samadhi.
Even if I keep an unbroken (bodily) samadhi applied, (even so, by) remaining silent in this way, the mind's stillness cannot come about.
By remaining silent, inner silence is not obtained, even by remaining lovingly absorbed deep within.
Even though one be silent and remains absorbed in Lord's constant love he obtains not mind's silence.

By the speech's remaining silent, the stillness which is the mind's peace — free of sankalp and vikalp (the mind's resolves and waverings) — does not come about, even if one were to keep the (liv) vritti (mental current) applied like a continuous stream of oil.
ZERL: Bhukh = trishna, greed. Bhukhia = while remaining subject to craving. Na utri = cannot be removed. Banna = were I to bind up, gather in. Puri = world, realm. Puria bhar = the loads of all the realms. Bhar = the aggregates of goods.
Even if I gather in the heaps of the goods of all the realms, even so, while remaining subject to trishna (craving), the craving cannot be removed.
The hunger of the hungry is not appeased, even by piling up loads of worldly goods.
The hunger of the hungry departs not, even though they may pile up loads of the world's valuables.

By staying hungry — that is, by performing emaciating vows such as the chandrayan fast — or, (bhukhia) for those possessed of craving, the hunger for Maya does not depart; that is, trishna is not brought to cessation, even if the loads of the goods of all the realms, Indra's and the rest, were bound up and given over. The sense: even upon obtaining all these goods, craving only keeps on growing.
9MN2: Sahas = thousands. Sianpa = clevernesses. Hohi = should there be. Ik = even one cleverness.
Even if there should be thousands and hundreds of thousands of clevernesses (in me), (still, of them all) not even one cleverness stands by one.
Hundreds of thousands of clever tricks, but not even one of them will go along with you in the end.
Man may possess thousands and lacs of wits, but not even one (goes with him) avails him in the Lord's court.

If a person should possess (sahas) thousands upon hundreds of thousands of worldly clevernesses, even then, in the attainment of Parmeshvar, not even one force of those clevernesses goes (nali) along with him — that is, it is of no help. Question:
MK1Q: Kiv = in what manner. Hoiai = can one become. Kurhai pali = the wall of falsehood, the partition of falsehood, the screen of falsehood. Sachiara = (sach-alaya) the abode of Truth, fit for the manifestation of Truth.
(Then) how can one become fit for the manifestation of Akal Purakh, and how can the wall of falsehood (within us) be broken?
So how can you become truthful? And how can the veil of illusion be torn away?
How can we be true and how can the screen of untruth be rent?
Then in what manner may one become true with Parmeshvar, and how may the (pali) screen of falsehood (tutai) — that is — be destroyed? Answer:
H0PC: Hukami = in the Hukam. Rajai = the One possessed of raza, Akal Purakh. Nali = along with the jiv itself, from the very origin, since the world was made. ||1||

To walk in the Hukam of Akal Purakh, the Master of raza (sovereign will) — (this alone is the method). O Nanak! (This method) has stood written from the very origin, from when the world came into being. ||1||
O Nanak, it is written that you shall obey the Hukam of His Command, and walk in the Way of His Will. ||1||
O Nanak! By obeying, the pre-ordained order of the Lord's will.

Let a person walk in the Hukam of (rajai) Akal Purakh — that is, in pain and in pleasure let him accept the bhana (divine will) and remain content; thus the screen of falsehood breaks, and one becomes (sachiara) true. Or: walking in the Hukam (rajai) content — that is, pleased — by this one remains true with Parmeshvar. Guru Nanak Ji says: the prarabdh karma that stands written for me is with me; no one can lessen or increase it — like an arrow already loosed. By understanding it thus, the screen of falsehood breaks. ||1|| Question: you have said one must walk content in the Hukam — how great, then, is that Hukam, hearing which conviction may arise and one's own sense of 'I' (ahanta) may fall away? Answer:
60LK: Hukami = in the Hukam, according to Akal Purakh's Hukam. Hovani = they come to be, come into existence, are formed. Akar = forms, shapes, bodies. Na kahia jai = cannot be stated, cannot be described.
According to the Hukam of Akal Purakh all bodies are formed, (but this) Hukam cannot be told — of what kind it is.
By His Command, bodies are created; His Command cannot be described.
By the Lord's order bodies are produced. His order cannot be narrated.

First: His Hukam in its entirety cannot be told, for it is limitless; yet even so, something is related. All these gross bodily forms (akar), in their entirety, come to be by the Hukam of the Hukami, Parmeshvar; and by the Hukam alone do jivs attain manifestation (avirbhav). Or: 'akar' by indication — the a-kar, u-kar and m-kar (the three letters of Om), Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesh — all come to be by the Hukam of the (Hukami) Parmeshvar.
UVSL: Jia = beings, creatures. Hukami = according to the Hukam. Vadiai = honour, glory.
According to God's Hukam alone do all beings come to birth, and according to the Hukam alone is honour obtained (at God's door).
By His Command, souls come into being; by His Command, glory and greatness are obtained.
With His fiat the souls come into being and with His fiat greatness is obtained.

Further, through those (forms), the forms of the other jivs too — the stationary and the moving (sthavar and jangam) — all come to be by the Hukam of the Hukami. By the Hukam alone do these jivs receive greatness or littleness.
GLXS: Utamu = excellent, good. Likhi = having been written, according to the writ. Paiahi = are received, are undergone.
In God's Hukam one man becomes good, another bad. In His Hukam alone, according to the writ (of one's own done deeds), pains and pleasures are undergone.
By His Command, some are high and some are low; by His Written Command, pain and pleasure are obtained.
By His command the mortals are make high and low and by His written command they obtain woe and weal.

By the very Hukam of the Hukami have the high and the low come to be — or, the low become high and the high become low. As King Ang's son Ven became low; and Valmiki was low, and by Parmatma's Hukam, through repeating Ram, became high(1). And the written record of pain and pleasure — that, by the Hukam of the (Hukami) Parmeshvar, 'paiahi', that is, is undergone.
P2VG: Ikna = to some men. Bakhsis = gift, bestowal. Iki = some men. Bhavaiahi = are made to wander, are cast into the round of birth and death.
In the Hukam alone does bakhshish (bestowal, from Akal Purakh's door) at times come upon men, and in His Hukam alone are many men made to wander perpetually in the round of birth and death.
Some, by His Command, are blessed and forgiven; others, by His Command, wander aimlessly forever.
Some obtain gifts through His order and some through His order are ever made to wander in transmigration.

To some, by the very Hukam of the Hukami, comes the bakhshish which is the attainment of the atam-pad (the state of the Self). Some, by Parmatma's Hukam, are made to wander perpetually in the eighty-four (lakh births), the round of birth and death.
MX4P: Andari = within God's Hukam alone. Sabhu ko = every being. Bahari hukam = outside the Hukam.
Every being is within God's Hukam alone; no being can be outside the Hukam (that is, a rebel against the Hukam).
Everyone is subject to His Command; no one is beyond His Command.
All are subject to His fiat and none is exempt from His fiat.

So everyone is within the Hukam alone; from Brahma down to the ant, no one is outside the Hukam. Question: if all are within the Hukam alone, then why does the jiv say 'I do this, and I shall do this'? And how may that sense of 'I' and 'mine' (ahanta, mamta) fall away? Answer:
FKUU: Hukamai = the Hukam. Bujhai = should understand. Haumai kahai na = does not speak the words of haumai, does not say 'I, I', does not become self-interested. ||2||
O Nanak! If a man should come to understand the Hukam of Akal Purakh, then he no longer speaks words of self-interest (that is, he then gives up the self-interested life). ||2||
O Nanak, one who understands His Command, does not speak in ego. ||2||
O Nanak! if man were to understand Lord's fiat, then no one would take pride (speak in ego).

Sri Guru Ji says: O Siddhas! If one understands the Hukam, then in no way does he speak (haumai) words of pride — that 'I did this, and I shall do this'. All will accept only the command of Akal Purakh. Question: He whose Hukam is such — how great is His power? For a Hukam runs by force. Answer:
VUQD: Ko = some man. Tanu = strength, the power of Akal Purakh. Kisai = to whichever man. Tanu = capacity.
Whichever man is granted the capacity, he sings God's tan (might) — (that is, he does His praise and recounts those works of His from which His great power stands revealed).
Some sing of His Power-who has that Power?
Who can sing His might? Who has power to sing it?
Who (ko gavai) can sing the entire (tanu) power of that Akal Purakh? Only when such strength be in someone can he sing it.
7AC7: Dati = the bestowed goods. Nisanu = the sign (of the bestowal).
Some man sings His gifts alone, (for) he understands (these gifts to be) the sign (of God's mercy).
Some sing of His Gifts, and know His Sign and Insignia.
Who can sing His bounties and know His resplendent effulgence?
(Nisanu) means manifest — that is, who can know His gift as a directly pointed-out 'this' (idam)? Hence, who can know His power?
MB8C: Some man recounts God's beautiful virtues and beautiful glories.
Some sing of His Glorious Virtues, Greatness and Beauty.
Some chant the Lord's beautiful excellences and magnificences.
His virtues, and further His glories, the (char) four Vedas recount, yet they do not find the end. Who, then, can sing His power?
C5NR: Vidia = through learning. Vikhamu = difficult, hard. Vicharu = gyan. {Note: the word 'char' is an adjective, which with a singular masculine becomes 'charu', and with a plural or with a feminine remains 'char'. But the word 'chari' is the word denoting the number 'four'. As in: (1) 'chari kunt dah dis bhrame, thaki aae prabh ki saam'; (2) 'chari padarath kahai sabhu koi'; (3) 'chacha charan kamal gur laga; dhani dhani ua din sanjog sabhaga; chari kunt dahdis bhrami aaio; bhai kripa tab darsanu paio; char bichar, binsio sabh dua; sadh sangi manu nirmalu hua'; (4) 'tati tirathi nahi manu patiaai; char achar rahe urjhaai'. ||2||}
Some man, by the strength of learning (vidya), sings Akal Purakh's difficult gyan (that is, through the shastras and the like he reflects upon the hard subjects of spiritual philosophy).
Some sing of knowledge obtained of Him, through difficult philosophical studies.
Who can chant God's Knowledge, whose study is arduous?
He, the reflection upon whose Vedanta-learning is greatly (vikhamu) difficult — who can sing His power?
HZSG: Saji = having brought forth, having fashioned. Tanu = the body. Kheh = ashes.
Some man sings thus: 'Akal Purakh, having fashioned the body, (then) turns it to ashes'.
Some sing that He fashions the body, and then again reduces it to dust.
Some sing that He fashions the body and then reduces it to dust.

In the manner that, having (saj) fashioned the (tan) bodies of these jivs, He then (kheh) destroys them — or, as He fashions these bodies out of (kheh) earth and the other elements — who can sing His power?
13CH: Jia = the jivatmas, the souls. Lai = having taken. Deh = gives, puts in. {Note: 'jia' is the plural of 'jiu'. Here the 'h' of the word 'deh' has been used to match the 'kheh' of the previous line. Otherwise the noun 'deh' means 'body', as in 'bhariai hathu pairu tanu deh'. To understand the words 'de', 'dehi' and 'deh' properly, the following lines from Japji are given: (1) 'denda de laide thaki pahi' (Pauri 3); (2) 'aakhahi mangahi dehi dehi, dati kare dataru' (4); (3) 'gura ik dehi bujhai' (5); (4) 'nanak nirguni gunu kare gunvantia gun de' (7); (5) 'bhariai hathu pairu tanu deh' (20); (6) 'de sabunu laiai ohu dhoi' (20); (7) 'aape janai aape dei' (25). de = gives; de = having given; dei = gives; dei = having given; deh = body; dehi = give (imperative-future).}
Some sing thus: 'Hari, drawing the souls out (of the bodies), then puts them (into other bodies)'.
Some sing that He takes life away, and then again restores it.
Some sing that God takes away life and again restores it.

The jiv of subtle form, which, receiving His sustaining power (satta), carries this gross body about; or, He who draws the jiv out of this body and puts a jiv into another body — who can sing His power?
4SBX: Some man says: 'Akal Purakh seems far, appears far off';
Some sing that He seems so very far away.
Some sing that God seems and appears to be far off.
He who is far from knowing and far from seeing — who can sing His power?

ELAE: Hadra haduri = present and beholding (hazir-nazir), present in all places.
But some say: '(No, He is near), He is present in all places, He is watching over all'.
Some sing that He watches over us, face to face, ever-present.
Some sing that He is beholding us just face to face.

If one sees Him (hadra haduri) present before the very presence — that is, manifestly — then one can sing His power. Now they state a second meaning: (ko) some — those of the Puranas — in whatever measure they have the strength of intellect, sing Akal Purakh's power by writing out the episodes of the slaying of Madhu and Kaitabh and the rest. Some — those of the Pancharatra persuasion, Narad and the rest — sing knowing hands, feet, eyes and such priceless things to be His manifest gift. Some — those of the Sankhya-shastra persuasion — sing this greatness and these (achar) workings: that through the gunas rajas, tamas and sattva, having framed the Mahat-tattva and the rest, He sustains and destroys. Some — the Naiyayikas — sing Bhagvant's power by reflecting again and again upon the difficult learning. Some — the Kala-vadis (upholders of Time) — knowing Time to be supreme, in the manner that it fashions the body and then destroys it, sing the Lord's power. Some, who are the Mimamsakas, sing the Lord's power from the supremacy of karma: that according to karma Ishvar takes the body away from the jiv, and according to karma gives another body. Some, who are the Patanjalis (the Yoga school), sing the Lord's power knowing Him far from japa and far from seeing. Some, who are Vedantis, sing with the sense of non-duality (advait), knowing Him (hadra haduri) most near — that is, manifestly their own very Self. Question: how great is the katha of such a Mighty One? Answer:
7922: Kathna = to tell, to describe. Kathna toti = the exhaustion of telling, the end of describing the virtues.
The describing of the Hukam has known no exhaustion (that is, by describing and describing, no end of the Hukam could be reached; the Hukam's true form could not be found);
There is no shortage of those who preach and teach.
There is no dearth of persons who dwell upon the Lord's discourses.

As many knowers of the Smritis, Puranas and Shastras as there are, all of them have told the katha of Parmeshvar's power — His true resolve (satya-sankalp) and the rest. But (toti) the end comes to none. Question: if many joined together to tell it, might the end be found? Answer:
Y9R8: Kathi = having told. Kathi kathi kathi = has been told by telling and telling, the telling has been told over and over; the Lord's Hukam has been described countless times. Koti = crore, by crores of beings. {Note — determination of the words koti, kotu, kot: (1) koti = crore (adjective): 'koti karam karai hau dhare; sramu pavai sagle birthare' (3.12, Sukhmani); 'koti khate khin bakhsanhar' (3.30, Bhairau M:5). (2) kotu = fort (noun, singular): 'lanka sa kotu samund si khai' (Asa, Kabir Ji); 'eku kotu panch sikdara' (Suhi, Kabir Ji). (3) kot = forts (noun, plural): 'kanchan ke kot datu kari bahu haivar gaivar danu' (Siri Rag M:1).}
Though crores of beings have described (Akal Purakh's Hukam) countless times.
Millions upon millions offer millions of sermons and stories.
Millions give millions upon millions of descriptions and sermons regarding God.

Crores have told it in the past, crores are telling it now, crores will tell it hereafter — but the end was not found, is not found, and will not be found. Question: what is the Giver like, whose katha is thus without end? Answer:
1UMU: Deda = giving, the giving one, God the Bestower. De = gives (ever), keeps giving. Laide = taking, the beings who receive. Thaki pahi = grow weary.
The Giver, Akal Purakh, keeps on giving (sustenance to all beings), but the beings grow weary of receiving.
The Great Giver keeps on giving, while those who receive grow weary of receiving.
The Giver continues giving but the recipients grow weary of receiving.
That Giver — He who is (deda) the giving one — keeps on giving His gift, while (laide) the receivers grow weary.
32FN: Juga jugantari = juga jug antari, in all the ages, from ever onwards. Khahi khahi = they keep on consuming, have been using all along.
(All beings) have been consuming (the things given by God) from ever onwards.
All the ages through the partakers partake of His provision.
And through the ages upon ages they consume the things (khahi) given by Him; or, they consume again and again.
Q13S: Hukami = the Master of the Hukam, Akal Purakh. Hukami hukamu = the Hukam of Hari, the Master of the Hukam. Rahu = the way, the course of the world.
The Hukam of the Master of the Hukam alone is driving the way (the course of the world).
The Commander, by His Command, leads us to walk on the Path.
The Commander, by His command, makes man walk on His path.
Such an (hukami) Akal Purakh drives many ways within His own Hukam.
6VSN: Nanak = O Nanak! Vigsai = is blossoming, is pleased. Veparvahu = without care, free of anxiety. ||3||
O Nanak! That Nirankar is ever carefree and in bloom (pleased). ||3||
O Nanak, He blossoms forth, Carefree and Untroubled. ||3||
O Nanak! the carefree Master makes merry.

Sri Guru Ji says: O Siddhas! He is (veparvah) free of desire, and He (vigsai) is pleased. The sense is this: Akal Purakh drives all within His own Hukam, and the jivs say, 'I did such a deed, I gave this'. Hearing these words of ignorance He is pleased; He does not become wrathful. ||3|| Question: of what kind are His lordship and His Nam? Answer:
PU7L: Sacha = the one who exists, ever-abiding. Sachu = ever-abiding. Naai = nyaya, justice, law, the law that drives the course of the world. Bhakhia = speech. Bhau = love. Aparu = shoreless, limitless. {Note on 'sachu naai': it is a rule of grammar that the adjective of a noun carries the same gender as that noun. In the line with 'sachu naai', 'sahibu' is masculine, therefore 'sacha' too is masculine. 'Sachu' is masculine, so the noun of which it is the adjective must also be masculine, and must be in the nominative case, as 'sahibu' is. So long as the word 'nau' is used in the nominative or the objective case, its form remains just this, as in: (1) 'amrit vela sachu nau vadiai vicharu' (4); (2) 'changa nau rakhai kai jasu kirati jagi lei' (7); (3) 'jeta kita teta nau' (Pauri 19); (4) 'uche upari ucha nau' (Pauri 24). This same word 'nau' occurs once more in Japji, but there it is a verb and its meaning is 'bathe', as in: 'antargati tirath mali nau' (Pauri 21). The plural of 'nau' occurs twice in Japji; its form is 'nav', as in: (1) 'asankh nav asankh nav' (Pauri 19); (2) 'jia ja (source breaks off here).}
Akal Purakh is ever-abiding, and His law too is forever immovable. His speech is love, and He, Akal Purakh, is Himself limitless.
True is the Master, True is His Name-speak it with infinite love.
True is the Lord, true His Name and the true have repeated His Name with infinite love.

O Siddhas! That Sahib is true, and His Nam too is true. That Nam has been (bhakhia) uttered by those in whom limitless love has arisen. Or: those who have uttered it — to them has come the (bhau) gyan of the limitless Parmatma.
AY0H: Aakhahi = we say. Mangahi = we ask. Dehi dehi = (O Hari!) give us, bestow upon us.
We beings ask gifts of Him and say: '(O Hari! Give us) gifts'. That Bestower makes bestowals.
People beg and pray, "Give to us, give to us", and the Great Giver gives His Gifts.
People pray and beg: "give us alms, give us alms", and the bestower bestows His gifts.
From that Bestower, Akal Purakh, all beg, saying (aakhahi) with the mouth, 'give, give'; and He, according to their karma, gives the fitting gift. Question:
NFYC: Pheri = (if He Himself is making all the bestowals, then) then. Ki = which offering. Agai = before God. Rakhiai = should be placed, should we place. Jitu = by grace of which offering. Disai = might come into sight.
(If He Himself is bestowing all the gifts, then) which offering should we place before that Akal Purakh, by grace of which His Darbar might come into our sight?
So what offering can we place before Him, by which we might see the Darbaar of His Court?
Then, what should be placed before His where-by His court may be seen?

Before that Akal Purakh, what (pheri) offering should we place — or, in return, what should we place(1)? — by which the darshan of that true (darbaru) court, that is, of His own form, might come about?
XPT5: Muhau = from the mouth. Ki bolanu = which word? Jitu suni = hearing by means of which. Dhare = might place, might hold. Jitu = by means of which utterance.
What word should we speak with the mouth (that is, what manner of prayer should we make), hearing which that Hari might hold love (for us)?
What words can we speak to evoke His Love?
Which words should we utter with our mouths by hearing which, He may begin to bear us love?
And what (bolanu) word should we speak with the mouth, hearing which Akal Purakh might take up love? Answer:
Y0C8: Amrit = kaivalya, nirvana, moksha, full bloom. Amrit vela = the hour of amrit, the time of full bloom, the time when a man's mind is generally free of the world's entanglements, early dawn, daybreak. Sachu = ever-abiding. Nau = God's Nam. Vadiai vicharu = reflection upon the glories.
Let it be the time of full bloom (that is, the early-dawn hour); let us (remember) the Nam and reflect upon His glories.
In the Amrit Vaylaa, the ambrosial hours before dawn, chant the True Name, and contemplate His Glorious Greatness.
Early in the morning utter the True Name and reflect upon God's greatness.

O Siddhas! To do the jaap of the True Nam in the amrit vela — let this very thing be placed as the offering; by this alone His Darbar comes into sight. And, reflecting upon His glory — how He has protected the bhagats, and so forth — to do kirtan.
L7P6: Karmi = by the Lord's mercy. Karam = bestowal, mercy. (As in: 'jeti sirathi upai vekha, vinu karma ki milai lai', Pauri 9; 'nanak nadri karmi dati', Pauri 14.) Kaprha = robe, the robe of love, the robe of limitless bhau, the robe of loving praise, the garment of sifat-salah. As in: 'sifati saram ka kaprha magau' (4.7, Prabhati M:1). Nadri = by the glance of God's mercy. Mokhu = mukti, release from 'falsehood'. Duaru = the door, God's door.
(In this way,) by the Lord's mercy the robe of praise (sifat) is obtained; by His glance of grace comes release from the 'wall of falsehood', and God's door is attained.
By the karma of past actions, the robe of this physical body is obtained. By His Grace, the Gate of Liberation is found.
By Good actions the physical robe is obtained and by the Lord's benediction the gate of salvation.

Hearing that, the True Sahib takes up love. And when the jiv, the doer of such worship-form karma, becomes one upon whom mercy rests (karmi), then by (nadri) Hari's glance of grace the (kaprha) siropao (robe of honour) in the form of bhagti is obtained; and from that, the door of moksha — gyan — is attained(1).
HJP9: Evai = in this way (upon making this effort, and upon Akal Purakh's glance of grace falling). {Note: the word 'evai' makes plain that the last three lines are the answer to the question put in the third and fourth lines of this pauri: if in the amrit vela we reflect upon His glories, then by His mercy the robe of praise is obtained and that Lord comes into sight everywhere.} Janiai = is known, is experienced. Sabhu = in all places. Sachiaru = the abode of existence, the Master of being. ||4||
O Nanak! In this way the understanding comes that the Master of existence, Akal Purakh, is pervading in all places. ||4||
O Nanak, know this well: the True One Himself is All. ||4||
Know thus, O Nanak! that the True One is all by Himself.

Sri Guru Ji says: O Siddhas! (Evai) in this way let it be known that the (sachiaru) True Akal Purakh is Himself in every place. As in Sukhmani: 'ban trin parbat hai parbrahmu'. ||4|| Question: is He anyone's made thing — that is, is He nadi (born through the sound-lineage of a guru) or bindi (born of seed)? Answer:
34GD: Thapia na jai = cannot be established, cannot be conceived (in a womb). The Sanskrit root stha means 'to stand'. From it the causative root is sthapaya, meaning 'to make stand, to set up, to lay a foundation'. From this causative root comes the noun sthapan, whose meaning is the punsavan sanskar: when the first signs of a woman's being with child appear, this rite is performed in Hindu homes so that a son may be born. Prefixing ud to sthapaya gives utthapaya, whose meaning is the opposite — 'to uproot, to destroy' — as in: 'aape dekhi dikhavai aape; aape thapi uthape aape' (M:1). Kita na hoi = (our) making does not make Him. Na hoi = does not come into being.
Neither can He be brought forth, nor does our making make Him.
He cannot be established, He cannot be created.
He is neither established nor created by any one.
O Siddhas! That Akal Purakh is not anyone's established creation — that is, He is not nadi; nor is He anyone's bindi, procreated offspring.
8KH1: Aape aapi = purely His own self — that is, He has neither any begetter nor any maker. Soi niranjanu = that Hari, free of anjan. Niranjan = free of anjan, free of Maya, who is not made of Maya, in whom there is no part of Maya (nir-anjan: nir = without; anjan = collyrium, blackness, the taint of the vices, Maya's influence). He upon whom there is no influence of Maya.
He is purely His own self alone. That Akal Purakh is beyond Maya's influence.
He Himself is Immaculate and Pure.
That Pure One is all in all Himself.
That Niranjan, free of the filth of Maya, is His own self, self-established (sute-siddh) — that is, without beginning and without end.
TPDM: Jini = the man who. Tini = that man. Manu = respect, honour.
The man who has remembered that Akal Purakh — he alone has obtained honour.
Those who serve Him are honored.
They who serve Him, obtain honour.
Those Gurmukhs who have served Him — they have obtained honour.
3K42: Guni nidhanu = the treasury of virtues. Gaviai = let us do His praise.
O Nanak! (Come,) let us too sing the praise of that Hari, the treasury of virtues.
O Nanak, sing of the Lord, the Treasure of Excellence.
O Nanak! sing praises of the Lord who is the treasure of excellences.

Sri Guru Ji says: making such resolve, one ought to sing the (guni nidhanu) treasury of virtues — that is, the virtues of Akal Purakh. Question: singing happens only when there is some hearer? Answer:
H4D8: Mani = in the mind. Rakhiai = let us lodge. Bhau = God's love.
(Come, let us) sing and hear (the virtues of Akal Purakh), and lodge His love in our mind.
Sing, and listen, and let your mind be filled with love.
With the Lord's love reposed in your heart sing and hear His praises.

To one lesser than oneself, (gaviai) let one recount; and from one greater than oneself, let one hear. When the conjunction of the two is not to be had, then let one keep (bhau) love in the mind. Or: (gaviai) the singer-expounder is Sri Satiguru Ji — from him let one (suniai) hear; then (mani) let one do manan (reflection); then (rakhiai) let one do nididhyasan (sustained contemplation); then (bhau) direct gyan arises.
TE18: Dukhu parhari = having driven pain away. Ghari = in the heart. Lai jai = takes it home, earns it.
(The man who makes this effort) drives his pain away and lodges sukh in his heart.
Your pain shall be sent far away, and peace shall come to your home.
Thus shall you shed pain and shall take happiness to your home.

Its fruit: having (par) thoroughly (hari) destroyed the pains, he becomes (lai jai) undivided from the home of all comforts, atam-sukh — that is, the sukh by a mere trace of which the beings in the fourteen realms are living in bliss. Question: give an illustration of that undividedness? Answer:
3PHR: Gurmukhi = with the face turned toward the Guru; the man whose face is toward the Guru; through the Guru. Nadan = sound, the stir of life, the Shabad, the Nam. Vedan = gyan. Rahia samai = is pervading, is present in all places.
(But that God's) Nam and gyan (are obtained) through the Guru. Through the Guru alone (comes the conviction that) that Hari is pervading in all places.
The Guru's Word is the Sound-current of the Naad; the Guru's Word is the Wisdom of the Vedas; the Guru's Word is all-pervading.
Gurbani is the Divine Word, Gurbani the Lord's Knowledge and through Gurbani the Lord is realised to be all pervading.

The Gurus who are foremost (mukh) — theirs is the (nadan) Shabad; when the Guru-facing seeker, having heard it, came to know (vedan) its siddhant, then he abides (rahia samai) undivided in Parmatma — the Guru who is the venerable chief. Question: relate the greatness of such Gurus? Answer:
5YV5: Isaru = Shiv. Barma = Brahma. Parbati mai = Mother Parbati.
The Guru alone is (for us) Shiv; the Guru alone is (for us) Gorakh and Brahma; and the Guru alone is (for us) Mother Parbati.
The Guru is Shiva, the Guru is Vishnu and Brahma; the Guru is Paarvati and Lakhshmi.
The Guru is Shiva, the Guru Vishnu and Brahma, the Guru is Shiva's consort Parbati, Vishnu's consort Lakhshmi and Brahma's consort Saraswati.

It is by taking a Guru that (isaru) Shiv Ji became what he is; by taking a Guru that (gorakhu) Vishnu Ji became; by taking a Guru that (barma) Brahma Ji became; by taking a Guru that Parbati Ji, (ma) Lakshmi Ji and (i) Sarasvati Ji became what they are. Or: the Guru himself is the form of all the devas. Taking on Ishar's quality, he destroys the Sikhs' ignorance; taking on Vishnu's quality, he sustains the good virtues; taking on Brahma's quality, he brings forth love and the other virtues. In the same way, taking on Parbati's quality, he destroys the demerits; taking on Lakshmi's quality, he is the giver of the virtues of daivi sampada (divine endowment); taking on Sarasvati's quality, he gives light to bani. Question: tell yet more of such Gurus' greatness? Answer:
X1GF: Hau = I. Jana = were I to understand, to experience. Aakha nahi = I cannot describe it. Kahna... jai = it cannot be told, cannot be said.
Even so, if I were (even) to understand (this Akal Purakh's Hukam), I still could not describe it. (Akal Purakh's Hukam) cannot be told.
Even knowing God, I cannot describe Him; He cannot be described in words.
Even though I Know God, I cannot narrate Him, He cannot be described by words.

O Siddhas! If I could know the greatness of such Satigurus as a definite 'this' (idanta), what would I not say? — the sense is, it is limitless. Even if I wished to tell it, it cannot be told, since it is not within the range (avishay) of mind and speech. Question: say at least something? Answer:
5KPL: Gura = O Satiguru! Ik bujhai = one understanding.
(This is my prayer,) O Satiguru! Give me this one understanding,
The Guru has given me this one understanding:
The Guru has explained one thing to me.
The Gurus have given me one understanding.
DJAR: Iku data = the One Akal Purakh, the Giver of gifts. Visari na jai = may He not be forgotten. (The word 'ik' is feminine gender and is the adjective of 'bujhai'; the word 'iku' is masculine and is the adjective of 'data'. Keep in mind the difference between the spellings of the two words.) ||5||
that the One God who is the Giver of gifts to all beings — may I never forget Him. ||5||
there is only the One, the Giver of all souls. May I never forget Him! ||5||
There is but one Bestower for all the beings May, I never forget Him.

The Giver of all beings is the One Akal Purakh. O Siddhas! He does not slip from my remembrance. On this answer, perceiving Guru Ji's adroitness, greed arose in the Siddhas' minds: 'if Nanak the Nirankari should come into our order, our glory would become great'. Thinking this, they said: 'O young one! We shall take you on pilgrimage, and show you the mine of jewels, pearls and gemstones — come along with us'. Answer:
7NRN: Tirathi = at the tirath. Nava = I should bathe. Tisu = that God. Bhava = I should become pleasing. Vinu bhane = without being pleasing to God, if it is not accepted in God's sight. Ki nai kari = having bathed, what shall I do?
I should bathe at a tirath only if by so doing I could please that Parmatma; but if Parmatma is not pleased in this way, then what shall I gain by bathing (at the tirath)?
If I am pleasing to Him, then that is my pilgrimage and cleansing bath. Without pleasing Him, what good are ritual cleansings?
If I become pleasing to Him that is my pilgrimage bath. Without pleasing Him of what avail is the ablution?
O Siddhas! Only if we are pleasing to Parmeshvar should one go bathe at a tirath — then the tirath-bathing also bears fruit. If, without His being pleased, one did bathe, what would it accomplish?
8HGP: Jeti = as much. Sirathi = srishti, the world. Upai = created. Vekha = I look upon. Vinu karma = without the Lord's mercy; as in: 'vinu karma kichhu paiai nahi, je bahu tera dhavai' (Tilang M:1). Ki milai = what is obtained? Nothing is obtained. Ki lai = what can anyone take?
As much of the world created by Akal Purakh as I look upon — (in it,) without Parmatma's grace no one obtains anything; no one can take anything.
I gaze upon all the created beings: without the karma of good actions, what are they given to receive?
All the created beings, that I behold, without good acts what are they given and what do they obtain?

As much of the created creation as I look upon — without karma, what does anyone obtain, and what can this jiv take by his own strength? The sense: if it is in our karma and it pleases Ishvar, then we shall of ourselves do the pilgrimage; what need have we of you?
J6KZ: Mati vichi = within (a man's) intellect itself. Manik = pearls. Ik sikh = one teaching. Suni = be heard, if it be heard.
If one teaching of the Satiguru be heard, then within a man's intellect jewels, gems and pearls (spring up — that is, God's virtues arise).
Within the mind are gems, jewels and rubies, if you listen to the Guru's Teachings, even once.
In the mind are gems, jewels and rubies, provided you you act upon (hearken to) even one instruction of the Guru.

O Siddhas! (Je) when the Gurus' teaching of (ik) Oneness is heard — that is, when from the Gurus one hears the updesh of the One Parmatma — then within one's own (mati) intellect itself the jewels, gems and pearls are found(1).
NVVQ: (Therefore,) O Satiguru! (This is my prayer before you:) give me this one understanding,
The Guru has given me this one understanding:
The Guru has explained one thing to me.
The Gurus have given me one understanding.
AGUV: by which that Akal Purakh may never be forgotten by me, who is the Giver of gifts to all beings. ||6||
there is only the One, the Giver of all souls. May I never forget Him! ||6||
There is but one Bestower for all the beings. May, I never forget Him.

The Giver of all beings is the One Akal Purakh. O Siddhas! He does not slip from my remembrance. ||6|| Again the Siddhas spoke to Guru Ji: 'if you come into our order — that is, take up the garb of Yoga — then by the power of Yoga your state will become great'. Upon the Siddhas' urging, Sri Guru Ji spoke the answer:
MLKE: Jug chare = as long as the four ages. Aarja = life span. Dasuni = tenfold.
If a man's life were to become as long as the four ages, (nay, not merely this, but) even ten times more besides,
Even if you could live throughout the four ages, or even ten times more,
Though a man's age be equal to four ages and grow even ten times more,
O Siddhas! If the life span were of four ages, and were even ten times more besides,
C69U: Nava khanda vichi = that is, in the whole creation. Janiai = be known, become manifest. Sabhu koi = every man. Nali chalai = walks along with him, becomes a supporter, takes his side.
if he were to become known in the whole world, and every man were to walk behind him,
and even if you were known throughout the nine continents and followed by all,
Even though he be known in the nine continents and all were to walk with him (or follow in his train),
if the man were also known in the nine khands(1) — that is, become renowned — and everyone were to walk along with him, that is, the whole creation move at his command,
CZ4N: Changa... kai = having earned good repute, having become one of good name. Jasu = praise. Kirati = renown. Jagi = in the world. Lei = takes, earns.
if, earning a good name, he were to obtain praise and renown in the whole world,
with a good name and reputation, with praise and fame throughout the world-
and he were to assume good name and obtain praise and renown in the world.
if he were also to keep a good name in the world — (jasu) praise within the land and (kirati) renown in other lands; or, jasu to his face and kirati behind his back, with everyone giving both —
EPP1: Tisu = of Akal Purakh. Nadari = into the glance of grace. Na aavai = cannot come. Vat = news, notice. Na ke = no man.
(yet) if he cannot come into Akal Purakh's glance of mercy, then he is like the man of whom no one asks any news (that is, even holding so much honour and greatness, he is in truth without shelter).
still, if the Lord does not bless you with His Glance of Grace, then who cares? What is the use?
If God's gracious glance falls not one him, them, no one would care for him,

O Siddhas! If the man does not come into Hari's (nadari) glance of grace, then no one in the world asks after him. Or, (ke) those mahatma-jan who are the Beloved of Parmeshvar do not ask after him — that is, they account him paltry.
FTM0: Kitu = worm. Kari = making, deeming, setting down as. Dosu dhare = lays the charge. Kita andari kitu = a worm among worms, a paltry worm.
(Rather, such a man before Akal Purakh is) a mere worm ('khasmai nadri kirha aavai', Asa M:1). Akal Purakh, setting him down as an offender, lays upon him the charge (of forgetting the Nam).
Among worms, you would be considered a lowly worm, and even contemptible sinners would hold you in contempt.
he is accounted a vermin among worms and even the sinners impute accusations to him.
Among the worms he too becomes one worm, upon whom even the (dosi) leprous or the sinful lay blame; or, on his being an offender, charges are laid upon him in the next world.
Q2DD: Nirguni = in the virtueless man. Gunvantia = to the virtuous men. Kare = brings forth. De = gives.
O Nanak! That Akal Purakh brings forth virtue in the virtueless man, and it is He alone who bestows virtue upon the virtuous.
O Nanak, God blesses the unworthy with virtue, and bestows virtue on the virtuous.
O Nanak! God grants virtue to the non-virtuous and bestows piety on the pious.
Sri Guru Ji says: O Siddhas! Parmeshvar gives virtue even to the virtueless, and to the virtuous He grants the obtaining of yet more virtue.
SYSB: Teha = such. Na sujhai = is not to be found. Ji = who. Tisu = to that virtueless one. ||7||
No other such one is to be seen who could give any virtue to the virtueless being. (That is, only the Lord's glance of mercy can raise him; long life and the world's praise are of no help.) ||7||
No one can even imagine anyone who can bestow virtue upon Him. ||7||
I can think of no such one who can show any goodness to Him.
No such one is to be seen who could give virtue to that Parmeshvar — that is, render Him a return for His benefactions. ||7|| Now in four pauris Guru Ji tells the greatness of hearing the Nam.
ZYF3: Suniai = by hearing, upon hearing, if the surat be joined to the Nam. Sidh = those Yogis whose discipline and labour have borne fruit. Suri = devas.
This is the blessing of the Nam's lodging in the heart: that by hearing Vahiguru's praise, (ordinary men) attain the rank of the Siddhas, the Pirs, the devas and the Naths;
Listening-the Siddhas, the spiritual teachers, the heroic warriors, the yogic masters.
By hearing God's Name the mortal becomes a perfect person, religious guide, spiritual hero and a great yogi.

Gorakh and the other Siddhas, and the Pirs of the Muslim faith, and the devas, then the nine Naths — or, (surinath) Indra — all these obtained their rank through hearing the Guru's updesh alone. Further, rank is of two kinds: for those with desires (sakami), the rank of the siddhis, of svarg and the rest; for the desireless (nishkami), the attainment of one's own true form.
A7FY: Dhaval = the bull, the support of the earth.
And by hearing Vahiguru's praise, the understanding comes to them that the support of earth and sky is that Lord;
Listening-the earth, its support and the Akaashic ethers.
By hearing God's Name the reality of the earth, it's supposed supporting bull and the heaven is revealed to the mortal.

(Dharti) the earth, and (dhaval) the dharma-form (the bull of dharma), and the sky — all these came to be through hearing the Nam. The sense: their presiding (abhimani) devas, by hearing the Nam, attained greater eminence.
QYGU: Dip = the seven dips of the earth's division. Loa = the loks, the realms.
By hearing Vahiguru's praise the understanding comes that Vahiguru is pervading in all the dips, the loks and the patals,
Listening-the oceans, the lands of the world and the nether regions of the underworld.
By hearkening to the Lord's Name man comes to have the knowledge of the continents, the worlds and the nether regions.
The presiding devas of the seven dips, and of the seven (loa) loks, and of the seven patals — by hearing the Nam they attained eminence.
F28C: Pohi na sakai = cannot touch, cannot frighten, cannot exert its influence.
(Death too cannot touch the men who hear Vahiguru's praise — that is, death cannot frighten them.)
By hearing the Lord's Name death cannot torment (touch) the mortal.
Through hearing, Kal (death) cannot (pohi) touch them — the sense: Markandeya and the other long-lived ones attained the rank of chiranjivi (the deathless) through hearing the Nam alone.(1)
3477: O Nanak! In the hearts of the bhagats (who join their surat to Akal Purakh's Nam) bloom abides forever,
O Nanak, the devotees are forever in bliss.
O Nanak! the devotees ever enjoy happiness.
Sri Guru Ji says: O Siddhas! Such is the greatness of hearing the Nam, by which everlasting (vigasu) anand — that is, nityanand — has been attained.
FVWP: (For) by hearing His praise, (a man's) pains and sins are destroyed. ||8||
By hearing to the Master's Name sorrow and sin meet with destruction.

Such is the greatness of hearing that Nam: the bhagats who have heard it with love — all their kinds of pains and sins are destroyed, and everlasting (vigasu) anand, that is, nityanand, has been attained(1). ||8||
TENR: Isaru = Shiv. Indu = the deva Indra.
Through joining the surat to Akal Purakh's Nam, an ordinary man rises to the rank of Shiv, Brahma and Indra;
By hearing the Lord's Name the status of god of death, god of creation and god of rain is obtained.
(Isaru) Shiv, (barma) Brahma, (indu) Indra — or Chandra — and the rest: their rank was obtained through the hearing of the Nam alone.
7M4S: Mukhi = with the mouth, from the mouth. Salahan = the praises, God's glories. Mandu = the bad man.
Even the bad man begins to utter God's praises with his mouth;
By hearing God's Name even the evil come to sing Lord's praises with their mouth.

Those who were of low caste and low deeds, highway robbers such as Valmiki — they, through hearing alone, attained such a rank as Adi-kavi (the first poet), worthy of (salahan) praise from every mouth.
UCWQ: Jog jugati = the method of Yoga, the means of Yoga. Tani = of what is within the body. Bhed = the matters.
(Even to one of ordinary understanding) the secret of the hidden things within the body becomes known (that is, of the runnings of the senses — eyes, ears, tongue and the rest — toward the vices);
Listening-the technology of Yoga and the secrets of the body.
By hearing God's Name the mortal understands the ways of uniting with the Lord and the body's secrets.
By the method of ashtang (eight-limbed) Yoga, the knowing of the six chakras within the body — this secret of the body, all of it, has come through hearing alone.
BXPY: The understanding of the method of union with the Lord comes; the understanding of the Shastras, the Smritis and the Vedas comes (that is, the real high aim of the religious books is grasped only when we join the surat to the Nam; otherwise we merely read off the bare words and do not reach that true fervour in which those religious books were uttered).
Listening-the Shaastras, the Simritees and the Vedas.
By hearing the Lord's Name the Knowledge of the four religious books, six school of philosophy and twenty seven ceremonial treatise is acquired.
The 6 Shastras, the 27 Smritis, the 4 Vedas — the siddhant of all these has been obtained through hearing alone.

Countless devotees contemplate the Wisdom and Virtues of the Lord.
Countless are the votaries who reflect over the Lord's excellences and theology.
Countless bhagats reflect upon the gyan of the Lord's virtues.

Countless the holy, countless the givers.

O Nirankar! You are forever of established form. ||18|| Now they say this: that Parmatma's names and dwellings are endless:

Countless are Akal Purakh's Nams; countless are the dwellings — Kanshi, Kanchi, Baikunth and the rest.

He is beyond the reach of such as ourselves; beyond Brahma and the rest He is unreachable, farther still; and Parmatma, giving sustaining power to countless beings, is (loa) giving light.

(Akhri) it is according to the writ inscribed that the Nam is japped, and according to the writ inscribed that praise and the kirtan of the virtues is done.

From the Word, come the written and spoken words and hymns.
In letters the uttered hymns are recorded.
Again, it is according to the writ inscribed that the writing and the speaking of bani comes about. Question: what are those letters? Answer:
7C0T: Akhra siri = by means of letters alone. Sanjogu = the writ of destiny. Vakhani = can be expounded, can be told.
(By means of letters alone can the conjunction of destiny be expounded.)

So in whatever way He commands, in that same way he writes. The sense is this: that Brahma too is not independent.

Without Your Name, there is no place at all.
Without Your Name, there is no place.

Without nam and rup there is no place; or, (jeta) as much as anyone has attained of an excellent state, that much the Nam alone has done. is washed clean by applying soap.

actions repeated, over and over again, are engraved on the soul.

these, by themselves, bring only an iota of merit.
bring only a sesame (tiny amount) of honour (merit), if any.

Whoever does all these deeds with desire and full of pride obtains (til ka manu) an honour that slips away. The sense is this: the fruit of these deeds is svarg; and so, when the merits are exhausted, he is cast down again into the world of death. Forgetting the former comfort, he then experiences nothing but pain(1).
ND4F: Sunia = (the man who) has heard Akal Purakh's Nam. Mannia = (whose mind, hearing that Nam,) has accepted it, has become convinced. Mani = in the mind. Bhau kita = (who) has done love.
(But the man who) has joined his surat (to Akal Purakh's Nam), whose mind has become convinced (in the Nam), and who has set (Akal Purakh's) love within his mind,
Listening and believing with love and humility in your mind,
Whoever heartily hears, believes and loves God's Name,
Whoever does the (sunia) hearing, the (mannia) manan, and the (mani kita) nididhyasan of the Nam, to him comes (bhau) the gyan of the tattva.

By listening and believing, and deeply loving in your mind (this itself is worship). That person has cleansed their inner shrine. All virtues are Yours — none belong to me. Without cultivating virtue, there can be no true devotion/worship. I take refuge in You, the Word, the Creator. You are true, beautiful, and always happy.
W7L9: Antargati = the inner. Tirathi = at the tirath. Antargati tirathi = at the inner tirath. Mali = having scrubbed and scrubbed, thoroughly. Nau = he has bathed.
That man has (as it were) bathed with full scrubbing in his own inner tirath (that is, joining himself to the Akal Purakh dwelling within, he has thoroughly washed off the filth of his mind).
cleanse yourself with the Name, at the sacred shrine deep within.
obtains salvation by thoroughly bathing in the shrine within himself.

Its fruit: he then, within himself — that is, in the heart — in the tirath which is (gati) the attained bliss of the atma, (malu) scrubs and (nau) bathes; the sense: he stays absorbed in the bliss of the atma. Or: (antargati) the distinction between jiv and Ish is destroyed; and for the world-river that is the filth, he becomes the (nau) boat, for carrying across those who have come to his refuge(1).
6MYT: Sabhi = all. Mai nahi koi = I am nothing, I have no standing at all.
I have no standing at all (that I might sing Your virtues); these are all Your own greatnesses.
All virtues are Yours, Lord, I have none at all.
All virtues are Yours, O Lord! I have none.
O Akal Purakh! All virtues are Yours; in me there is not one virtue at all.
BCM6: Vinu gunu kite = without bringing forth virtue, if You do not bring forth virtue, if You do not bring forth Your virtues within me. Na hoi = cannot be done.
(O Akal Purakh!) if You do not bring forth (Your own) virtues (within me), then Your bhagti cannot be done by me.
Without virtue, there is no devotional worship.
Without acquiring the virtues, Lord's devotional service can not be performed.
O Siddhas! Without taking on this virtue which is humility, bhagti does not come about. Question: did the world's creation come about from the sargun or from the nirgun? Answer:
E30D: Suasati = victory be Yours, may You abide forever (that is, I take Your support alone). Barmau = Brahma.

(O Nirankar!) may You ever be victorious! You Yourself are Maya, You Yourself are Bani, You Yourself are Brahma (that is, the Maya, Bani or Brahma who make this creation are not of a separate existence from You, as people have supposed).
I bow to the Lord of the World, to His Word, to Brahma the Creator.
My obeisance is to God, who Himself is the creator of world and Brahma etc.

(Suasati) the Ishvar of auspicious form, strengthened by Maya, (aathi) is; from Him arose Bani in the form of the resolve — 'from One let Me become many' — and from that came (barmau) Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesh, and the whole expanse.
4SDK: Sati = ever-abiding. Suhanu = subhan, beautiful. Mani chau = bloom in the mind.
You are ever-abiding, You are beautiful, and in Your mind there is ever bloom (You alone are the maker of the world; You alone know when You made it).
He is Beautiful, True and Eternally Joyful.
He is true and beautiful and rapture ever abides within His mind.
So Parmatma is in truth sat (existent), and is (suhanu) of the form of consciousness; 'sada mani chau' — He is forever (mani) the supreme (chau) bliss itself.
V7HC: Vela = time. Vakhatu = time, hour. Thiti varu = the lunar dates are counted from the moon's course, as ekam, dooj, teej and so on; and from the sun come day and night and the weekdays, som, mangal and so on.
What was that time and that hour, what was the lunar date, what was the day,
What was that time, and what was that moment? What was that day, and what was that date?
What the time, what movement, what lunar day, what week day,
Then what (vela) time was it, and what hour was it? 'Vela' the Hindus say; 'vakhat' the Muslims say. Then what tithi was it, what day was it?

What was the time, the moment, what day, what date, when the world was created? The Yogis don't know, nor do the Semitic scriptures (Quran, etc.) — the Pandits couldn't find the time either, even if it was written in the Puranas. That time is not known to the Qazis. Only the Creator who made the world knows Himself. How do I speak of Him? How do I praise Him? How do I describe Him, how do I come to know Him? O Nanak, everyone tries to speak of Him, each thinking they are smarter than the other. Great is the Master, great is His Name/Glory — whatever happens in the world is His doing. O Nanak, if one thinks that by their own intellect they can know it all, they will not be received well (honourably) in God's court. ||21||
G0TE: Kavani si ruti = which were those seasons. Mahu = month. Kavanu = which. Jitu = in which, at which time. Hoa = came into being, was brought forth, was made. Aakaru = this visible world. {Note: the word 'var' is used in two forms, 'var' and 'varu'. 'Var' is feminine, whose meaning is 'a turn'. 'Varu' is masculine, and its meaning is 'day'. In Japji Sahib this word has come in the following lines: (1) 'sochai sochi na hovai, je sochi lakh var' (1); (2) 'varia na java ek var' (16); (3) 'jo kichhu paia su eka var' (31); (4) 'kavanu su vela, vakhatu kavanu thiti, kavanu varu' (21); (5) 'rati ruti thiti var' (34). In citations 1, 2 and 3 'var' is feminine. In no. 4 'varu' is masculine singular, and in no. 5 'var' is masculine plural. When this word comes with an (i), then it is a verb, as in: 'vari varau anik dariu, sukh pria suhag palak rati' (1, Rahau, 3.42, Kanra M:5). Here 'vari' means 'to be a sacrifice'.}
Which were those seasons and which was that month, when this world came into being?
What was that season, and what was that month, when the Universe was created?
and what the season and what month, when the creation came into being?
At the time when this (aakaru) expanse came about, what season was it, what month was it? Answer:
WN0J: Vel = time, hour. Paia = found, discovered. Vel na paia = the time was not found. (Note: 'vela' is masculine and 'vel' is feminine.) Pandti = by the Pandits. Ji = otherwise. Hovai = there would have been, would have been made. Lekhu = subject, composition. Lekhu puranu = a Puran in the form of this composition, a Puran on this subject (that is, as several other Purans have been made, a Puran on this subject too would have been made).
(When did this world come into being?) The Pandits too did not come to know that time. Had they known, then a Puran would have been written (upon this subject too).
The Pandits, the religious scholars, cannot find that time, even if it is written in the Puraanas.
The Pundits find not the time, even though it be mentioned in the Puran's texts.
O Siddhas! That time neither Vyas nor the other Pandits have found. Had they found it, it would have been written in a Puran.
MP96: Vakhatu = the time when the world was made. Na paio = was not found. Kadia = by the Qazis. The Arabic letters zuad, zoe and ze are pronounced with the letter 'd'. The word 'kagaz' is pronounced 'kagad', 'nazar' as 'nadari', 'hazur' as 'haduri'. In this same way 'Qazi' is pronounced 'Kadi'. Ji = otherwise. Likhani = (the Qazis) would have written. Lekhu quranu = a composition like the Quran (that is, as the Qazis, gathering together the verses uttered by Muhammad Sahib, wrote the Quran, so they would also have written the subject of the time of the world's making). {Note: by twisting the meanings of the words 'vakhatu', 'paio' and 'kadia' used in this pauri, Qadiani Muslims are misleading unlearned Sikhs, saying that here Guru Nanak Dev Ji, by way of prophecy, has instructed the Sikhs that they should not give vakhat (trouble) to the prophet who is to appear in the town of Qadian. We are not going to enter into any debate here, nor to mislead anyone. We only wish to draw attention to the construction of the words and to their meanings. The word 'kadia' has already been explained in the word-meanings. The word 'vakhatu' is the Arabic word 'vaqt'. In speaking of the Hindus, the Indic word 'vela' has been used. In speaking of the Muslims, the Muslim word (source breaks off here)}
The Qazis could get no news of that time; otherwise they would have written the composition, just as they (gathering the verses together) wrote the Quran.
That time is not known to the Qazis, who study the Koran.
Nor do the Qazis, who scribe the writing of Quran, Know the time.
(Kadia) Muhammad and the other prophets too did not find (vakhatu) the time; had they found it, it would have been written down in the Quran.
S0KM: (When the world was made,) which lunar date it was and which weekday, no Yogi knows this either. There is no man (who can tell) which season it was then and which month.
The day and the date are not known to the Yogis, nor is the month or the season.
Neither the yogi nor any one else knows the lunar day, week day season and the month.
(Jogi) the practisers of pranayam too cannot know the tithi, the day, the season or the month; nor can anyone else know.
YXDC: Ja karta = which Creator. Sirathi kau = the world. Saje = brings forth, makes. Aape soi = He Himself alone.
The Creator who brings this world into being — He Himself alone knows (when He fashioned the world).
The Creator who created this creation-only He Himself knows.
The Creator who creates the world, He Himself Knows (the time).
O Siddhas! (Ja) the Creator who — or, when the Creator — fashions the making of the creation, then that Creator Himself alone knows that time.
XEQL: Kiv kari = in what manner, in what way. Aakha = I should say, I should describe, I might tell. Salahi = I should praise, I should do Akal Purakh's greatness. Kiu = in what manner, in what way. Varni = I should describe,
In what way should I tell (Akal Purakh's greatness), in what way should I do Akal Purakh's praise, in what way should I describe (Akal Purakh's greatness), and in what way could I understand it?
How can we speak of Him? How can we praise Him? How can we describe Him? How can we know Him?
How to express, how to praise, how to describe and how to know You, O Lord?

In what way shall I tell of that Lord's manner of creating? Then in what way shall I describe His manner of sustaining? And in what way am I to know how He does the destroying in such a way? Therefore how shall I make (salahi) His praise?

RW45: Sabhu ko = every being. Aakhani aakhai = as for the saying, he says it; he makes the attempt to say. Ik du iku siana = each becoming wiser than the next, one man reckoning himself wiser than another. Du = than.
O Nanak! Every being, thinking itself wiser than the next, makes the attempt to tell (Akal Purakh's greatness) — but it cannot be told.
O Nanak, everyone speaks of Him, each one wiser than the rest.
Nanak! All describe Your discourse and each is wiser then the other.
Sri Guru Ji says: O Siddhas! As for the (aakhani) akhyan — that is, the telling of the katha and its episodes — everyone speaks, each making himself greater than the next; but no one finds the end.
FN4U: Sahibu = Master, Akal Purakh. Nai = greatness. Ja ka = of which (Akal Purakh). Kita ja ka hovai = the Hari of whose doing everything is.
Akal Purakh is the greatest of all; His greatness is exalted. Whatever is happening in the world is of His doing.
Great is the Master, Great is His Name. Whatever happens is according to His Will.
Great is the Master and great His Name and what he does, comes to pass.
Therefore know just this: as the Master is great, so great is His (nai) greatness — because whatever He does can come to be; the sense: His resolve is true (sat-sankalp).
SM79: Je ko = if some man. Aapau = of himself, from his own self, on the strength of his own intellect. Na sohai = does not look beautiful, does not obtain honour. Agai gaia = having gone to Akal Purakh's door. ||21||
O Nanak! If some man attempts (to find the end of the Lord's greatness) on the strength of his own intellect, he goes to Akal Purakh's door and obtains no honour there. ||21||
O Nanak, one who claims to know everything shall not be decorated in the world hereafter. ||21||
Nanak! if someone deems himself potent to do, He shall not look adorned on his arrival in the world hereafter.

Sri Guru Ji says: whoever (aapau janai) knows his own self — that is, thinks 'I can tell it' or 'I can do every work' — such a proud man, going on into the next world, obtains no glory. The sense is that he obtains a base condition. ||21|| Question: but in this creation a fixed rule has been laid down of 7 patals and 7 skies. Further, a measure has been given for the earth of forty-nine crore yojans, and for the mountains and the rest as well. You say that no one at all can tell it — how is this to be understood? Answer:
YB5R: Patala patal = beneath the patals there are further patals. Aagasa aagas = above the skies there are further skies.
(All the Vedas with one voice say:) 'Beneath the patals there are lakhs more patals, and above the skies there are lakhs more skies;
There are nether worlds beneath nether worlds, and hundreds of thousands of heavenly worlds above.
There are nether worlds beyond the nether worlds and lacs of skies over skies.

O Siddhas! Beneath lakhs of patals there are patals. Above lakhs of skies there are skies. The word 'lakh' works by the dehli-dipak nyaya (the lamp on the threshold, lighting both rooms), so it joins with both together. 'Sky' by implication is to be understood as the sky-dwelling realms, Maharlok and the rest; further void upon void cannot be, since 'sky' is only the name of emptiness. The second manner is this: within each single hair of Parmeshvar there are crores upon crores of universes. By this manner no doubt at all can arise.

There are nether-worlds beyond nether-worlds, and skies/heavenly realms beyond realms. People have grown weary of searching for God's limit — the Vedas have said this. The Semitic scriptures (Quran, Gospel, Torah, Psalms) say there are 18,000 worlds, of which the origin is the One. Even if an account could be written, the very means of counting would be exhausted (limitless). O Nanak, God is called great, but only He Himself knows how great. ||22||
CWGK: Orhak = the end, the limit, the farthest bounds. Bhali thake = they have grown weary searching and searching. Kahani = they say. Ik vat = one thing, with one voice.
(Countless rishis and munis) have grown weary searching for their farthest bounds (but could not find them).'
The Vedas say that you can search and search for them all, until you grow weary.
The scriptures say one thing: searching for God's limits and bounds, (without success) people have grown weary.

(Orhak) the word orhak means 'end': there is no (orhak) end of the creation, nor is there any (orhak) end of the Creator; or, (orhak) putting forth their strength they have grown weary of searching, yet even so Hari's end was not found. The 4 Vedas say one thing:
2B00: Sahas atharah = eighteen thousand (worlds). Kahani kateba = the katebas say. Kateba = the four books of the Christian faith, Islam and so on: the Quran, the Injil (Gospel), the Taurat and the Zabur (Psalms). Asulu = origin. (Note: this is an Arabic word. The (u) beneath the letter 's' is to indicate the Arabic letter 'suad'.) Ik dhatu = the one Akal Purakh, the one Creator.

(All four) katebas (of the Muslims, Christians and the rest) say: 'There are eighteen thousand worlds in all, whose origin is the one Akal Purakh.' (But the true thing is that the words) 'thousands' and 'lakhs' too cannot be used in the reckoning of the creation.
The scriptures say that there are 18,000 worlds, but in reality, there is only One Universe.
The Semitic scriptures say that there are eighteen thousand worlds, but in reality there is only one essence; that the Lord is limitless.

The 4 Vedas, and the thousand rishis and munis, and the 18 Purans, and the katebas — 1 Taurat, 2 Injil, 3 Quran, 4 Zabur — all these together say one thing: 'asulu', that is to say, in truth the one Parmatma is sat (real). All other name and form is (dhatu) that which will run away, of the form of Maya — the sense: it is mithya (unreal).
1H1W: Lekha hoi = if a reckoning could be made. Likhiai = it could be written. Lekhai vinasu = the ending of the reckoning, the end of the reckoning.

(Akal Purakh's creation's) reckoning could be written only if a reckoning could be made at all. (This reckoning cannot be made; while making the reckoning,) the reckoning itself comes to an end (the very figures of counting run out).
If you try to write an account of this, you will surely finish yourself before you finish writing it.
If there be any account of His creation, then man would finish while writing.

O Siddhas! If (lekha) a counting could be made, then (likhiai) it could be written — the sense: the counting cannot be made. Akal Purakh is beyond reckoning (alekh); and whatever thing comes within reckoning, that thing has a destruction.
WR3V: Aakhiai = is called (the Akal Purakh whom). Aape = that Akal Purakh Himself alone. Janai = knows. Aapu = His own self. ||22||
O Nanak! The Akal Purakh who is being called great (throughout the world) — He Himself alone knows His own self. (He alone knows His own greatness.) ||22||
O Nanak, call Him Great! He Himself knows Himself. ||22||
O Nanak! Call Him great. He Himself knows His Own-self.
Sri Guru Ji says: that Parmatma is called great; He Himself alone knows His own self. ||22||
YTFR: Salahi = the praiseworthy Parmatma. Salahi = having done praise. Eti surat = this much understanding (of how great Akal Purakh is). Na paia = no one has gained it.

By uttering and uttering the greatnesses of the praiseworthy Akal Purakh, no man has gained this much understanding — of how great Akal Purakh is. (The men who do His praise merge into that very Akal Purakh.)
The praisers praise the Lord, but they do not obtain intuitive understanding
The praisers praise the Lord, but they obtain not this understanding

O Siddhas! The praise of Akal Purakh, who is (salahi) worthy of praise, all have indeed done. Or: the sants who are the praisers have indeed done His praise; but as to how much (eti) His greatness is, that (surati) knowledge was not attained even by them — that is, it did not become an object of definite apprehension (idanta).

The praisers praise God, but still nobody has been able to fully understand Him. Rivers and streams flow into the ocean, but don't know its vastness. The emperors and sultans of the oceans, with mountains of wealth and property — they are not even equal to an ant, if God is forgotten in that ant's mind. ||23||
5WQP: Atai = and. Vah = streams, channels. Pavahi = they fall. Samundi = into the ocean. Na janiahi = they are not known, those rivers and streams cannot be recognised (separately thereafter), (they merge within it, and cannot fathom the ocean's depth).
Rivers and streams fall into the ocean, but (thereafter) they cannot be recognised (separately) (they merge within it, and cannot fathom the ocean's depth).
the streams and rivers flowing into the ocean do not know its vastness.
that they may know His greatness; as the steams and the rivers falling into the ocean understand not its extent.

As rivers and (vah) streams all fall into the ocean, but do not (na janiahi) know the ocean's end — nor which is the water of the rivers and which the water of the streams; it is all ocean alone. As in Sukhmani: 'jiu jal mahi jalu aai khatana; tiu joti sang joti samana'. In this same way the sants become of the form of Brahm.
X2T8: Samund sah sultan = the emperors and sultans of the oceans. Girha seti = as great as mountains.
The emperors and sultans of the oceans (in whose treasuries there may be heaps of) wealth and goods as great as mountains —
Even kings and emperors, with mountains of property and oceans of wealth
Wealthy Kings and emperors with oceans and mountains of property and wealth

O Siddhas! That Akal Purakh, ocean-like, is the (sah sultanu) emperor of emperors; those who do not forget Him from the mind become (samundr) of the form of Brahm itself. And though there be (girha)(1) wealth and goods (seti) equal to Indra's, or (girha) like the mountains —
5K0J: Tuli = equal. Na hovni = they are not. Tisu manahu = from that ant's mind. Je na visarahi = if You are not forgotten, (O Hari!) ||23||
— they are not equal even to a single ant (in the eyes of the one who does the Lord's praise), if (O Akal Purakh!) You are not forgotten from that ant's mind. ||23||
-these are not even equal to an ant, who does not forget God. ||23||
equal not this ant who forgets not the true Lord.

So they are not equal to an ant, not equal to those possessionless sants — the sants who do not forget that Vahiguru from their minds, or who are not forgotten from that Vahiguru's mind. ||23|| Again — by the nyaya of digging for the post, they tell of His limitlessness.
40DA: Siphati = of the praises. Kahani = by telling, by declaring.
There is no bound at all to (Akal Purakh's) virtues; even by counting, no end of (the virtues) can be reached (they cannot be counted).
Endless are His Praises, endless are those who speak them.
There is no limit to the Lord's praises and to those who describe.
O Siddhas! Neither is there any end of that (siphati) Akal Purakh, nor is there any end of His (kahani) praise, or of those who do His praise.

There is no limit to His praises, no limit to those who speak them. Endless is His creation, as are His gifts. By seeing or hearing His virtues, we will never reach the end. What is in God's mind — we cannot know its limit. The limit of His creation cannot be perceived. Its limits here and beyond cannot be perceived. Many cry out, trying to find His limit. But His limits cannot be seen/found.
VKD8: Karnai = of the creation He has made. Deni = in the giving, by the giving of gifts.
No end can be reached of Akal Purakh's creation and of His gifts.
