Endless are His Actions, endless are His Gifts.
Limitless are His workings and limitless His givings.

(Karnai) of the doings of the doers — the sense: of the fashioning of the expanse and the rest — there is no end either. Or: of the jap and tap and the rest that come to be done, of these too there is no end. And of what He gives in dan to the beings there is no end either; or, of the gifts themselves there is no end.
X8NU: Vekhani sunani = by seeing and by hearing.
By seeing and by hearing too, the far shore of His virtues cannot be reached.
Endless is His Vision, endless is His Hearing.
There is no limit to watching and hearing His virtues.
Of the gyanis who see Him there is no end either. Of the seekers who do the hearing, no end is known either.
N8DF: Na japai = is not perceived, is not seen. Mani = in (Akal Purakh's) mind. Mantu = counsel.
What counsel there is in that Akal Purakh's mind — of this too no end can be found.
His limits cannot be perceived. What is the Mystery of His Mind?
What is Lord's motive? It's limit is not known.
What (mantu) mantra — that is, counsel — is in Akal Purakh's mind, of that too no end is known.
WHBU: Kita = made. Aakaru = this world which is seen.
Akal Purakh has made this world (which is seen), but even of this no end can be found.
The limits of the created universe cannot be perceived.
The limit of His created creation is not discerned.
Of the expanse of the creation which He has made, in the form of the inert and the moving, of this too no end is known.
5T92: Paravaru = the far bank and the near bank.
No near shore or far shore of it can be seen.
Its limits here and beyond cannot be perceived.
The bound of His this and yonder end is not known.
Of the near side and the far side too no end is known.
LDZY: Ant karani = to find the bound. Kete = many men. Bilalahi = they wail, they cry out.
Many men have been crying out to find Akal Purakh's bound,
Many struggle to know His limits,
Good many bewail for knowing His bounds
O Siddhas! To take His end, how many beings (bilalahi) weep.
J73M: Ta ke ant = that Akal Purakh's bounds. Na pae jahi = cannot be found.
But His bounds cannot be found.
but His limits cannot be found.
but His limits are not found.
The ends of that Akal Purakh's virtues are not found by them.
CXK7: Ehu ant = this bound (which limitless beings search for).
This bound (of Akal Purakh's virtues, which limitless beings are searching for) no man can find.
No one can know these limits.
That this alone is the end — no one knows it so.

This limit, nobody knows. The more He is called great, the greater He appears (leaving more unsaid). Great is the Lord, high is His heavenly home. His reputation is the highest of the high. If anyone could be as great/high as God, only they would know how great God is. How great God is, only He Himself knows. O Nanak, by His glance of grace, He blesses us with gifts. ||24||
WRQ5: Bahuta kahiai = the more Akal Purakh is called great, the more His virtues are told. Bahut hoi = the more He begins to appear greater and greater.
The more this is said, that He is great, the greater and greater He begins to appear.
The more you say about them, the more there still remains to be said.
The more we describe, the more obscure He becomes.
However much they tell, so much the more is there left to tell — the sense: the whole does not come within the telling.
0W15: Thau = the station of Akal Purakh's dwelling.
Akal Purakh is great; His station is exalted.
Great is the Master, High is His Heavenly Home.
Great is the Lord and high his seat.

For this reason that Master too is great and exalted, and His (thau) Sach Khand, the abode of Baikunth, is also great and exalted — that is, it is beyond all. In the Gita too it is written: 'that, having reached which, one does not fall again — that is My supreme abode'.
E6WZ: Uche upari ucha = higher than the high, very exalted. Nau = renown, greatness.
Highest of the High, above all is His Name.
His Name is the higher than the high.
Of all the exalted ones told of above, the Lord's Nam is the most exalted.
BLFR: Evadu = so great. Hovai koi = if some man were.
If some other were as great as He,
Only one as Great and as High as God
If any one be as great and high as He is
Of the greatness told of above — when (evadu) someone becomes so great and exalted,
J79G: Tisu uche kau = that exalted Akal Purakh. Soi = that man alone.
he alone could understand that exalted Akal Purakh (of how great He is).
can know His Lofty and Exalted State.
then alone he would know that Lofty Being.
then he would know the secret of that exalted Akal Purakh. The sense is this: neither is anyone equal to Him, nor can anyone know His secret as a definite apprehension (idanta).
RMD4: Jevadu = how great. Janai = knows. Aapi aapi = He alone Himself (besides Him no other knows).
Akal Purakh Himself alone knows how great He Himself is.
Only He Himself is that Great. He Himself knows Himself.
How great He is, only He Himself knows.
O Siddhas! As great as He Himself is, He Himself alone knows His own self.
W145: Nadri = the Hari who casts the glance of mercy. Karmi = by the deed, by the bestowal. Dati = bestowal. ||24||
O Nanak! (Every) gift is obtained through the bestowal of the Akal Purakh who casts the glance of mercy. ||24||
O Nanak, by His Glance of Grace, He bestows His Blessings. ||24||
O Nanak! the compassionate Lord by His grace bestows gifts.
Sri Guru Ji says: O Siddhas! (Nadri) Vahiguru gives gifts according to the beings' (karmi) deeds. ||24||
YXH5: Akal Purakh's bestowal is so great that it cannot be brought into writing.
His Blessings are so abundant that there can be no written account of them.
Good many are His bounties, these cannot be recorded.
Hari's (karamu) doing is very great; for this reason it cannot be written.

So great are His blessings, they cannot be written about. The Great Giver has not even a sesame-seed's worth of greed. Countless warriors beg at God's door. Countless are contemplated on Him beyond counting. Many are consumed and destroyed in vice and corruption. So many take and take, then deny receiving (don't believe it was from God). Many fools just keep consuming and consuming. So many endure sorrow, hunger, and constant abuse — but even these are Your gifts, Great Giver. Liberation from bondage comes only by God's will; nobody can suggest another path. If some fool suggests another way, he alone knows how many blows he receives on his face (for it). He Himself knows our needs, He Himself gives. So many people say this. Whoever is blessed with the gift of singing His praises — O Nanak, he becomes the king of kings. ||25||
QRM0: Tilu = even a sesame seed's worth. Tamai = greed, craving. Data = the giver of gifts.
He is the giver of great gifts; He has not the least greed.
The Great Giver does not hold back anything.
He is the great Giver and has not even an iota of avarice.
That Akal Purakh is (vada) the Giver, and does not hold even a sesame seed's worth of (tamai) desire.
8F5K: Kete = many. Jodh apar = limitless warriors, countless heroes. Mangahi = they beg.
Limitless warriors are begging (at Akal Purakh's door),
There are so many great, heroic warriors begging at the Door of the Infinite Lord.
The multitudes of warriors beg from the Infinite Lord.
How many men of desire beg limitless (jodh) valour of the Lord — that there may never be a defeat for me in battle.
WATD: Ganat = counting. Ketia = of many. Vekar = in the vices.
And there are many other such (beggars) whose number cannot be reckoned.
So many contemplate and dwell upon Him, that they cannot be counted.
Good many beyond reckoning, ponder over Him.
And how many desireless ones beg for that Brahm-vichar whose counting there is not.
E536: Khapi tutahi = they are consumed and destroyed.
Many beings (using His gifts) are consumed and destroyed in the vices alone.
So many waste away to death engaged in corruption.
Many pine away to extinction in wickedness.
How many, consuming themselves in the vices, are broken off from Parmeshvar — the sense: they remain turned away from Him.
MZZ6: Kete = limitless beings. Mukaru pahi = they deny it.
Limitless beings, having received (things at Akal Purakh's door), then deny it (that is, they never come to gratitude and say that the Lord Himself is giving all things).
So many take and take again, and then deny receiving.
Some continually take gifts and yet deny them.
How many fools, taking and taking the Lord's gifts, fall into denial — the sense: they forget that Giver.
3N29: Khahi khahi = they eat, they keep on eating. {Note: 'tun dekhahi hau mukari paau'; 'sabhu kichhu sunda vekhda, kiu mukari paia jai'. In both these lines the word is 'mukari', but in the line above it is 'mukaru'. The meaning of both is one and the same. 'Mukari' fits correctly according to grammar. Regarding this word, still further research is needed.}
Countless fools (taking the things) keep on eating (but do not hold the Giver in remembrance).
So many foolish consumers keep on consuming.
How many fools do nothing but the (khahi) eating and eating of things — the sense: they are never satisfied.
TRBN: Ketia = to many beings. Dukh = many pains and afflictions. Bhukh = hunger (that is, they do not even get food to eat). Sad = ever.
For countless beings, blows, afflictions and hunger alone (are written in their lot).
So many endure distress, deprivation and constant abuse.
Good many endure distress hunger and perpetual chastisement.
How many have the constant blow of the pain of hunger — that is, they remain in pain at all times.
5AFL: Dati = bestowal. Datar = O bestowing Akal Purakh!
(But) O Bestowing Akal Purakh! This too is only Your bestowal (because it is through these pains and afflictions that a man comes to understand how to walk in Your will).
Even these are Your Gifts, O Great Giver!
Even these are Yours gifts, O Bestower!
Therefore, for the removal of such affliction, let us make this prayer: O (datar) Giver! This too is Your gift — the sense: even in pain let us accept the Hukam alone.
W1JH: Bandi = from the bondage, from the love of Maya. Khalasi = mukti, release. Bhanai = by walking in Akal Purakh's will. Hoi = comes about.
And release from the bondage (which is the love of Maya) comes only by walking in Akal Purakh's will.
Liberation from bondage comes only by Your Will.
Liberation from bondage is effected by God's will.
(Band) to be imprisoned, and (khalasi) to be liberated from the eighty-four — all this happens within Akal Purakh's (bhanai) Hukam.
85FC: Horu = any other way contrary to the will. Koi = any man.
No man can tell of any other way apart from the will (that is, no man can say that there could be any other means of release from attachment besides walking in the will).
No one else has any say in this.
No one else has any say in it.
No one can say this: 'why was it done thus? It should have been done so'.
7AFD: Khaiku = a raw man, a fool. Aakhani pai = makes the attempt to say, (that is,) makes the attempt to tell (of some other means of release from attachment).
(But) if some fool makes the attempt to tell (of some other means of release from the love of Maya),
If some fool should presume to say that he does,
If some (khaiku) fool begins (aakhani pai) to tell of His end,
R3S4: Ohu = that fool alone. Jetia = how many (blows). Muhi = upon the face. Khai = he takes.

then he alone knows how many blows he takes upon his face (through this folly) (that is, there is only one way to be saved from 'falsehood', that a man walk in the will. But if some fool seeks some other way, then instead of being saved from this 'falsehood' he becomes all the more afflicted).
he shall learn, and feel the effects of his folly.
he shall know how many lashes he receives on his face.

he alone will know how many blows he takes upon his face from the Jamduts in the next world. As in: 'thau nahi khaika'. The purport is this: those who speak contrary to the Vedas, Shastras and the Guru's words most certainly receive the punishment of Dharam Rai.
GXTL: 'Akal Purakh Himself knows (the beings' needs) and Himself gives (the gifts)' —
He Himself knows, He Himself gives.
The Lord Himself knows everything and Himself gives.
The Lord Himself knows the beings' condition, and Himself gives all the provision — food, drink, clothing, dwelling and the rest.
JWU4: Aakhahi = they say. Si bhi = this thing too. Kei kei = many men.
— many men say this too. (Not all are ungrateful.)
Few, very few are those who acknowledge this.
Again few are those who acknowledge God's gifts.
There are also some few who say this, and this is their conviction.
ZDF9: O Nanak! The man upon whom Akal Purakh bestows His own praise —
One who is blessed to sing the Praises of the Lord,
Anyone whom the Lord grants wisdom to praise and eulogize Him,
Sri Guru Ji says: O Siddhas! He upon whom (siphati) Akal Purakh bestows the doing of His own (salahi) praise —
B8J0: Nanak = O Nanak! Patisahi patisahu = the emperor of emperors. ||25||
— he becomes the emperor of emperors (praise is the highest gift of all). ||25||
O Nanak, is the king of kings. ||25||
O Nanak! he is the (spiritual) king of kings.

— that Gurmukh who does the praise is the emperor of emperors. As in: 'brahm giani aapi parmesaru'. Here the word is 'patisahi', and in pronunciation it is 'patisahin', joined with a bindi. There it is to be understood thus: when the bir of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji was bound, the Sikhs made ardas: 'O Merciful to the poor, You have nowhere placed the adhak or the bindi in the words'. Then the utterance came from His own mouth: 'my Sikhs, knowing what is fitting, will pronounce it so'. ||25|| Now they tell the greatness of those sants:
MU2K: Amul = beyond price, that upon which no price can be set. Gun = Akal Purakh's virtues.
(Akal Purakh's) virtues are beyond price (that is, no price can be set upon the virtues). The trading in (these virtues) is beyond price too.
Priceless are His Virtues, Priceless are His Dealings.
Priceless are Yours merits, O Lord! and priceless Your dealings.

Those virtues whose price cannot be told — their name is 'beyond price'. So such priceless virtues as gyan and the rest are in the sants; and to free the seekers of the sense of 'I' and 'mine' and to bring about the attainment of the true Self — this trading of theirs is beyond price too.

Priceless are those who engage in this trade, as are the treasures of His virtue. Priceless are those who come for this, and those who take it away. Priceless are those who love Him, those absorbed in Him. Priceless is divine justice, as is His court. Priceless are His scales of justice, and the weights used. Priceless are His gifts and signs of approval. Priceless is divine mercy, His divine command. Priceless, so priceless, it cannot be described. By speaking of Him continually, one remains absorbed in Him. The Vedas and Puranas speak of Him. The scholars speak and lecture about Him. Brahma describes You, as does Indra. As do Gopis and Govind (Krishna). Shiva describes You, as do Siddhas. The many Buddhas created by You try to describe You. The demons describe You, the demi-gods describe You. The god-like humans, the silent sages, and devotees speak of You. So many try to describe You. So many have described You over and over, and left this world. If You were to create this many beings again, even then they could not describe You. He is as great as He wants to be. O Nanak, only the true Lord knows (His greatness). If any boastful person tries to say that they can describe Him, then he will be counted as a great fool. ||26||
XEQ3: Vapariye = those who trade in Akal Purakh's virtues. Bhandar = the storehouses.
Those men too are beyond price who trade (in Akal Purakh's virtues); the storehouses (of the virtues) are beyond price too.
Priceless are His Dealers, Priceless are His Treasures.
Priceless are Yours dealers and priceless Your treasures.

Those who desire mukti, who have renounced the longing for happiness even up to Brahm-lok, the mumukshus who are the traders in this wealth — they too are beyond price. And the heart of the Satigurus, in which stands established the storehouse of bhagti, direct-realised and joined with all virtues — that too is beyond price.
EU2A: Aavahi = the men who come (for this trade). Lai jahi = they carry away (having bought this merchandise).
Those men are beyond price who come (into the world for this trade). They too are of great fortune who (buying this merchandise) carry it away.
Priceless are those who come to Him, Priceless are those who buy from Him.
Priceless are they who come to You and priceless they who purchase and fetch goods from You.
The mumukshu's coming to the sants for the taking of this wealth — that too is beyond price. And the virtues they carry away from the sants — those too are beyond price.
T80Z: Bhai = in bhau, in love. Samahi = they are merged (in Akal Purakh).
Those men who are in Akal Purakh's love, and those men who are merged in that Akal Purakh — they too are beyond price.
Priceless is Love for Him, Priceless is absorption into Him.
Priceless is Your affection and priceless the absorption in You.
And the (bhai) love that is mutually between Guru and Sikh — that too is beyond price; and the coming to be (samahi) of the bliss of the atma through union with the Gurus — this too is beyond price.
0T04: Dharmu = law, statute. Dibanu = court, royal court.
Akal Purakh's law and His royal court are beyond price.
Priceless is the Divine Law of Dharma, Priceless is the Divine Court of Justice.
Priceless is Your Divine law and priceless Your Court.
(Dharmu) bhagti too is beyond price; the (dibanu) assembly of sants, that too is beyond price.
YH93: Tulu = weighing, scales. Parvanu = the standard, the weight used in weighing.
Those scales are beyond price and that weight is beyond price (with which He weighs the beings' good and bad deeds).
Priceless are the scales, priceless are the weights.
Priceless are Your scales and priceless Yours weights.

The (tulu) scales that are the sant-jans' intellect are beyond price too; the (parvanu) weight that is reflection is beyond price too — with which the mumukshus weigh their own atma, that is, come to certainty.
7UZX: Bakhsis = mercy, compassion. Nisanu = the mark of Akal Purakh's bestowal.
His bestowal, and the marks of that bestowal, are beyond price too.
Priceless are His Blessings, Priceless is His Banner and Insignia.
Priceless are Yours gifts and priceless Your mark of approval.

The bestowal that is the Gurus' updesh is beyond price too; and the (nisanu) manifesting of the atma that comes about through it is beyond price too. Or: the (nisanu) mark of bhagti which the Satigurus have given — that too is beyond price.
NKLS: Akal Purakh's bestowal and His command too are beyond all pricing (no one can take their measure).
Priceless is His Mercy, Priceless is His Royal Command.
Priceless are Your benevolence and priceless Your order.

The Satigurus' grace too is beyond price; and the (phurmanu) speaking of the Satigurus' command, that too is beyond price. Question: the Parmeshvar by whose bhagti the sant-jans are priceless — what is that Parmeshvar like? Answer:
ABFZ: Amulu = beyond estimating. Amulo amulu = priceless upon priceless, beyond all estimating.
Akal Purakh is beyond all estimating; no measure of Him can be taken.
Beyond price and invaluable, the Lord cannot be expressed.
He is beyond price of the priceless. His greatness cannot be told at all as a definite apprehension (idanta), that 'He is this much'.
D11C: Aakhi aakhi = taking the measure again and again. Rahe = they have been left behind, they have grown weary. Liv lai = having fastened liv, having fastened the attention.
The men who, fastening their attention, take Akal Purakh's measure — they (in the end) are exhausted.
Speak of Him continually, and remain absorbed in His Love.
By continually speaking of You, I remain absorbed in Your love.

Even so, telling and telling, in the past and the future and now in the present too, the sant-jans keep their disposition fastened upon Him. Question: is it the sants alone who tell His glory, or does anyone else tell it too? Answer:
99JY: Aakhahi = they are saying, they describe. Ved path = the recitations of the Vedas, the mantras of the Vedas.
The mantras of the Vedas and the Purans take Akal Purakh's measure.
The Vedas and the Puraanas speak.
The reciters of the Vedas and the Puranas Proclaim You.
The 4 Vedas say it too; the 18 Purans say it too.
ZEVZ: Parhe = learned men, scholars. Karahi vakhian = they make discourse, they give updesh, they recite to others.
Learned men too, who give updesh (to others), make description (of Akal Purakh).
The literate repeat Your Name and deliver discourses apropos You.
And those who recite them say it too; and those who, having recited that text, make discourse and katha upon it — or who make discourse and teeka — they say it too.
FDPH: Barme = many Brahmas. Ind = the devas Indra.
Many Brahmas and many Indras utter Akal Purakh's greatness.
Brahmas speak of You and Indras speak of You as well.
Brahma Ji says it too; (indu) Chandra, or Indra, says it too.

WTLL: The Gopis and many Krishnas take Akal Purakh's measure.
The milk-maids and Krishna speak of You.
The Gopis say it too, and (govind) Krishna Ji says it too, in the Gita and the rest; or, the Gopis say it to that Govind.
Q9NN: Many Shivs and Siddhas utter Akal Purakh's greatness.
The Shiva speak of You and the miracle-mongers speak of You as well.
And (isar) Mahadev Ji says it too, and Gorakh and the other Siddhas say it too.
SQND: Kete = limitless, many. Kite = created by Akal Purakh. Budh = Mahatma Buddh.
The limitless Buddhs created by Akal Purakh utter His greatness.
All the Buddhas, created by You, proclaim You.
And how many (of the wise) Parmeshvar has made — or the planet Budh and the rest — they say it too.
ABKG: Demons and devas (too) utter Akal Purakh's greatness.
The demons speak, the demi-gods speak.
The demons proclaim You and the gods proclaim You.
The danavs, the offspring of Danu — Prahlad and the rest — say it too. The devas who were fashioned at the beginning of creation as the ordainers, who bear the designation ajan, they say it too.
M8B4: Suri nar = men of the disposition of the suras. Muni jan = the munis. Sev = sevaks.
Men of deva-like disposition, munis and sevaks take Akal Purakh's measure.
The spiritual warriors, the heavenly beings, the silent sages, the humble and serviceful speak.
The demi-gods the men, the silent persons and the servants speak of You.
(Muni) Narad and the rest say it too; and equally all the suras and men and (jan) the muni-bhagats, and (sev) those who are the worshippers of Shiv Ji, all say it.
3XVL: Kete = many beings. Aakhani pahi = they attempt to say.
Limitless beings are taking Akal Purakh's measure, and limitless more are attempting to take it.
Many speak and try to describe Him.
Good many describe You and attempt to describe You.
So how many in the present time have set about telling — that is, in the future they will tell.
71Q6: Kahi kahi = saying and saying, setting a price upon Akal Purakh again and again, taking Akal Purakh's measure again and again. Uthi uthi jahi = they are departing from the world.
Limitless beings, taking the measure again and again, are departing from this world.
Many have spoken of Him over and over again, and have then arisen and departed.
Many have repeatedly described You and arising and getting ready have departed.
How many in the past time have told and told and risen and gone.
4YZF: Ete kite = so many beings have been created. Hori = other limitless beings. Karehi = if You were to create (O Hari!).
So many (limitless) beings have been created in the world (who are describing Him); but (O Hari!) if You were to create still more (limitless beings),
If He were to create as many again as there already are,
Were You to create as many more as already created,
So many as have been made for the counting — if He were to make as many again — the sense: let them be added to the former ones —
F5CB: Ta = even then. Na kei kei = no man at all. Aakhi sakahi = they can say.
even then no being could take Your measure.
even then, they could not describe Him.
even then they can not describe a few virtues of Yours.
even then (koi) by no means at all will they be able to tell it.
M1HS: Jevadu = how great. Bhavai = He wishes. Tevadu = that great.
O Nanak! Parmatma becomes as great as He wishes (He expands His own creation).
He is as Great as He wishes to be.
The Lord becomes so great as great He pleases.
However great an expanse He wishes to make, that great He becomes — the sense: Parmeshvar is of true resolve (sat-sankalp).
JCDQ: Sacha soi = that ever-abiding Akal Purakh.
That ever-abiding Hari Himself alone knows (how great He is).
O Nanak, the True Lord knows.
O Nanak! Only the True Lord Himself knows His greatness.
Sri Guru Ji says: that True One alone knows all.
33KG: Bolu vigaru = a loose talker, a loud mouth.
If some loud-mouthed man sets about telling (how great Akal Purakh is),
If anyone presumes to describe God,
If some prater says that he can describe God
If some (bolu vigaru) speaker of empty words tells Parmeshvar's end, saying 'Parmeshvar is this much',
G676: Likhiai = (that loud-mouth) is written down. Siri gavara gavaru = a boor above boors, the fool of fools, an utter fool. ||26||
then that man is reckoned the fool of fools. ||26||
he shall be known as the greatest fool of fools! ||26||
then write him down as the most foolish of the foolish.

then he is written down as a boor above boors, that is, among the utter fools. ||26|| Question: what is the door and the home of such a Creator like, where He sits and does the sustaining of all the moving and unmoving creation — that is, sustains all? Answer:
G6UD: Keha = of what kind, utterly wondrous. Daru = door. Jitu = where. Bahi = having sat. Sarab = all the beings. Samale = You have done the sustaining.
That door and home is utterly wondrous, where, sitting, (O Nirankar!) You are doing the sustaining of all beings.
Where is that Gate, and where is that Dwelling, in which You sit and take care of all?
Which is that gate and mansion, sitting where-in You takest care of all, O Lord!

That door and that home, in truth, cannot be told at all. According to your question, for the sake of the seekers' meditation, we describe something of the door and home in sargun form. Standing before Parmeshvar, He makes His supplication and utters the answer to the Siddhas. The true Self is the home, the satsang the door; or Baikunth is the home and the world the door. Now they tell of the making of Parmeshvar's door — the world:

Which is that door of Yours, which is that house, where You sit and take care of everything? Countless sounds/melodies are playing there, and many musicians playing instruments. There are countless Ragas and Raginis, and countless beings who sing (of You). The wind, waters, and fire sing of You; the righteous judge of Dharma sings of You at Your door. Chitr and Gupt (the recording angels) who know how to write, and reflect on Dharma through their writing, also sing of You. Shiva, Brahma, and the goddess of beauty sing of You, who look beautiful, having been adorned by You. Indra, sitting on his throne, sings of You, with the deities at Your door. The Siddhas, absorbed in deep meditation, sing of You, and the Sadhs who contemplate on You. The celibates, charitable, and contented sing of You; as do the mighty warriors. The great Pandits and Rishis sing of You, who study the Vedas across the ages. The enchanting heavenly beauties who entice the heart, in heaven, on earth, and the unconscious, also sing of You. The celestial jewels You created sing of You, as do the 68 places of Pilgrimage. The mighty warriors and spiritual heroes sing of You, as do the creatures of all four sources (all beings).
3HYE: Nad = sound, shabad, melody. Vavanhare = the players.
(In this creation of Yours) there are countless instruments and melodies; limitless beings are the players (of those instruments).
The Sound-current of the Naad vibrates there, and countless musicians play on all sorts of instruments there.
Countless musical instruments of various types resound there and too may are the musicians.
O Siddhas! At the doorway of that home there are countless instruments, nad and the rest, and they are sounding in countless ways, and how many are their players.
4DUL: Pari = ragini. Siu = together with. Pari siu = together with the raginis. Kahiani = they are told, they are spoken of.
Limitless ragas, together with their raginis, are told, and countless beings are the singers (of these ragas) (who are singing You)!
So many Ragas, so many musicians singing there.
Good many measures with their consorts and good many minstrels hymn You.
How many endless ragas, together with their (pari) raginis, are told of. How many are the singers of those ragas, the Gandharvas and the other ragis.
WXCD: Tuhno = You (O Akal Purakh!). Baisantaru = fire. Raja dharamu = Dharam-raj. Duare = at Your door (O Nirankar!)
(O Nirankar!) air, water and fire are singing Your virtues. Dharam-raj, standing at Your door, is glorifying You.
The praanic wind, water and fire sing; the Righteous Judge of Dharma sings at Your Door.
The wind, the water and fire sing You and the Righteous Justice sings Yours praises at Your door.

(Tuhno) You are sung by the wind, and by water — that is, by Varun, the presiding deva of water — and by (baisantaru) fire: the jatharagni (digestive fire) 1, the barvagni (submarine fire) 2, the davagni (forest fire) 3. And at Your door, the Dharam Raja who takes the reckoning of all, or Parmatma the King, also sings the praise.
VNN6: Chitu guptu: those beings who, dwelling in the Jam-lok, write the reckoning of the good and bad deeds of the world's beings. This idea comes down through the religious books of the ancient Hindu faith. Dharamu = the king of all. Likhi likhi = having written and written, that is, whatever those Chitr-Gupt write.
Those Chitr-Gupt too, who know how to write (the reckoning of beings' good and bad deeds), and whose writing Dharam-raj reflects upon, are doing Your praises.
Chitr and Gupt, the angels of the conscious and the subconscious who record actions, and the Righteous Judge of Dharma who judges this record sing.
Chitra Gupat (the recording angels) who know how to write and on the basis of whose scribed writ the Righteous Judge adjudicates, sing You.

He who writes down the hidden deeds of the beings on the mind — that is Chitr-Gupt, who knows the good and evil deeds of the beings; and according to his writing Dharam Raja reflects upon the judgment, and gives the fruit of good and evil, svarg and narak and the rest — that Chitr-Gupt too sings of You.
6DR6: Isaru = Shiv. Barma = Brahma. Devi = the goddesses. Sohani = they look beautiful, they appear comely. Savare = adorned by You.
(O Akal Purakh!) the goddesses, Shiv and Brahma, who are adorned by You, are singing You.
Shiva, Brahma and the Goddess of Beauty, ever adorned, sing.
Shiva, Brahma and goddess, ever beautiful, as adorned by You, sing You.

Adorned by You, that is fashioned by You, (isaru) Shiv and (barma) Brahma, and their goddesses — that is, their shaktis — who are resplendent: they, together with those shaktis, sing Your praise daily.
SLHX: Ind = the devas Indra. Idasani = (id-aasani), upon Indra's seat. Dari = at Your door. Devatia nale = together with the devas.
Many Indras, seated upon their thrones, are praising You at Your door together with the devas.
Indra, seated upon His Throne, sings with the deities at Your Door.
Indra, seated on his throne with the deities at Your gate, sings You.
Indra, seated upon Indra's throne amid the (dari) host of devas, sings Your praise at Your door; or, sings (nale) together with the devas, joined with honour.
TAMR: Samadhi andari = joined in samadhi, having fastened samadhi. Sidh = in the ancient Sanskrit books, the Siddhs are held to be those beings who were above the rank of men and below the devas. These Siddhs were a mass of purity and were reckoned masters of all eight siddhis. Vichare = having reflected and reflected.
The Siddhs, fastening their samadhis, are singing You; the Sadhs, reflecting and reflecting, are praising You.
The Siddhas in Samaadhi sing; the Saadhus sing in contemplation.
In their meditative mood the perfect persons sing of You and the saints on their contemplation sing as well as.
The Siddh-folk, established in samadhis, sing Your praise. And the Sadhus who are possessed of reflection sing the praise with reflection.
Z22B: Sati = the charitable, those who give in dan. Vir karare = sturdy warriors.
Men of continence, men of charity, and men of contentment are singing Your virtues, and (limitless) sturdy warriors are uttering Your greatnesses.
The celibates, the fanatics, the peacefully accepting and the fearless warriors sing.
The celibates, the contented, sing Yours praises and the dauntless warriors admire You.

The jatis; and the satis, the speakers of truth; and the santokhis, those who stay content with whatever is obtained; and the fifty-two virs (karare) attentively — or, (vir) the warriors who are (karare) unyielding — sing Your praise.
NU8S: Parhani = they read. Rakhisar = (rikhi isar), the very great rishis, the maharishis. Jugu jugu = in every age, ever. Veda nale = together with the Vedas.
(O Akal Purakh!) the Pandits and the great rishis who read (the Vedas) are singing You together with the Vedas.
The Pandits, the religious scholars who recite the Vedas, with the supreme sages of all the ages, sing.
The scholars, the readers of the Vedas of all the ages, together with seven supreme sages, exalt You.
The Pandits, and the readers — that is, the students — and the sense-conquering rishishvars, in age after age, together with the Vedas: all these sing Your praise.
BZ16: Mohania = beautiful women. Machh = in the mortal world. Paiale = in patal.
Beautiful women, who in svarg, in the mortal world and in patal (that is, everywhere) entice a man's mind, are singing You.
The Mohinis, the enchanting heavenly beauties who entice hearts in this world, in paradise, and in the underworld of the subconscious sing.
The captivating She-seraphs who beguile the heart in paradise, this world and the nether-regions, sing You.
The (mohania) women who entice the mind — those of svarg, those of (machh) the mortal world, then those of (paiale) patal; or, O Enticer of the mind! — all these sing Your praise.
RURG: Upae tere = created by You. Ath sathi = sixty-eight. Tirath nale = together with the tiraths.
(O Nirankar!) the jewels created by You, together with the sixty-eight tiraths, are singing You.
The celestial jewels created by You, and the sixty-eight holy places of pilgrimage sing.
The fourteen invaluable objects created by You, with sixty-eight places of pilgrimage, hymn You.

(Ratan) the most excellent of the excellent things in this creation which You have brought forth(1) — they too sing Your praise. The 68 tiraths, (nale) the rivers and streams — that is, their presiding devas — all these sing Your praise. In the Guru's bani the word 'athsathi' indicates the principal tiraths. If the tiraths happen to be more than these, there is no fault in it. Then this is the meaning: the presiding devas of the principal tiraths and of the rivers and streams sing Your praise.
T08A: Jodh = warriors. Maha bal = of great strength. Sura = heroes. Khani chare = the four khanis: andaj, jeraj, svetaj, utbhuj. Khani = a mine, that which is dug into to bring out metals or jewels and such things. This is a Sanskrit word. The root is 'khan', whose meaning is 'to dig'. Khani chare: from ancient times this idea has been coming down in the Hindu religious books, that there are four mines of the making of all the inert and conscious things of the world: the egg, the womb, sweat, and springing up of itself. 'Chare khani' here means the beings of all four mines, the whole creation.
Warriors and heroes of great strength are doing Your praise. The beings of all four khanis are singing You.
The brave and mighty warriors sing; the spiritual heroes and the four sources of creation sing.
The supremely mighty warriors and Divine heroes sing You and four sources of creation magnify You.

(Jodh) the rathi, who fights against one his own equal; (mahabal) the maharathi, who fights against ten thousand; (sura) the atirathi, who alone fights against countless numbers, as Sri Krishan Ji or Sri Guru Gobind Singh Ji — for an atirathi does not come to be except from an avatar. Inwardly: he who has conquered the body is the rathi; he who has conquered the body and the senses is the maharathi; he who has conquered the countless currents of the mind is the atirathi — all sing Your praise alone. And the beings in the four khanis — andaj, jeraj, svetaj, utbhuj — all these sing Your praise.
99PA: Khand = a piece, a piece of the universe, (that is) each earth. Mandal = a circle, one circle of the universe, in which one sun, one moon, an earth and so on are reckoned. Varbhanda = the whole creation. Kari kari = having made, having fashioned. Dhare = set in place.
The whole creation, and all the creation's khands and mandals, which You have created and set in place, are singing You.
The planets, solar systems and galaxies, created and arranged by Your Hand, sing.
The continents, worlds and solar systems, created and installed by Your hand, chant Yours glories.

Those which He has (kari kari) fashioned and fashioned and held in place by His own sustaining power — such nine khands, and the mandals, the portions lying within a khand, which they now call a hata: the Bengal hata, the Punjab hata, the Madras hata; or a hundred yojans is called a mandal — their inhabiting kings, or their presiding devas, all sing Your praise. And (varbhanda)(1) the universes, which are endless — their presiding devas too sing Your praise.
SP1N: Sei = those beings alone. Tudhu bhavani = they are pleasing to You. Rate = dyed, intoxicated in love. Rasale = (ras aalay) the homes of relish, the relishers.
(O Akal Purakh!) (in truth) only those bhagats sing You, dyed in Your love and full of relish (that is, their singing alone bears fruit), who are pleasing to You.
They alone sing, who are pleasing to Your Will. Your devotees are imbued with the Nectar of Your Essence.
Your saints who are pleasing to You and are steeped in Name (the home of Nectar), they alone eulogise You.
In truth those alone sing You who are pleasing to You. Who are they that are pleasing? The bhagats who are dyed in You, who are (rasale) the gathering, or the home of love.
TB32: Hori kete = countless other beings. Mai chiti = in my mind. Mai chiti na aavani = they do not come into my mind, they cannot be counted by me, they are beyond my reflection. Kia vichare = what reflection can he make?
Countless other beings are singing You, who cannot even be counted by me. (And) what reflection can (poor) Nanak make?
So many others sing, they do not come to mind. O Nanak, how can I consider them all?
Many others, whom I cannot recollect within my mind, sing You. How can Nanak think of them?

Besides those told of before, (kete) endless others too sing You. They do not come into my mind in remembrance. Sri Guru Ji says: how far shall I reflect? — the sense: the count of those singers does not come within remembrance.
3BSB: That Akal Purakh is ever-abiding. That Master is true, and His greatness too is forever immovable.
That True Lord is True, Forever True, and True is His Name.
That and that Lord is ever true His is true and true is His Name.
That same ever-true Master was in the past; that same True One, possessed of true (nai) greatness, is now.
Q2ZY: Hosi = He will be, He will abide. Jai na = He is not born. Na jasi = nor will He die. Jini = which Akal Purakh. Rachai = has brought into being.
The Akal Purakh who has brought this creation into being is present at this moment and will abide forever. He was not born, nor will He die.
He is, and shall always be. He shall not depart, even when this Universe which He has created departs.
He, who created the creation is and shall also be. He shall not depart when the creation shall depart (disappear).

(Bhi) again, that same True One will (hosi) be forever in the future. And the creation will (jai) pass away and be gone; He who has fashioned it will not (jasi) go. Or: He who made the creation was not born nor will He (jasi) be destroyed. Question: did He make that creation from His own pure Self, or in some other manner? Answer:
MC85: Rangi rangi = of colours and colours, of many colours. Bhati = of many kinds. Kari kari = having created. Jinsi = of many species. Jini = which Akal Purakh.
The Akal Purakh who has fashioned Maya of many colours, kinds and species —
He created the world, with its various colors, species of beings, and the variety of Maya.
God, who fashioned the world, has by diverse contrivances created the creation of various colours and Kinds.

Of colours and colours, white and yellow and the rest; (bhati) of many sorts — the sense, having the differences of individuals; of species and species, that is having the differences of man, deva, asur, beast, bird and the rest — (kari kari) fashioning and fashioning, He has displayed it. And He who has brought it forth by means of Maya — the sense: it is in this manner that the Maya-strengthened One has made it.
9GWC: Vekhai = He does the sustaining. Kita aapna = His own created world. Jiv = just as. Vadiai = will.
— just as is His will (that is, as great as He Himself is, with a heart that great He has fashioned the world and) is also doing the sustaining of what He has created.
Having created the creation, He watches over it Himself, by His Greatness.
Having created the creation, He as it pleases His Honour, beholds His handiwork.
As is that Akal Purakh's (vadiai) wish, so does He fashion and fashion and watch over the world He has made.
5GNH: Karsi = He will do. Na karna jai = it cannot be done.
Whatever pleases Akal Purakh, that alone will He do; no being can lay a command before Akal Purakh (one cannot say to Him, 'do not do it thus, do it so').
He does whatever He pleases. No order can be issued to Him.
Whatever pleases Him, He does that. No one can issue an order to Him.

Whatever seems good to Parmeshvar, that very work He does, and hereafter too He will (karsi) do. No command can be laid upon Him by anyone — that 'why was this work done thus, and why was it not done so'.
DT5S: Saha pati sahibu = the emperor of emperors. Rahanu = abiding (is possible), abiding befits. Rajai = in Akal Purakh's will. ||27||
Akal Purakh is the emperor, the emperor even of emperors. O Nanak! For the beings, to abide in His will alone (is what befits them). ||27||
He is the King, the King of kings, the Supreme Lord and Master of kings. Nanak remains subject to His Will. ||27||
He is the King, the Emperor of the Kings, Nanak remains subject to His will.

O brother! That Parmeshvar is the emperor of shahs and emperors. Sri Guru Ji says: therefore it is fitting to abide within His command alone. ||27|| The Siddhas then said: O young Nanak! Take up the garb of Yoga; wearing the earrings, the wallet, the ashes, the patched coat, the staff and the rest, make obeisance to Gorakh. You will be excellent, and the disciples of the Aai Panth will stay with you. You will conquer the world; seize the nad, and the riddhis and siddhis will remain present before you. To them he spoke this answer:
2Y9L: Munda = earrings. Saramu = effort, labour. Patu = the vessel, the begging-bowl. {Note on 'patu': in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji this word comes in three forms, 'pati', 'pat', 'patu'. Though in Punjabi it may seem to be one and the same word, all three have come separately from Sanskrit. The word 'pati' in Sanskrit means 'husband, master'. In Punjabi another meaning of it is also used, 'honour, repute'. The word 'patu' is singular. In Sanskrit it is 'patra', whose meaning is 'vessel, cup, begging-bowl'. Its plural is 'pat', but in this above meaning the word 'pat' has not come in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji. So for the word 'pat' there is another word in Sanskrit, 'patra', whose meaning is 'the leaves of trees'.} Karahi = if you make. Bibhuti = the ash of cow-dung.
(O Yogi!) if you make contentment your earrings, effort your begging-bowl and wallet, and the ash of meditation upon Akal Purakh (that you smear upon your body),
Make contentment your ear-rings, humility your begging bowl, and meditation the ashes you apply to your body.
Make contentment your ear-rings, modesty your begging bowl and wellect and the Lord's meditation your ashes.

To remain pleased with whatever is obtained — this is contentment; and to feel (saram) shame at evil deeds — these two earrings have been worn. In Ramkali too it is said: 'sarme kia mundra paau tun jogi'. And the Yogis keep a wallet: to be free of sins and to have kept one's (pati) honour intact in this world and the next — this very thing is the wallet that has been worn. To stay established always in meditation upon the Akal Murati — this very thing they make the smearing of ashes.
ZEPX: Khintha = the patched coat. Kalu = death. Kuari kaia = the virgin body, the body saved from the objects and the vices, the body untouched by the vices. Jugati = the discipline of the Yoga creed. Partit = faith, conviction.
let death (the fear of it) be your patched coat, let keeping the body safe from the vices be your Yoga-discipline, and make faith your staff (then the wall of falsehood within can be broken).
Let the remembrance of death be the patched coat you wear, let the purity of virginity be your way in the world, and let faith in the Lord be your walking stick.
Let thought of death be your patched coat, chastity like that of virgin's body, your life's department and faith in God your staff.

This (kuari) morsel of Kal, the impermanent (kaia) body — such an understanding is what has been made the patched coat. As in the taking off of a patched coat and the putting on of another there is neither labour nor anxiety, in that same way he has understood the body to be impermanent. A patched coat is made of pieces of many colours; so in this too there are endless kinds — the fair and dark colours, blood, bone, fat, marrow and the rest — thus has he understood it. The sense is this: he has seen himself as distinct from the body. Or: so long as it is (kuari) virgin of Kal — that is, Kal has not yet seized the body — to join oneself (jugati) to the bhajan before that, this very thing has been made the patched coat. And to join the disposition with (partit) certainty upon the Akal Murati — this very thing is the staff that has been taken up.
UNDR: Aai panthu = there are 12 sects of the Yogis; among them the 'Aai Panth' is reckoned the highest. Panthi = one of the Aai Panth, one connected with the Aai Panth. Sagal = all the beings. Jamati = those who study in one and the same school, in one and the same class; friends and companions who sit together in one place. Mani jitai = the mind being conquered, if the mind be conquered. (Note: phrases of this kind come many times in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji, as: nai visariai = if the Nam be forgotten; nai manniai = if the Nam be accepted.)

The man who reckons all the beings of the whole creation as his own friends and companions is (in truth) the one of the Aai Panth. If one's own mind be conquered, then the whole world is conquered (that is, then the world's Maya cannot separate one from Parmatma).
See the brotherhood of all mankind as the highest order of Yogis; conquer your own mind, and conquer the world.
Make the brother hood with all, the highest sect of yogic order and deem the conquering of self the conquest of the world.

'Aai Panth' is the name of a particular sect of the Yogis: those at the end of whose name there is an 'i', as Bal Gundai — that is to be known as the Aai Panth. This sect is held the highest among the Yogis. (Sagal jamati) our love is toward all the companies(1) — this alone is our Aai Panth. And having conquered the mind, we have become the conquerors of the world(2).
CBB2: Aadesu = obeisance. Tisai = to that same Akal Purakh.
(So, to remove the wall of falsehood) make obeisance to that (Akal Purakh) alone,
I bow to Him, I humbly bow.
Obeisance, my obeisance is to that Lord.
The Yogis speak the greeting 'aades, aades'. 'Aades' is the name for a bowing in salutation. (Aadesu) to Him who is free of the limitations of place, time and thing, our (aadesu) salutation is made.
CBMX: Aadi = from the beginning. Anilu = free of blemish, pure, of pure form. Anadi = He who has no beginning. Anahati = (an-aahati); aahati = destruction, decay (the Sanskrit root of this word is 'han', whose meaning is 'to strike, to destroy'); anahati = free of destruction, unbroken. Jugu jugu = in every age, ever. Vesu = form. ||28||
who is the beginning (of all), who is of pure form, whose beginning cannot be found, who is beyond destruction, and who ever remains one and the same. ||28||
The Primal One, the Pure Light, without beginning, without end. Throughout all the ages, He is One and the Same. ||28||
He is primal, pure, sans beginning, indestructible and of the same one vesture all the ages through.

So He who is the beginning of all, and (anilu) free of the colours such as blue(1), and anaad, free of any beginning, and (anahati) not struck down by any second — the sense: He is unbroken — and in (jug jug) all four ages is of one (vesu) form. ||28||
FFJA: Bhugati = churma (the sacred food). Bhandarani = the woman who serves out the bhandara. Ghati ghati = in every body. Vajahi = they are sounding. Nad = the shabad. (Yogis sound a nadi at the time of eating the bhandara, which they keep hung about their neck.)

(O Yogi! If) the gyan of Akal Purakh's all-pervadingness be your bhandara (the sacred food), and compassion be the server of this (gyan-form) bhandara, and (if, while partaking of the bhandara, there be sounding within you) that current of life which runs within every being, this nadi,
Let spiritual wisdom be your food, and compassion your attendant. The Sound-current of the Naad vibrates in each and every heart.
Make Divine Knowledge your food and mercy your steward and listen to the Divine music that beats in every heart.

The Yogi folk call prepared food 'bhugati'. So the inner faculty's disposition becoming Brahm-formed, seeing Him complete in all things — this very gyan-form is what has been made the bhugati; that is, we are satisfied by the bliss of the atma. Knowing the Lord's own form to be all, to show compassion upon all beings — this very thing is what has been made the woman who serves; the sense: compassion alone is the giver of gyan and the other virtues. The shabad which is sounding in every heart — that is, being uttered — that alone is our nad. Or: the conscious sustaining power which is known to be (vajahi) manifesting in every heart, that alone is our nad.
6V6K: Aapi = Akal Purakh Himself. Nathi = threaded through, in His control. Sabh = the whole creation. Ridhi = glory, greatness. Sidhi = among the Yogis eight great siddhis are held. The literal meanings of 'sidhi' are 'success', a miracle. (The eight siddhis are these: anima, laghima, prapti, prakamya, mahima, ishitva, vashitva, kamavasayita. Anima = becoming as small as an atom. Laghima = becoming of a very light weight. Prapti = the capacity to obtain every thing. Prakamya = an independent will which none can oppose. Mahima = the power to make oneself as great as one wishes. Ishitva = lordship. Vashitva = bringing another under one's own control. Kamavasayita = the power to keep lust and the other vices under control.) Avara = other, those which lead one away from Akal Purakh. Sad = relishes, cravings.

let Akal Purakh Himself be your Nath, in whose control the whole creation lies (then the wall of falsehood can break within you and your distance from Parmatma can be effaced. The riddhis obtained through Yoga-practices are worthless; these) riddhis and siddhis (are only) relishes that lead one off in some other direction.
He Himself is the Supreme Master of all; wealth and miraculous spiritual powers, and all other external tastes and pleasures, are all like beads on a string.
He Himself is supreme Lord who has snaffled all. Riches and miracles are extraneous relishes not liked by saints.

He who is the mahant among the Yogis is called a Nath. So He in whose thread of command the whole creation is threaded — that is, made subject — He Himself alone is our Nath. The Yogis have riddhis and siddhis with them. Now riddhi is that no shortage comes when one sets about serving out grain and the rest; and the eight siddhis, anima and the rest, are the principal ones. Or 18, or 23 — theirs is (avara) an inferior relish, because these are an obstruction in the attainment of the Akal Murati, the Dweller in Sach Khand; therefore their renunciation alone has been held the excellent thing(1).
8TCX: Sanjogu = union, that portion of Akal Purakh's will by which beings meet, or the world's other works come about. Vijogu = separation, that portion of Akal Purakh's will through which beings are parted, or by which some existing things are destroyed. Dui = both. Kar = the work of the world. Chalavahi = they are driving. (Among the Yogis there is one man for the bhandara who brings the provisions; understand this as Akal Purakh's 'sanjog'-form power. The second is the one who serves out, who is the 'vijog' power.) Lekhe = according to the reckoning of the deeds done. Aavahi = they come, they are obtained. Bhag = each one's own share, each one's own portion. (When serving out the bhandara the Yogis give each his portion in order; Akal Purakh's 'sanjog' and 'vijog' powers are serving out to all beings the portions of joy and sorrow according to the writ of their done deeds.)

Akal Purakh's 'sanjog' power and 'vijog' power are both (together) driving the work (of this world) (that is, through past conjunctions the beings of a family and so on come together here; then in His will they part and part again, and each in his own turn departs from here), and according to the writ (of all the beings' done deeds) the (portions of joy and sorrow) are being served out, each in his order (if this conviction be formed, then the wall of falsehood breaks within).
Union with Him, and separation from Him, come by His Will. We come to receive what is written in our destiny.
Union and separation both regulate the world's business and by destiny man obtains his share.

The Yogis have disciples with them. Whatever thing is to come, the karma-form disciple who does the joining brings it. Whatever thing is to go, the karma-form disciple who does the parting takes it away. The sense: according to prarabdh, joy and sorrow keep coming and going. In this way the two disciples, sanjog and vijog, drive the work. Whatever is written in our writ, that (bhag) portion comes to us — the sense: it is obtained.

481K: (So, to remove the wall of falsehood) make obeisance to that (Akal Purakh) alone,
I bow to Him, I humbly bow.
Obeisance, my obeisance is to that Lord.
The Yogis speak the greeting 'aades, aades'. 'Aades' is the name for a bowing in salutation. (Aadesu) to Him who is free of the limitations of place, time and thing, our (aadesu) salutation is made.
0QT9: who is the beginning (of all), who is of pure form, whose beginning cannot be found, who is beyond destruction, and who ever remains one and the same. ||29||
The Primal One, the Pure Light, without beginning, without end. Throughout all the ages, He is One and the Same. ||29||
He is primal, pure sans beginning, indestructible and of the same one vesture through all the ages.

So He who is the beginning of all, and (anilu) free of the colours such as blue, and anaad, free of any beginning, and (anahati) not struck down by any second — the sense: He is unbroken — and in (jug jug) all four ages is of one (vesu) form. ||29|| Now they tell, at some length, the manner of the creation:
7F2E: Eka = alone. Mai = Maya. Jugati = by a method, by a way. Viai = gave birth. Parvanu = manifestly.
(Among people this idea is commonly current that) Maya alone, by (some) method, gave birth, and manifestly three sons were born to her.
The One Divine Mother conceived and gave birth to the three deities.
The unique Mother (Master) formulating a plan of propagation installed three approved disciples.

O Siddhas! The One who is the Akal Murati Parmatma — when He came to (jugati) join with (mai) Maya, then Maya (viai) gave birth. First Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesh — these three disciples were made established. Or: (eka mai) the One who is Ishvar possessed of Maya — Maya joining with Him (viai) gave birth; the sense: being brought forth from Maya they are called sons; and since Parmatma gave them updesh, for that reason they are called disciples.
Maya, in her own way, gave birth to (the three) — their three disciples (Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva).
VRZR: Sansari = a householder. Bhandari = the master of the storehouse, the giver of sustenance. Lae = he holds. Dibanu = court, tribunal. {Note on 'tini': this word has three forms: 'tin', 'tini' and 'tini' (with long i). 'Tini' (long) means three. 'Tini' also means 'three', but it has another meaning besides. 'Tin' is a pronoun in the plural and 'tini' is a pronoun in the singular. Set against these, 'jin' is plural and 'jini' singular. (1) Tini = that man (singular): 'jini sevia tini paia manu' (Pauri 5). (2) Tin = those men (plural): 'jin hari japia tin phalu paia, sabhi tute maia phande' (3). Note: the word 'parvanu' also needs a little attention. In Japji Sahib this word has come in the following lines: (1) 'panch parvan, panch pardhanu' (Pauri 16); (2) 'amulu tulu, amulu parvanu' (Pauri 26); (3) 'eka mai jugati viai tini chele parvanu'; (4) 'tithai sohani panch parvanu' (Pauri 34). In Sanskrit this word is 'praman', which has several meanings, as: (a) a weight; (b) capacity; (c) proof, testimony; (d) one possessed of authority, acknowledged and accepted. In this meaning the word is used in two ways, as: 'vyakarane panini pramanam' and 'vedah pramanah', that is, in the singular (source breaks off here)}

Of them one (Brahma) became a householder (that is, he set about bringing forth the beings and creatures); one (Vishnu) became the master of the storehouse (that is, he set about the work of conveying sustenance to the beings); and one (Shiv) holds the court (that is, he destroys the beings).
One, the Creator of the World; One, the Sustainer; and One, the Destroyer.
One the world's creator (Brahma), one steward who gives sustenance (Vishnu) and one who has the disposition of destroying (Shiva).

One, Brahma, set about the bringing forth of the world; therefore he was called sansari. One, Vishnu, set about the sustaining of all by giving food and clothing; therefore he was called bhandari. One, Rudra, set about the (dibanu) laying (lae) — the dissolving and destroying — of this world; or, the habit of dissolving and destroying came about in the one Rudra.

One who created the world (Brahma), one who sustains it (Vishnu), and one who holds a court of justice (Shiva, the destroyer). Just as it pleases Him, so He runs the world — as it is His will (not Brahma, Shiva, or Vishnu's). He sees all, but none see Him — how wonderful is this! Surrender, to You I surrender. He is from the very beginning, pure, without beginning, and constant — throughout all ages, He is the same. ||30||
6Q3P: Jiv = just as, in what manner. Tisu = to that Akal Purakh. Chalavai = He drives (the work of the world). Phurmanu = command.

(But the true matter is this, that) just as it pleases that Akal Purakh and just as His command is, so He Himself is driving the work of the world (these Brahma, Vishnu and Shiv have nothing in their hands).
He makes things happen according to the Pleasure of His Will. Such is His Celestial Order.
As it pleases Him and as is His order, He makes them walk.

In whatever way it pleases that Akal Murati, in that way He drives these three. And in whatever way the (phurmanu) command is, in that way the three move. Or: in whatever way it pleases that Parmeshvar, (tivai) in that same way those three drive the world; and in whatever way Parmeshvar's (phurmanu) command is, in that same way they themselves also move.
YMXX: Ohu = Akal Purakh. Ona = to the beings. Nadari na aavai = is not seen. Vidanu = a wondrous marvel.
This is a great wonder, that Akal Purakh is watching (all the beings) but Akal Purakh is not seen by the beings.
He watches over all, but none see Him. How wonderful this is!
He beholds them but they see Him not. This is the greatest wonder.

That Akal Purakh watches the time of the beginning and end, and the strength, of those disciples Brahma and the rest; and (ona) to those three His form is not seen as a definite apprehension (idanta) — this is a very great (vidanu)(1) wonder.
A3DN: (So, in place of Brahma, Vishnu, Shiv and the rest) make obeisance to that (Akal Purakh) alone,
I bow to Him, I humbly bow.
Obeisance my obeisance is to the Lord.
The Yogis speak the greeting 'aades, aades'. 'Aades' is the name for a bowing in salutation. (Aadesu) to Him who is free of the limitations of place, time and thing, our (aadesu) salutation is made.
2JDC: who is the beginning (of all), who is of pure form, whose beginning cannot be found, who is beyond destruction, and who ever remains one and the same. (This alone is the means of removing the distance from that Lord.) ||30||
The Primal One, the Pure Light, without beginning, without end. Throughout all the ages, He is One and the Same. ||30||
He is primal, pure, sans beginning, indestructible and of the same one vesture all the ages through.

So He who is the beginning of all, and (anilu) free of the colours such as blue, and anaad, free of any beginning, and (anahati) not struck down by any second — the sense: He is unbroken — and in (jug jug) all four ages is of one (vesu) form. ||30|| Question: in what place is the seat of such a Nath?
6YHD: Aasanu = station. Loi = in the realm. Loi loi = in every realm. Aasanu bhandar = the station of the storehouses.
The station of Akal Purakh's storehouses is in every realm (that is, in every realm Akal Purakh's bhandaras are running).
On world after world are His Seats of Authority and His Storehouses.
Lord's seat and store houses are in all the worlds.
His seat is in all the realms — that is, it is everywhere; and the storehouse too is in all the realms. Sri Guru the 10th, in the Dasam Granth: 'jan ko det ajan ko det jamin ko det jaman ko daihain'.

In all realms are the Lord's storehouses. Whatever was put there, was put once for all. Having created the world, the Creator watches over it. O Nanak, true is the work of the True One. Surrender, to You I surrender. He is from the very beginning, pure, without beginning, and constant — throughout all ages, He is the same. ||31||
3AYC: Paia = Akal Purakh has put in. Kari kari = having created (the beings). Vekhai = He does the sustaining. Sirjanharu = the Akal Purakh who brings forth the creation.
Whatever (Akal Purakh) has put (into those storehouses) He has put in at one single time (that is, His storehouses are ever inexhaustible).
Whatever was put into them, was put there once and for all.
Whatever was put into them, was put but once for all.
Whatever each has received from that storehouse according to his own karma, all have received it at one single time. In that alone the maintenance goes on for the whole of life.
SKBT: Sachi = ever immovable, free of error.
The Akal Purakh who brings forth the creation, having created (the beings), is doing (their) sustaining.
Having created the creation, the Creator Lord watches over it.
Having created the creation the creator is beholding it.
As the Nath who is the mahant keeps the account of all the storehouses, so the Creator Akal Purakh, having fashioned all the places, keeps watching over them.
E1CC: O Nanak! This work (of the sustaining of the creation) of the ever-abiding (Akal Purakh) is forever immovable (it is free of error).
O Nanak, True is the Creation of the True Lord.
O Nanak! true is the work of the True Lord.

Sri Guru Ji says: all the work of that True Purakh is true; as He began it from the beginning, that same rule runs on right up to the dissolution. The sinners get narak, the meritorious get svarg, the gyanis get moksh, and so on.
9STB: (So) make obeisance to that (Akal Purakh) alone,
I bow to Him, I humbly bow.
obeisance, my obeisance is to that Lord.
The Yogis speak the greeting 'aades, aades'. 'Aades' is the name for a bowing in salutation. (Aadesu) to Him who is free of the limitations of place, time and thing, our (aadesu) salutation is made.
1RNS: who is the beginning (of all), who is of pure form, whose beginning cannot be found, who is beyond destruction, and who ever remains one and the same (this alone is the way by which the distance from that Lord can be effaced). ||31||
The Primal One, the Pure Light, without beginning, without end. Throughout all the ages, He is One and the Same. ||31||
He is primal, pure, sans beginning, indestructible and of the same one vesture all the ages through.

So He who is the beginning of all, and (anilu) free of the colours such as blue, and anaad, free of any beginning, and (anahati) not struck down by any second — the sense: He is unbroken — and in (jug jug) all four ages is of one (vesu) form. ||31|| Question: how may the darshan of such a Master be had? Answer:
FZ3S: Iku du = from one. Ik du jibhau = from one tongue. Hohi = they were to become. Lakh = a lakh (of tongues). Lakh hovahi = from a lakh of tongues they were to become. Lakh vis = twenty lakhs.
If from one tongue a lakh of tongues were to come, and from a lakh of tongues twenty lakhs were to be made,
If I had 100,000 tongues, and these were then multiplied twenty times more, with each tongue,
From one tongue let my tongues become a lakh and the hundred thousand become twenty lakhs.
Let one make such an imagining: that (ik du) from one tongue a lakh of tongues come to be, then from a lakh of tongues twenty lakh tongues come to be.

If my one tongue was to become 100,000, and that gets multiplied by 20 (2 million) — I would repeat, 100,000s of times, the Name of the One Lord of the Universe. On the path to God there is a ladder — one can climb and merge into Him (losing ego). By listening to the words of the heavens, even worms want to go there. O Nanak, by His grace, is He attained; the boasts of the false are false. ||32||
QG45: Gerha = rounds, turns. Aakhiahi = they be uttered. Eku namu jagdis = the one Nam of Jagdis. Jagdis = the Ish of the world, the Master of the world, Akal Purakh.

(if with these twenty lakh tongues) the one Nam of Akal Purakh were uttered a lakh times each (even then it is the false man's false boast; that is, if a man thinks 'on the strength of my own effort I can, by remembering the Nam in this way, attain Akal Purakh', then this is a false pride).
I would repeat, hundreds of thousands of times, the Name of the One, the Lord of the Universe.
With each tongue lakhs over lakhs times, I would repeat the Name of the world's Lord.

With each single tongue let the one Nam of Jagdis be uttered a lakh of lakh (gerha) times — as the utterance is, 'kot karan dijai mere karte', and so on; know the whole shabad. The settled point is this: let one jap the Nam night and day.
6PAP: Etu rahi = on this road, on the road that leads to meeting Akal Purakh. Pati pavarhia = the steps of the Husband, the steps that lead to meeting the Husband. Charhiai = it is climbed, it can be climbed. Hoi ikis = becoming of one form, effacing the sense of self.

On this road (the road of removing the distance from Parmatma), the steps that lead to meeting Akal Purakh can be climbed only by effacing one's sense of self. (With lakhs of tongues too, nothing comes of counted remembrance.
Along this path to our Husband Lord, we climb the steps of the ladder, and come to merge with Him.
In this way of the Bridegroom, there are ladders, by ascending whose steps, I would become one with Him.
By this road which is the japping of the Nam, let one climb the steps which are the stages(1) of the Husband; then the jiv's (ik) oneness with Ishvar comes about.
AGTS: Suni = having heard. Kita = to the worms.

Without removing the sense of self, this effort of counted recitations is as though) the worms, hearing talk of the sky, have also been seized with the wish to imitate (that they too might reach the sky).
Hearing of the etheric realms, even worms long to come back home.
By hearing celestial things even worms (the vile) wish to emulate.

Hearing the names of the stages, or hearing from two or four granths the reasonings and the greatness — as 'jaise brahm giani sada nirlepu', 'brahm giani aapi parmesuru' and so on, hearing the talk of the Brahm-gyanis who dwell in the chidakash — the worms, who are the sensual and base beings, proud of the body, sit down and imitate too, saying 'we also are gyanis'. As, seeing the Garuda flying in the sky, the worms too imitate the flying and begin to flap their wings — that is, with their own mouths they call themselves unattached. How can the ignorant worm reach the company of the gyani-swan?
HT8B: Nadri = by Akal Purakh's glance of mercy. Paiai = He is obtained, Akal Purakh is attained. Kurhai = of the false man. Kurhi thisi = a false boast, one's own false self-praise. ||32||
O Nanak! If Akal Purakh casts the glance of mercy, only then is He met; (otherwise) it is the false man's own merely false self-praise (that 'I am doing the remembrance'). ||32||
O Nanak, by His Grace He is obtained. False are the boastings of the false. ||32||
O Nanak! God is obtained by His grace and false is the boasting of the false.

Sri Guru Ji says: the Nam is obtained thus, by Parmeshvar's glance of grace. And it is (kurhai) the false ones' (kurhi this) false boast — the sense: without the practice of true gyan, what will the talk of the Shastras accomplish? ||32|| Everything is obtained by Akal Purakh's glance of grace; nothing comes about by one's own doing. This matter they now set forth at length:
NW8V: Aakhani = in the saying, in the speaking. Chupai = in (staying) silent. Joru = capacity, power, the wish of one's own mind.
In speaking too, and in staying silent, we have no power of our own at all.
No power to speak, no power to keep silent.
I have no power to speak and no power to remain silent.

Without Akal Purakh's glance of grace this jiv has not even the strength (aakhani) of speaking. When the tongue is stopped, then he cannot speak. Nor has he the strength of staying silent: when a dryness of the wind enters, then he keeps on babbling.

We have no power to speak or remain silent. No power to beg, no power to give. No power to live, no power to die (Kal's/God's). No power to acquire an empire or wealth, that causes us to become boastful. No power to be spiritually awakened by knowledge or contemplation. No power to liberate ourselves from worldly entanglements (the cycle of birth and death). The One whose hands hold that power, having created all, watches over it. O Nanak, by our own efforts, none are high or low. ||33||
8XBB: Mangani = in the begging. Deni = in the giving.
Neither does our own wish run in the begging, nor in the giving.
No power to beg, no power to give.
I have no power to beg and no power to give.

Nor has he the strength of begging, should he wish 'let me beg and bring away this thing'. As Kumbhkaran, setting out to beg for six months of waking, ended by begging for sleep. Nor has he the strength of giving: in the heart he wishes to give, but by the word of people and family, or by not having it to hand, he cannot give.
P07R: Jivani = in living. Marani = in dying.
In living too and in dying, our capacity (is of no use).
No power to live, no power to die.
I have no strength to live and no strength to die.

If he says 'let me stay living', in this too he has no strength: thousands of men die even while taking medicine. In dying too there is no strength: they have drowned in rivers, hung the noose, struck themselves with weapons, drunk poison, and yet did not die but were saved.
YKT7: Raji mali = in kingdom and wealth, in the obtaining of kingdom and wealth. Soru = clamour, puffing and blustering.
In the obtaining of this kingdom and wealth too our strength does not run (the kingdom and wealth on account of which there is puffing and blustering in our) mind.
No power to rule, with wealth and occult mental powers.
I have no strength to acquire empire and wealth, which stir up a commotion in the mind.

In the obtaining of kingdom and wealth, like Vasishth and the rest, there is no strength either. It is obtained, but no strength runs upon it at all — the sense: it wastes away. The doer is one, the outcome another. Let alone the rest: even upon the (soru) clamour of the mind's resolves and waverings there is no strength to stop it. Or, should he say 'having made myself a king and the rest, let me exert some strength', it is not so. All this is only the mind's clamour and uproar.
0GPM: Surti = in the surat, in spiritual wakefulness. Giani = in (obtaining) gyan. Vichari = in (doing) reflection.
Nor have we the capacity to stay in spiritual wakefulness, in gyan and in reflection.
No power to gain intuitive understanding, spiritual wisdom and meditation.
I have no power to gain understanding of Divine Knowledge and Lord's meditation.
The reciting of the shrutis and the Vedas and the doing of reflection upon gyan — in this too there is no strength.
WQC9: Jugati = in the discipline, in the observance. Chhutai = one is released, it comes to an end.
Nor is it in our power to abide in that discipline by which birth and death come to an end.
No power to find the way to escape from the world.
I have no power to find the way to escape from the world.

In the six Shastras there are many disciplines — that is, many illustrations — for being liberated from the world. But in taking them up too there is no strength of one's own. When the Creator's glance of grace falls, then they are taken up.
BPJS: Jisu hathi = in whose hand, in which Akal Purakh's hand. Kari vekhai = having fashioned (the creation) He is doing its sustaining. Soi = that same Akal Purakh. Sansaru = birth and death. {Note: to understand this line 'jisu hathi... soi', special attention needs to be given to the words 'soi' and 'kari vekhai'. In Japji Sahib the word 'soi' comes in the following lines: (1) 'aape aapi niranjanu soi' (Pauri 5); (2) 'ja karta sirathi kau saje, aape janai soi' (Pauri 21); (3) 'tisu uche kau janai soi' (Pauri 24); (4) 'nanak janai sacha soi' (Pauri 26); (5) 'soi soi sada sachu, sahibu sacha, sachi nai' (Pauri 27); (6) 'karahi anandu sacha mani soi' (Pauri 37). Of these lines above, only in the line of Pauri 24 is 'soi' said of the 'koi' man of the previous line; everywhere else it has come for 'Akal Purakh'. 'Kari vekhai' makes this same meaning firmer still. Vekhai = He does the sustaining, as: (1) 'gavai ko vekhai hadra haduri' (Pauri 3); (2) 'kari kari vekhai kita aapna, jiv tis di vadiai' (Pauri 27); (3) 'kari kari vekhai sirjanharu' (Pauri 31); (4) 'ohu vekhai ona nadari na aavai, bahuta ehu vidanu' (Pauri 27); (5) 'kari kari vekhai nadari nihal' (Pauri 37); (6) 'vekhai vigsai kari vicharu' (Pau (source breaks off here)}
That same Akal Purakh, in whose hand is the capacity, fashions the creation and does its sustaining (in every way).
He alone has the Power in His Hands. He watches over all.
He, in whose hand the power is, exercises and beholds it.

Therefore, the Akal Purakh in whose hand the strength is, He alone, having done it, is watching. In the Gita it is said: 'Ishvar, seated in the hearts of all beings, causes all to revolve'. As the machine-holder drives the machine, so the machine runs; the machine has nothing in its own power. All is in the machine-holder's power. As the Guru's authority has it: 'jiu janti ke vas jant'.
FWE0: O Nanak! In himself no man is high, nor is any low (that is, He Himself, the Lord, is the maker of beings virtuous or vicious. Only if this conviction be formed through the blessing of remembrance is the being's distance from Parmatma effaced). ||33||
O Nanak, no one is high or low. ||33||
O Nanak! By one's own strength, none can be good or bad.

Sri Guru Ji says: therefore this ought to be known, that in this creation no one is of himself low, nor high. As the Lord has made each according to his former deeds, so is he turning out. ||33|| Question: tell the manner of karam-kand? Answer:
KCH3: Rati = nights. Ruti = seasons. Thiti = lunar dates. Var = days.
Nights, seasons, lunar dates and weekdays,
God created nights, seasons, lunar days, week days,
O Siddhas! (Rati) the nights; (ruti) basant 1, grikham 2, varsat 3, sarad 4, himant 5, sisar 6; thiti 15; var 7.

Nights, seasons, days, weeks; air, water, fire, and space — within these, Earth was created as a place for righteousness to come to God. On Earth, through God's will, there is a diversity of beings; their names are countless and limitless. By our actions, we are judged. You are true (eternal), and true (eternal) is Your court. There, the Saints are beautiful and honoured, and by Your blessing, they bear Your mark of approval. The ripe (mature) and unripe (immature) is only found out there. O Nanak, only by going there is this truly understood. ||34||
ZREW: Pavan = air of every kind. Patal = all the patals.
air, water, fire and patal — within the gathering of all these (Akal Purakh)
wind, water, fire and the nether regions
wind, water, fire and nether lands.
Air, water, fire, patal and the rest, the 14 loks — this is the whole expanse.
U8TR: Tisu vichi = within the aggregate of all these. Here special attention needs to be given to 'tisu'. All the words of the first line are in the plural. 'Tisu' is singular, whose meaning is 'the gathering of all'. Thapi rakhi = having established it He has set it, having fashioned it He has set it in place. Dharamsal = the abode for the earning of dharma.
has set the earth in place as the abode for the earning of dharma.
in the midst of these, He established the earth as a home for Dharma.
In the midst of these He established the earth as a home for the Lord's meditation.

Within it the Creator has set in place the (dharti) earth as a dharamsala. This much is to be understood beyond that: among the earths, Bharat-bhumi too is the chief; this alone is called the karam-bhumi. The deed done here the jiv enjoys in the other khands and dips. Therefore Bharat alone has been spoken of as the 'dharamsala'.
5KTJ: Tisu vichi = upon that earth. Jia = the beings and creatures. Jia jugati = the discipline of the beings, the manner of the beings' living (He has made). Ke rang = of many colours.
Upon this earth dwell beings of many disciplines and many colours,
Upon it, He placed the various species of beings.
There-in He placed beings of various types and colours.
In that dharamsala, Bharat-bhumi, there are beings of many sorts. Theirs is a discipline of dharma, karma and worship of many sorts; and theirs are colours of many sorts — fair, dark and the rest.
3TLN: Tin ke = of those beings. Anant = limitless. {Note on 'ke rang': to understand this 'ke rang' it is necessary to consider the following lines with care: (1) 'jia jati ranga ke nav; sabhna likhia vurhi kalam' (Pauri 16); (2) 'tithai bhagat vasahi ke loa' (Pauri 37); (3) 'je tisu nadari na aavai, ta vat na puchhai ke' (Pauri 7); (4) 'aape janai aape dei; aakhahi si bhi kei kei' (Pauri 25); (5) 'ete kite hori karehi; ta aakhi na sakahi kei kei' (Pauri 26); (6) 'karmi aapo aapni ke nerhai ke duri'.
