In all these lines 'ke' means 'many'; 'na ke' means 'none at all'. In Pauri 21 'kei kei' has been used; in today's Punjabi too we say 'kai kai'. As 'ke rang' means 'of many colours', so 'ke nav' means 'of many names', and 'ke loa' means 'of many realms, of many dispositions'.}
whose names are many and countless.
Their names are uncounted and endless.
Various and endless are their names.
Theirs are names of many kinds, and (anant) countless are the beings.
AKMD: Karmi karmi = according to the deeds the beings have done.
According to the deeds each has done, the settling (at Akal Purakh's door) takes place
By their deeds and their actions, they shall be judged.
They are judged according to their deeds and actions.
(Karmi karmi) according to each one's own deeds, the reckoning of the several beings takes place.
Q66G: (in which there is no error, because the doer of justice) Akal Purakh Himself is true, and His court too is true.
God Himself is True, and True is His Court.
The Lord Himself is true and true His Court.
He Himself is true, and true is His (darbaru) court.
7RB7: Tithai = in Akal Purakh's court. Sohani = they look beautiful. Parvanu = manifestly.
In that court the sant-jan look beautiful, manifestly,
There, in perfect grace and ease, sit the self-elect, the self-realized Saints.
There the accepted saints look graceful
The (panch) sants who are the accepted ones obtain glory, seated in that court.
U1LH: Nadri = the Akal Purakh who casts the glance of mercy. Karmi = through the deed, by the bestowal. Nadri karmi = by Akal Purakh's bestowal. Pavai nisanu = the mark falls, the mark is set, the sign of greatness shines out (upon the forehead).
and by the bestowal of the Akal Purakh who casts the glance of mercy, the mark of greatness shines out (upon the foreheads of those sant-jan).
They receive the Mark of Grace from the Merciful Lord.
and they come to bear the mark of the grace of the merciful Master.
Upon their foreheads is inscribed the (nisanu) writ that is the grace of Vahiguru who casts the glance of mercy.
U24Q: Kach = rawness. Pakai = ripeness. Othai = in Akal Purakh's court. Pai = it is found, it becomes known.
(Here in the world, being called great or small by anyone counts for nothing; their) rawness or ripeness becomes known only on reaching Akal Purakh's door.
The ripe and the unripe, the good and the bad, shall there be judged.
The bad and the good shall, there, be assayed.

In this world the being may be an outward hypocrite and fashion himself however he wishes; but the raw dharma is a mere show, while the ripe and firm dharma — that is, the manner of the good and evil deeds — is found (othai) in that true court, that is, is there known.
7VQN: Gaia = only by going, only by arriving. Japai jai = it is known, it is seen, news of it is had. ||34||
O Nanak! Only on going to Akal Purakh's door does the understanding come (of who is in truth ripe and who raw). ||34||
O Nanak, when you go home, you will see this. ||34||
O Nanak! on arrival at that place this shall be seen.
Sri Guru Ji says: the true and the false are (japai jai) known by going on ahead.
24CD: Dharamu = purpose, working. Aakhahu = tell, describe, understand.
This alone (which has been told above) is the working of Dharam Khand.
This is righteous living in the realm of Dharma.
This aforesaid is the moral duty of the realm of righteousness.

This alone is the manner of karam-kand, as has been told in the former lines. Or, 'dharam khand ka eho dharamu' is to say: such is the dharma of karam-kand — as the deed is done, so the fruit is made to be borne. Question: tell the manner of gyan-kand? Answer:

This alone is the purpose of the realm of righteousness (Dharam Khand). And now will be described the realm of knowledge (Gyan Khand). In this creation, there are many winds, waters, and fires; many Krishnas and Shivas. Many Brahmas are being created, who have many forms and colours. So many earths, Mount Merus, so many devotees like Dhruva through their teachings. So many Indras, moons, suns; so many universes and countries. So many Siddhas, Buddhas, Naths; so many attires of the goddesses. So many demi-gods, demons, and silent sages; so many jewels (oceans of jewels). So many sources of life, so many languages, so many kings and rulers. So many types of meditation, so many servants — Nanak, there are no limits, no bounds. ||35||
K1RK: Karam = work, working. Eho = this same, which has been told above.
Now understand (also) the working of Gyan Khand (which is in the following lines).
And now we speak of the realm of spiritual wisdom.
Now I describe the doings of the realm of knowledge.

O Siddhas! Now we tell the (karamu) manner of gyan-kand. Those who have had the realisation of the true Self, and have known Akal Purakh as complete in all, and who see the limitless power of the Creator — theirs is such a vision.
N50P: Kete = many, limitless. Vaisantar = fires. Mahes = (many) Shivs.
(In Akal Purakh's creation) there are many kinds of air, water and fires; there are many Krishans and many Shivs.
So many winds, waters and fires; so many Krishnas and Shivas.
Good many are winds, waters, fires and good many Krishanas and Shivas.
How many airs there are, and living creatures, and fires; how many Krishan avatars there are; how many Rudras there are.
4WPT: Barme = many Brahmas. Gharhati gharhiahi = they are shaped in the shaping, they are being brought forth. Ke ves = of many garbs (for the meaning of this 'ke' see the previous Pauri no. 34).
Many Brahmas are being brought forth, whose forms, colours and garbs are many.
So many Brahmas, fashioning forms of great beauty, adorned and dressed in many colors.
There are many Barhmas, who are fashioning forms, and many beauties, colours and raiments.

How many Brahmas are shaping the shaping of the world; how many are their forms, four-faced, eight-faced and the rest; how many are their colours, white, dark and the rest; how many are their garbs of clothing and the like.
FEM5: Ketia = many, limitless. Karam bhumi = the lands for the doing of deeds, the earths. Mer = Mount Meru. Dhu = Dhru bhagat. Updes = the teachings of those Dhru bhagats.
(In Akal Purakh's creation) there are limitless earths, limitless Meru mountains, limitless Dhru bhagats and their teachings.
So many worlds and lands for working out karma. So very many lessons to be learned!
Numberless are the earths and the mountains for doing virtuous deeds and numberless over numberless Dhrus, the instruction receivers.

Through the divisions of the universes, how many (karam bhumi) Bharat-lands there are; how many Sumeru mountains there are; how many Dhru bhagats there are; how many are their instructors, the rishi Narad and the rest.
Q0HU: Ind = the devas Indra. Chand = the moon. Sur = the sun. Mandal des = circles of realms.
There are limitless Indra devas, moons, limitless suns and limitless circles of realms.
So many Indras, so many moons and suns, so many worlds and lands.
Numberless are Indras, the moons the suns, numberless universes and numberless countries.
Indras too are many; moons too are many; suns too are many; mandals too are many; the lands lying within the mandals are many.
D1W9: Budh = Buddh avatar. Devi ves = the garbs of the goddesses. (Note: 'kete' is masculine and has been used with the word 'ves'. For this reason 'devi ves' is to be rendered 'the garbs of the goddesses'.)
There are limitless Siddhs, limitless Buddh avatars, limitless Naths, and limitless garbs of the goddesses.
So many Siddhas and Buddhas, so many Yogic masters. So many goddesses of various kinds.
Innumerable there are proficients, Gautamas, great yogis and innumerable over innumerable the forms of goddesses.
Siddhs, (budh) Pandits or the wise, and Naths too are (kete) many.
1Q0R: Danav = demons, daityas. Muni = the silence-keeping rishis. Ratan sumand = jewels and oceans.
(In Akal Purakh's creation) there are limitless devas and demons, limitless munis, and limitless kinds of jewels and (oceans of) jewels.
So many demi-gods and demons, so many silent sages. So many oceans of jewels.
How many deities, demons and silent sages and how many over many oceans and jewels.
How many devas there are; how many danavs there are; how many munis there are; how many oceans possessed of jewels — or how many jewels and how many oceans — there are.
2ZEN: There are limitless khanis (of the making of beings); (the beings' tongues too are not four but) there are limitless banis; there are limitless emperors and kings,
So many ways of life, so many languages. So many dynasties of rulers.
How many the mines of production, languages and many the dynasties of kings (or masters of men).
How many khanis there are, andaj and the rest; how many banis there are — para, pashyanti, madhyama, vaikhari; and how many (pat) emperors there are; and how many (narind) kings there are.
LWRF: Surti = the surats, the fastened attentions. (Note: with a little attention to this whole pauri it becomes plainly evident that 'kete' has been used with masculine words and 'ketia' with feminine words. So 'surti' is feminine, and is the plural of 'surati'.) ||34||
There are limitless kinds of meditation (which beings fasten through the mind), and limitless sevaks. O Nanak! No end can be reached at all. ||35||
So many intuitive people, so many selfless servants. O Nanak, His limit has no limit! ||35||
Countless are the men of Divine knowledge and countless the servants of God. O Nanak! there is no limit to His bounds.

How many shrutis there are; and how many are the servers of those Vedas. In this pauri all have been called countless. In the sky which is Brahm there are countless universes as the measure; from the ocean of Brahm the countless universes are waves — thus is the limitlessness to be known. Sri Guru Ji says: O Siddhas! Neither is there an end of His creation, nor can anyone know Parmeshvar's end; the sense: in the view of the learned, the creation is beyond describing. ||35||
RSBW: Mahi = in. Parchand = fierce, powerful, mighty.
In Gyan Khand (that is, in a man's state of gyan) gyan alone is mighty.
In the realm of wisdom, spiritual wisdom reigns supreme.
In the domain of knowledge Divine deliberation is greatly resplendent.

The gyan that has been told of within gyan-kand is (parchandu) possessed of splendour. The sense: for the destruction of ignorance it does not require the help of karma or of worship. Question: what is the anand of those gyanis like? Answer:

In the realm of knowledge, divine knowledge is all-powerful. There, Naad-sounds resound with many spectacles/plays. In the realm of effort (Saram Khand), the mind becomes more beautiful. In this state, the mind is molded into a very beautiful form. That state cannot be described in words — anyone who tries will later regret it. In that state of effort, one's consciousness is molded and awakened. In that state, the understanding of gods and Siddhas is formed. ||36||
K59J: Tithai = in that Gyan Khand. Nad = raga. Binod = spectacles. Kod = marvels. Anandu = relish.
In this state (as it were) the relish of all ragas, spectacles and marvels comes.
The Sound-current of the Naad vibrates there, among the sounds and the sights of bliss.
Celestial strain resounds there from whom myriads of amusements and joys proceed.
There is the anand of (nad) the shabad(1); or, for them an anand a crore times greater than the anand of nad and the (binod) sporting of the sense-objects abides at all times.

RZ2R: Saram = effort, labour. Saram khand ki = of the state of effort. Bani = fashioning. Rup = beauty.
The fashioning of the state of effort is beauty (that is, coming into this state, the mind begins day by day to become beautiful).
In the realm of humility, the Word is Beauty.
Beauty is the language of the realm of spiritual effort.

'Saram' is the name for shame. To feel shame before people, before one's lineage, before the king, before the Gurus, before the Vedas, before Dharam Rai, in the doing of evil deeds — in the shame of all these, from not doing evil deeds there came a turning by force toward good deeds. Among those doers of good deeds, those who are the (saram) shamefast — that is, the men who are in the section of worship — their speech is (rupu) beautiful, that is, clean and true and sweet. The sense is this: they do not utter inauspicious speech.
L3PT: Tithai = in this state of labour. Gharhati gharhiai = it is shaped in the shaping. Bahutu anupu = (the mind) very beautiful.
In this state, through the (new) shaping, the mind is shaped very beautifully.
Forms of incomparable beauty are fashioned there.
There, an extremely incomparable make, is made.
(Tithai) there, among the worshippers, a very incomparable shaping of the seekers' inner faculty is shaped. The sense: the inner faculty becomes pure.
C8DN: Ta kia = of that state. Kathia na jahi = they cannot be told.
The things of that state cannot be described.
The proceedings of that place can not be described.
The talk of those dwellers in Saram Khand — that is, the greatness of their words — cannot be told at all.
Z1ZK: Ko = some man. Kahai = says, describes. Pichhai = after the telling. Pachhutai = he regrets it (because he remains unable to describe it).
If some man does describe it, he regrets it afterwards (because he remains unable to describe it).
One who tries to speak of these shall regret the attempt.
If any one endeavors to describe, he shall afterwards repent.
Whoever makes the effort of telling, he afterwards regrets it, because he cannot become capable of telling the whole greatness.
4Q9F: Tithai = in that Dharam Khand. Gharhiai = it is shaped. Mani budhi = wakefulness in the mind.
In that state of labour, a man's surat and mat are shaped (that is, the surat and mat become exalted), and wakefulness is brought forth in the mind.
The intuitive consciousness, intellect and understanding of the mind are shaped there.
There inner consciousness, intellect, soul and understand are moulded afresh.

(Tithai) there the (surati) disposition of the chitt, the (mati) intoxication — that is, ahankar — the mind and the buddhi, the fourfold inner faculty, are shaped and made pure, that is, they become free of vikars.
AMXU: Sura ki sudhi = the understanding of the devas. Sidha ki sudhi = the understanding of the Siddhs. ||36||
In Saram Khand the understanding of the devas and the Siddhs is formed (within a man). ||36||
The consciousness of the spiritual warriors and the Siddhas, the beings of spiritual perfection, are shaped there. ||36||
There the genius of the pious persons and men of miracles is moulded a new.

(Tithai) there the shaping of the suras and Siddhs is shaped. The sense is this: the suras are of great rank, but they are envious; those of Saram Khand become free of envy — this very purity is the shaping that is shaped. And having obtained the siddhis, having accomplished great disciplines and practices, they became proud; but those of Saram Khand, who do the worship that is desireless bhagti of Parmeshvar, hold the siddhis utterly paltry. This is the shaping of the Siddhs' purity. ||36|| Such a one of Saram Khand, whose whole shaping has been shaped pure, has reached Karam Khand. The sense is this: he becomes a vessel of grace, and the Creator shows grace upon him.
5ULX: Karam = bestowal. Bani = fashioning. Joru = strength, power.

The fashioning of the state of bestowal is strength (that is, when Akal Purakh's glance of mercy falls upon a man, such strength is brought forth within him that the objects and vices can exert no influence upon him),
In the realm of karma, the Word is Power.
There is spiritual force in the language (of the man) of the realm of grace.

Those worshippers upon whom (karam) grace has fallen — the speech of those (khand) companies is possessed of (joru) strength. The sense: whatever blessing or curse they utter is not fruitless. Or: it is that which (joru) joins one with Parmeshvar, that is, unites.

In the realm of Grace (Karam Khand), the power/expression is different — nothing else exists there but God. There are mighty spiritual warriors, within whom the Lord (Ram) is completely permeated. There, beauty upon beauty exists within (God's) glory — their forms cannot be described. They do not die (spiritually), nor can they be deceived by Maya — within whose minds the Lord abides. There, the devotees of many realms dwell, and are in bliss forever, because God abides in their minds. In the realm of truth (Sach Khand — being one with God), the Formless Lord abides. Having created all, He watches over with a glance of grace. There, there are planets, solar systems, and universes; if one speaks of them, there is no limit or end. There, countless realms and forms are seen; as He commands, so they happen (in that state, we see this). One sees that God watches over all and is pleased. O Nanak, to describe this is as hard as steel! ||37||
BJM6: Horu = any second besides Akal Purakh. Horu na koi horu = besides Akal Purakh there is no second at all.
because in that state, within a man, there is no second at all besides Akal Purakh.
(Except those mentioned below) no one else resides in that domain.
(Tithai) there, among the worshippers, no (horu) other can (horu) turn back their strength; that is, none is greater than they.
BNJ2: Jodh = warriors. Mahabal = of great strength. Sur = heroes.
In that state (the men who are there are) warriors, mighty ones and heroes.
except the warriors of great power, the spiritual heroes.
The very powerful warriors and heroes dwell there.

Those dwelling among those worshippers who are warriors, conquerors of the body, are rathis; those who are conquerors of speech and the other senses are (mahabal) maharathis; the conquerors of the mind are (sur) atirathis.
7VNW: Tin mahi = within them. Ramu = Akal Purakh. Rahia bharpur = He is filled to the brim, He is dwelling in every pore.
In their every pore Akal Purakh is dwelling.
They are totally fulfilled, imbued with the Lord's Essence.
Within them the might of the all pervading Lord remains fully filled.

Within those worshippers Ram is complete — the sense: wherever the mind goes, there they see none but the all-pervading Hari. As in: 'brahmu disai brahmu suniai eku eku vakhaniai; aatam pasara karan hara prabh bina nahi janiai'. Question: where Ram is, Sita too ought to be? Answer:
WE5M: Sito sita = it is fully sewn, it is threaded. Mahima = (Akal Purakh's) praise, greatness. Mahi = within.
The mind of the men who have reached that (state of bestowal) stays wholly threaded in Akal Purakh's greatness alone.
Myriads of Sitas are there, cool and calm in their majestic glory.
They, who are fully sewn in the Lord's admiration, abide there.

So, with the nirgun Ram, Sita in the form of His greatness is (mahi) of a light like the moon's, and is (sito) the giver of coolness. The sense: the greatness of Bhagvant among those worshippers, that is Sita. Or: that which has (sito) sewn the disposition into the greatness — the sense, the disposition made to serve the greatness — this itself is the Sita among the worshippers there.
9LXP: Ta ke = of those men. Rup = beautiful form. Na kathne jahi = they cannot be told.
(Their bodies take on such a hue of gold that) their beautiful forms cannot be described (upon their faces nothing but radiance gleams).
The (rup) beauty of those worshippers cannot be told.
YCB7: Ohi = those men. Na marahi = they do not die the spiritual death. Na thage jahi = they cannot be deceived (Maya cannot deceive them).
(In this state) they do not die the spiritual death, and Maya cannot deceive them,
Neither death nor deception comes to those,
They, die not and nor are they hood-winked,
Those worshippers neither die, nor are they deceived by Maya the deceiver.
7V61: in whose mind Akal Purakh dwells.
within whose minds the Lord abides.
Those worshipping bhagats, in whose mind Ram dwells.
MT5G: Loa = the loks, the realms. Ke loa = of many realms. (See 'ke rang' in Pauri 34.)
In that state dwell the bhagat-jan of many realms,
The devotees of many worlds dwell there.
The saints of various worlds dwell there.
(Tithai) there (ke) certain bhagat (loa) folk alone dwell — the sense: among them the base do not dwell.
UMUK: Karahi anand = they make bliss, they stay ever in bloom. Sacha soi = that true Hari. Mani = is in (their) mind.
who stay ever in bloom, (because) that true Akal Purakh is (present) in their mind.
They celebrate; their minds are imbued with the True Lord.
They make merry, That True Lord is in their hearts.

That true Akal Purakh dwells in their mind; therefore they do the enjoying of anand. The sense is this: there no pain or affliction remains any longer. In sat-chit-anand they move about having themselves become sat-chit-anand. Question: the Nirankar whom the worshippers worship — where does He abide? Answer:
RQ4A: Sachi = in the true. Sachi khandi = in Sach Khand.
In Sach Khand (that is, in the state of becoming one with Akal Purakh) that Akal Purakh Himself dwells within the man,
In the realm of Truth, the Formless Lord abides.
In the realm of Truth abides the Formless Lord.
(Sachkhandi) in the (khand) place that holds the truth — the sense, among the worshippers — Nirankar dwells. Or: in Baikunth the true Master Nirankar Himself dwells, having taken on a sargun form.
ANCE: Kari kari = having fashioned the creation. Nadari nihal = with the glance that makes one blissful. Vekhai = He watches, He does the sustaining.
who, fashioning and fashioning the creation, does its sustaining with the glance of mercy.
Having created the creation, He watches over it. By His Glance of Grace, He bestows happiness.
God beholds the creation which He has created and renders them happy when He casts upon the beings His merciful glance.

So Nirankar, (kari kari) fashioning and fashioning His own creation, watches it — the sense: He sustains it. Or: He watches the deeds and the rest. Those upon whom He casts the (nadari) glance of grace become (nihal) blissful.
GSN9: Varbhand = the universe. Ko = some man. Kathai = should set about telling, should describe.
In that state (that is, in the state of becoming one with Akal Purakh) limitless khands, mandals and limitless universes (are seen by the man; so limitless that)
There are planets, solar systems and galaxies.
In that realm there are continents, worlds and solar systems.
In that Sach Khand which is His dwelling are the forms of the universes with their endless khands and mandals — the sense: the whole world is within His resolve alone.
VG6U: Ta ant na ant = the ends of these khands, mandals and universes cannot be reached.
if some man sets about the telling of it, no end of them can be reached.
If one speaks of them, there is no limit, no end.
if some one tries to describe them, he should know that there are no limits or bounds of them.
If anyone should tell His end, then no end comes — the sense: He is free of the limitations of place, time and thing.
MDYU: Loa loa = many loks, many realms.
In that state limitless realms and forms are seen, (in all of which)
There are worlds upon worlds of His Creation.
There are universes upon universes and creations over creations.
The forms of realm upon realm are all there, subordinate to the Nirankar.
UHV5: the work runs just as Akal Purakh's Hukam is (that is, reaching this state a man sees Akal Purakh's will operating in every place).
As He commands, so they exist.
As is the Master's mandate, so are their functions.
In whatever way Nirankar's Hukam is, in that same way the beings do their work.
2953: Vigsai = He blossoms, He is pleased. Kari vicharu = having made reflection.
(To him it is plainly seen that) Akal Purakh, having made His reflection, does the sustaining (of all beings) and is pleased.
He watches over all, and contemplating the creation, He rejoices.
The Lord beholds His creation and feels happy by contemplating over it.
Watching this play that He Himself has made, and making reflection upon the good and evil deeds, He (vigsai) is pleased.
9AJ4: Kathna = to tell, to describe. Saru = iron. Karrha saru = hard as iron is. {Note: to understand the word 'saru', the following citations are given by way of sample: (1) 'pahira agani hivai ghar badha bhojan saru karai' (1, Pauri 19, Majh Ki Var); (2) 'tun sagaro ratnagaro hau sar na jana teri ram' (Suhi Chhant M:5); (3) 'laha bhagati su saru gurmukhi paiai' (Majh Ki Var, Pauri 15); (4) 'dhanu vadbhagi nanaka, jin gurmukhi hari rasu sari' (1, Kanre Ki Var). The conclusion of these citations above is thus: (1) 'sar' is a noun, both masculine and feminine. The masculine 'saru' means 'iron' or 'essence'. The feminine 'sar' means 'awareness, news', as in citations (1) and (2). (2) 'sar' is an adjective, as in citation (3); its meaning is 'excellent'. (3) 'sari' is a verb, whose meaning is 'to take news of', 'to bring to mind', as in citation (4).} ||37||
O Nanak! To describe this state is very hard indeed (that is, this state cannot be described; it can only be experienced). ||37||
O Nanak, to describe this is as hard as steel! ||37||
O Nanak! to describe the realm of truth is hard like iron.

Sri Guru Ji says: O Siddhas! This telling of the Nirankar, the (saru) essence, which I have caused you to hear, is exceedingly (karrha) hard. The sense: as the shaping of gold is hard and it is the most excellent among the metals, in this same way reflection upon the Shabad which is the Guru's updesh is exceedingly hard and exceedingly excellent. ||37|| Question: you have said that the telling of the Shabad is hard, like the shaping of gold. For the shaping of gold there are materials; so tell the materials for the shaping of the Shabad too? Answer:
BEWM: Jatu = keeping one's bodily senses restrained from the vices. Pahara = the goldsmith's shop. Suniaru = the goldsmith.
(If) there be a shop of continence, and patience become the goldsmith,
Let self-control be the furnace, and patience the goldsmith.
Make continence your furnace, patience your goldsmith,

Let the tongue and the organ of generation be free of restlessness — such patience of the bhagats, that alone be the goldsmith; and the renouncing of all cravings and the turning back of all the senses from the sense-objects, of such continence let there be the (pahara) furnace.

Let self-control be the furnace, patience the goldsmith. Let one's intellect be the anvil, and Divine knowledge the tools/hammer. With awe of God as the bellows, disciplined spiritual practice the fire, and love of God as the melting pot, melt Amrit (the Name) in it. In such a true mint, the Guru's Shabad is made. This is the work of those whom God blesses with His glance of grace. O Nanak, God, with His glance of grace, makes them happy and blissful. ||38||
XXEE: Mati = intellect. Ved = gyan. Hathiaru = the hammer. {Note: the word 'ved' is used in Japji in the following lines: (1) 'gurmukhi nadan, gurmukhi vedan, gurmukhi rahia samai' (Pauri 5); (2) 'suniai sasat simriti ved' (Pauri 9); (3) 'asankh garanth mukhi ved path' (Pauri 17); (4) 'orhak orhak bhali thake, ved kahani ik vat' (Pauri 22); (5) 'aakhahi ved path puran' (Pauri 26); (6) 'gavani pandit parhani rakhisar, jugu jugu veda nale' (Pauri 27). Apart from the line of Pauri 5, in all the other pauris the word 'ved' is in the plural and points to the Vedas, the religious books of the Hindu faith. But in Pauri 5 'vedan' is singular and its meaning is 'gyan'. In this same way, in 'ved hathiar' the 'ved' is singular and its meaning is 'gyan'. But it is not necessary that wherever the word 'vedu' has come in the singular its meaning is 'gyan'. There are several shabads where, though 'vedu' is singular, it is the Ved, the religious book of the Hindu faith. But it is necessary to consider the context too. In this pauri the abstract nouns 'jatu', 'dhiraj', 'mati', 'bhau', 'tap tau' and 'bhau' have come; for this reason the word 'vedu' too, fitting with them (in the meaning 'gyan'), can only be an abstract noun.}
let a man's own intellect be the anvil, (and upon that anvil of intellect) let gyan (strike as) the hammer.
Let understanding be the anvil, and spiritual wisdom the tools.
understanding your anvil, Divine knowledge your tools,
And let the unmoving intellect be the anvil, upon which they place the gold and shape it; let the hearing of the Vedic utterances be the (hathiaru) hammer.
0VWK: Bhau = the fear of Akal Purakh. Khala = the skins, the bellows (with which goldsmiths blow and make the fire blaze). Tap tau = the burning with austerities, the doing of labour, the making of the earning.
(If) the fear of Akal Purakh (be) the bellows, and disciplined labour (be) the fire,
With the Fear of God as the bellows, fan the flames of tapa, the body's inner heat.
God's fear Yours bellows, practising of penance your fire,
The holding of (bhau) the fear of Akal Purakh, let this be the (khala) leather or brass tube that blows, with which they make the fire blaze. And the doing of tap, let this be the fire's heat.
9762: Bhanda = the crucible. Bhau = love. Amritu = Akal Purakh's Nam that makes one deathless. Titu = in that vessel.
and love be the crucible, then (O brother!) melt in that (crucible) Akal Purakh's amrit Nam.
In the crucible of love, melt the Nectar of the Name,
and love of Lord your pot, where-in filter the Nectar of God's Name.

Let (bhau) love be the vessel — that is, let the heart possessed of love be the crucible. (Titu) in that heart the Guru's updesh, which is amrit, is the equal of gold; melt it, the sense being: hold it in the heart.
766E: Gharhiai = it is shaped, it is fashioned. Gharhiai sabadu = the Shabad is shaped. Sachi taksal = in this true mint told of above.
(Because it is only in such) a true mint that the (Guru's) Shabad is shaped.
and mint the True Coin of the Shabad, the Word of God.
Thus in the true mint the Divine word is fashioned.
Then, in the true mint that is the sadh-sangat, the being himself is shaped into (sabadu) the form of Brahm.
C1Y3: Jin kau = upon which men. Nadari = the glance of mercy. Karamu = bestowal. Tin kar = this work is theirs alone (that is, those men prepare this mint told of above and shape the shaping of the Shabad).
This work belongs to those men upon whom the glance of mercy falls.
Such is the karma of those upon whom He has cast His Glance of Grace.
This is the daily routine of those on whom God casts His gracious glance.
Those upon whom the Satigurus' (karamu) grace and (nadari) glance rest, to those men falls the work of taking up the patience and the rest spoken of above.
K552: Nihal = pleased, joyful, in bliss. Nadri = the Lord who casts the glance of mercy. ||38||
O Nanak! Those upon whom the bestowal falls become blissful through Akal Purakh's glance of grace. ||38||
O Nanak, the Merciful Lord, by His Grace, uplifts and exalts them. ||38||
O Nanak! the Merciful Master, with his kind look, makes them happy.

Sri Guru Ji says: so, by Akal Purakh's glance of grace they become (nihal) fulfilled in their purpose — that is, they become free of the pain of birth and death, liberated. ||38|| Question: who is the world's Guru, and its mother and father? Answer:
XQLL: The life force (is for the bodies) is the Guru; water is the father; and Earth, the great mother of all. Day and night are the male and female nurses, in whose lap the whole world plays. Good deeds and bad deeds are read out in God's presence. By one's own actions, some are near Him, some are far from Him. Those who have meditated on His Name have made their efforts fruitful. O Nanak, their faces are radiant, and many others (by their company) are freed from the bonds of Maya. ||1||
62FB: Pavanu = air, breath, prana. Mahatu = great.
The prana (is for the bodies as) the Guru (is for the beings' souls). Water is the father (of all beings) and the earth is the great mother (of all).
Air is the Guru, Water is the Father, and Earth is the Great Mother of all.
Air is the Guru, water the Father, earth the great Mother,

Holding the world to be in the form of a child, they tell of its protectors: that the Guru of the whole world is the air. Of this there are two senses. First, the air is the greatest of all, because all the senses stand established upon the support of the air alone; therefore the air was called the Guru of all(1). Or: the Gurus' updesh comes about by means of the air — the sense, the shabad comes about by the air — and for this reason it was called Guru. And water is the father, because from water the bringing forth of all takes place; hence water is the world's father. And the (mahatu) great mother is the earth. As a mother keeps her son lifted up, so, like a child, she keeps the people lifted upon herself; and bringing forth grain she nourishes their bellies. Further: a mother throws her son's filth and urine upon the earth; for this reason the earth is greater than the mother of one's birth.
8TXG: Divasu = day. Dui = both. Divasu daia = the day is the male nurse. Rati dai = the night is the female nurse. Sagal = all.
Day and night are both the male and female nurses; the whole world is at play (that is, all the world's beings are absorbed, at night in sleeping and by day in their affairs).
Day and night are the two nurses, in whose lap all the world is at play.
and day and night the two female and male nurses, in whose lap the entire world plays.

It is the male nurse's part that he keeps the child at play — that is, he does the service through the day. The female nurse's part is to take the child along and put it to sleep, and, should the mother not be there, on occasion to give it milk and to fondle it. So night and day are the female and male nurses. By day the beings do endless works; by night they sleep. In this the whole child that is the world is at play. The sense is this: as the child's every movement is not hidden from the female and male nurses, in this same way the doings of the child that is the world are manifest to the presiding devas of day and night.
Q495: Vachai = he examines, he reads out (what is written). Haduri = in Akal Purakh's presence, at Akal Purakh's door.
Dharam-raj, in the presence of Akal Purakh, reflects upon the good and bad deeds (done by the beings).
Good deeds and bad deeds-the record is read out in the Presence of the Lord of Dharma.
The merits and demerits shall be read in the presence of Righteous Judge.

The (changiaia) good things which are the form of good deeds, and the buriaia which are the form of evil deeds, are (vachai) read out and recited by Chitr-Gupt in the (haduri) presence of Dharam Rai, making day and night the witnesses.
2D8J: Karmi = according to the deeds. Ke = many beings. Nerhai = near to Akal Purakh.
According to each one's own (deeds done), some beings come near Akal Purakh and some become far from Akal Purakh.
According to their own actions, some are drawn closer, and some are driven farther away.
According to their respective deeds, some shall be near and some distant from the Lord.

Whether near or far, wherever one may be, all obtain the fruit according to their own deeds. Or: some Dharam Rai seats near him and honours; some he casts out far. But by these good and evil deeds the coming and going is not ended; the wheel of birth and death keeps turning.
V9TG: Jini = which men. Te = those men. Dhiaia = have remembered. Masakati = mashaqqat, labour, the earning of discipline. Ghali = having laboured, having made it fruitful.
O Nanak! The men who have remembered Akal Purakh's Nam have made their labour fruitful.
Those who have meditated on the Naam, the Name of the Lord, and departed after having worked by the sweat of their brows
Who have pondered on His name, and have departed after putting in toil;
O Siddhas! Those who have done the meditation upon the Nam — that is, the simran — and have (ghali) performed the (masakati) labour of jap and tap and the rest, have gone.
9WAL: Mukh ujle = of radiant face. Keti = many beings. Chhuti = has been liberated, has become free of the bonds of Maya. Nali = in the company of those (Gurmukhs). ||1||
(At Akal Purakh's door) they are of radiant face, and (many more) beings, (abiding) in their company, have been freed (from the bonds of Maya, having broken down the 'wall of falsehood'). ||1||
-O Nanak, their faces are radiant in the Court of the Lord, and many are saved along with them! ||1||
O Nanak! their faces shall be bright and many shall be emancipated along with them.

Sri Guru Ji says: (te) the faces of those men have become radiant. And (keti) how much of the creation has, (nali) along with them — the sense, through their updesh — been freed from the world's bonds. The sense is this: of all the disciplines, the chief was declared to be the simran of the Nam. In the beginning too Satinam was uttered, and at the end, having spoken the conclusion together with the greatness of that Nam, Japu Ji was completed. Know this Sri Japu Ji to be the morning sandhya. ||1||
9ANB: The bani 'So Dar' of Guru Nanak Ji, in Rag Asa.
So Dar ~ That Door. Raag Aasaa, First Mehl:

From 'So Daru' Ji at the beginning down to 'Bhai prapati manukh dehuria', up to this point the people of the Guru's way recited the evening Rahiras down to the time of Sri Guru Arjan Sahib Ji. Then in the time of Sri Guru Gobind Singh, the True Emperor, the Chaupai and the rest, and other bani of the Tenth Guru, were joined to it as well. The meaning of this shabad has already been given at the 'So Daru' of 'Japu' Ji. There is a variant reading of a letter here and there. Its setting some state separately thus: that when He went beyond Dhru Lok into Baikunth Lok, then this shabad was uttered before Bhagvant. Or, when Bibi Nanaki Ji asked at Sultanpur, O brother Ji! You who went to the Sheikh Sain — what kind of house and door did you see there? Then He recited to Bibi Ji the 'So Daru' of 'Japu' Ji, and set down some variant readings from it. So here it is to be attached to a supplication made face to face. Or some mahatmas say thus, that the 'So Daru' of 'Japu' Ji was given as the answer to the Siddhs' question, and the 'So Daru' of Rahiras was given as the answer to Bibi Ji's question, and the 'So Daru' of Asa was uttered after going above Sachkhand and Dhru Lok. In truth there are only two 'So Daru': one of 'Japu' Ji and one of Rag Asa. And it is the one of Rag Asa that is written in Rahiras; there is no other third one. ||1||
GFAU: Akal Purakh is One, and He is met through the grace of the Satguru.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but one God. By the True Guru's grace He is obtained.
God is One. By the grace of the True Guru.
LH7J: Keha = of what kind? very wondrous. Daru = door. Jitu = where. Bahi = having sat. Sarab = all beings. Samale = You have taken care, You are taking care.
(O Prabhu!) That house of Yours and that door (of that house) must be very wondrous, where You sit and take care of all beings.
Where is That Door of Yours, and where is That Home, in which You sit and take care of all?
Which is Your gate and which the mansion, sitting where-in (You) takest care of all,(O Lord)!

O Bhagvant! What is that door of Yours like? And what is that house like, established in which You take news of all beings? The sense: in truth nothing at all can be said of Your house and door. But for the sake of the seekers' meditation He gives some description of His own house and door. ☬ (The satsang is of the form of the door) the house; or (the world is the door) Baikunth is the house. So now they describe the fashioning of Your worldly house and door.

Which is that door of Yours, which is that house, where You sit and take care of everything? Countless sounds/melodies are playing there, and many musicians playing instruments. Countless of Your Ragas and Raginis, countless of Your beings who sing of You. The wind, water, and fire sing of You; the righteous judge of Dharma (Yama) sings of You at Your door.
3HXF: Nad = sounds, shabad, rags. Vavanhare = the players.
(In this creation of Yours) there are countless and innumerable instruments and rags; countless beings are the players (of those instruments).
The Sound-current of the Naad vibrates there for You, and countless musicians play all sorts of instruments there for You.
Countless are Your musical instruments of various types which resound there and various are musicians there.
O You whose form is asankh, that is to say boundless! At Your door are countless instruments, nad and the rest. And at Your door are (kete) very many players of those instruments.
GBW3: Pari = the fairies of the rags, the raginis. Siu = together with. Pari siu = together with the raginis. Kahiahi = are spoken, are named.
Countless rags together with their raginis are named. Countless beings are the singers (through these rags and raginis they are singing Your praise).
There are so many Ragas and musical harmonies to You; so many minstrels sing hymns of You.
Good many are Your measures with their consorts and good many Your minstrels hymn You.
At Your door are named countless rags together with their raginis. And at Your door are very many singers of those rags and raginis. They now state those singers in brief.
J190: Gavani = they sing. Tudh no = You. Baisantaru = fire. Gavai = he sings {'gavai' is singular, 'gavani' is plural}. Raja dharamu = Dharam Raj. Duare = at (Your, O Prabhu!) door.
(O Prabhu!) Air, water and fire (and the other elements) are singing Your virtues (they move within Your will). Dharam Raj is singing (standing at Your door, the songs of Your praise).
Wind, water and fire sing of You. The Righteous Judge of Dharma sings at Your Door.
Sing You wind, water and fire; and the Righteous Justice sings (Yours) praises at (Your) door.
Air and water and again fire sing of You. And Dharam Raja too sings Your praise at Your door.
012K: Chitu guptu = an ancient Hindu conception has come down that these two persons, Chitr and Gupt, keep writing the accounts of the good and bad deeds done by all beings. Likhi janahi = {Know to write} they know how to write. Likhi likhi = (at every moment) writing and writing (whatever those Chitr and Gupt keep writing at every moment).
Those Chitr and Gupt too, who know how to write (the accounts of the good and bad deeds of beings) and whose writings Dharam Raj considers, are singing the songs of Your praise.
Chitr and Gupt, the angels of the conscious and the subconscious who keep the record of actions, and the Righteous Judge of Dharma who reads this record, sing of You.
Chitra Gupta (the recording angles), who know to write and on the basis of whose scribed writ, the Righteous Judge adjudicates, hymn You.
Those who know how to write the hidden deeds of beings, those Chitr Gupt Ji too sing Your praise. And writing and writing they consider dharam and adharam.

Chitr and Gupt, who record deeds and are judged by the king of Dharma through their writing, sing of You. Shiva, Brahma, and the goddess of beauty sing of You, who look beautiful, having been adorned by You. Indra, sitting on his throne, sings of You, with the deities at Your door. The Siddhas, absorbed in deep meditation, sing of You, and the Sadhs who contemplate You. The celibates, the charitable, and the contented sing of You, as do the mighty warriors. The Pandits and Rishis, who study the Vedas across the ages, sing of You. The enchanting heavenly beauties who entice the heart, in heaven, on earth, and the unconscious, sing of You.
NWQV: Isaru = Shiv. Devi = devis. Sohani = they look beautiful, they are resplendent. Savare = made beautiful.
(O Prabhu!) Countless devis, Shiv and Brahma (and the other devtas) who have been made beautiful by You are always resplendent (at Your door), singing of You (singing Your virtues).
Shiva, Brahma and the Goddess of Beauty, ever adorned by You, sing of You.
Shiva, Brahma, and goddess, ever beautiful as adorned by You, sing You.
(Isaru) Shivji and Brahma, together with the devis who have been (savare) made by You, sing of You and are resplendent always.
BV0B: Indrasani = {indra-asan} seated upon Indra's throne. Dari = at Your door. Devatia nale = together with the devtas.
Many Indra devtas seated upon their thrones together with the devtas are singing of You at Your door (singing the songs of Your praise).
Indra, seated on His Throne, sings of You, with the deities at Your Door.
Indra, seated in his throne, with the deities at Your gate, sings You.
Indra too, seated upon that seat which is the station of Indra, together with the devtas, sings at Your door.
0458: Samadhi andari = having fixed themselves in samadhi. Sidh = jogis accomplished in the disciplines of jog, those persons reckoned above the class of men and below the devtas; these Siddhs are held to be the very embodiment of purity and the masters of all eight siddhis. Bichare = bichari, having reflected.
(O Prabhu!) The Siddhs are singing of You, fixed in their samadhis. The sadhs are praising You, having reflected (upon Your virtues).
The Siddhas in Samaadhi sing of You; the Saadhus sing of You in contemplation.
In their meditative mood the perfect persons sing of You and the saints in their contemplation sins You as well.
O Bhagvant! Established within samadhi, the Siddhs too sing Your praise. And again the sadhs who possess discernment sing of You.

7AGV: Jati = those who hold back the desire of kam. Sati = the charitable. Vir = warriors. Karare = mighty.
Men of continence, of charity and of contentment are also singing Your virtues alone. Countless mighty warriors are proclaiming Your greatnesses alone.
The celibates, the fanatics, and the peacefully accepting sing of You; the fearless warriors sing of You.
The continents, the true and the patients sing Yours praises and the dauntless warriors, admire You.
Men of continence and speakers of truth, and again the contented, sing of You. And again the hardy warriors too sing of You.
8JZZ: Parhani = they read. Rakhisuru = {rikhi-isaru} the very great rishis, the maha-rishis. Jugu jugu = in every age. Veda nale = together with the Veds.
(O Prabhu!) The pandits and the great rishis who (read the Veds) are performing Your praise alone, together with the Veds.
The Pandits, the religious scholars who recite the Vedas, with the supreme sages of all the ages, sing of You.
The scholars, the readers of the Vedas of all the ages, together with the seven supreme sages, exalt You.
In age after age the pandits together with the Veds, and (parhani) the students who read them, and again the great rishis, sing of You.
M1J8: Mohnia = beautiful women. Manu mohani = who beguile the mind. Machhu = the mortal realm. Paiale = the nether realm.

The beautiful women who beguile the mind of man (by their beauty) are singing of You alone (that is, they are manifesting Your own beauty). The realm of heaven, the mortal realm and the nether realm (that is, all the beings of heaven, earth and the nether world) are proclaiming Your greatness alone.
The Mohinis, the enchanting heavenly beauties who entice hearts in paradise, in this world, and in the underworld of the subconscious, sing of You.
The captivating she-seraphs, who beguile the heat in paradise, this world and the nether regions sing You.
O You who beguile the mind, Parmeshvar! Or, the women who beguile the mind sing of You in heaven, and in (machh) the middle, that is the mortal realm, and in the nether world.
J64E: Upae tere = created by You. Athsathi = sixty-eight. Tirath nale = together with the tirthas.
(O Prabhu!) The jewels You have created, together with the sixty-eight tirthas, are singing of You alone.
The celestial jewels created by You, and the sixty-eight sacred shrines of pilgrimage, sing of You.
The (fourteen) invaluable objects, created by You with sixty-eight places of pilgrimage, hymn (You.)
O Bhagvan! The jewels created by You too sing of You. And the sixty-eight tirthas and the (nale) streams too sing — the sense being, the presiding deities of the rivers and streams sing.

The celestial jewels You created sing of You, as do the 68 places of pilgrimage. The mighty warriors and spiritual heroes sing of You, as do the creatures of all four sources (all beings). The planets and all the cosmos sing of You, which You created and established/supported. Only those who please You sing of You — Your devotees are intoxicated with the bliss of Your love. How many others sing of You, that I cannot even contemplate — what can the humble Nanak reflect on? He is God, always will be, eternal, forever true.
WSFG: Jodh = warriors. Mahabal = of great strength. Sura = heroes. Khani chare = the four khanis {andaj, jeraj, setaj, utbhuj}. Khani = a mine, which is dug so that metals or jewels and the like may be taken from within it {khan = to dig}. An ancient conception has come down that all the beings of the world are born from four khanis: the egg, the womb, sweat, and springing up of itself from the earth with the help of water (here the sense is: the beings of all four khanis, the whole creation).
The warriors and heroes of great strength are praising Your (might) alone (by displaying the strength You gave them). The beings of all four khanis are singing of You.
The brave and mighty warriors sing of You. The spiritual heroes and the four sources of creation sing of You.
The supremely mighty warriors and Divine heroes sing You and the four sources of creation magnify You.
The mighty heroes sing of You. And again the beings of the four khanis, the egg-born and the rest, sing of You.
AEML: Khand = a portion, a portion of the universe, each earth. Mandal = a circle, one circle of the universe in which one sun, one moon and an earth and the like are reckoned. Brahmand = the whole creation. Kari kari = having made. Dhare = set in place.
The whole creation, all the khands and mandals of the creation, which You have made and set in place, are singing of You alone.
The worlds, solar systems and galaxies, created and arranged by Your Hand, sing of You.
The continents the worlds and solar, system, created Yours glories.
The nine khands and the (mandal) islands and the brahmand — the sense being, the beings who dwell within them — sing of You, whom You have (kari kari) fashioned and fashioned and held in place.
S13U: Sei = those men alone. Tudhu bhavani = they seem good to You. Rate = dyed, engrossed in love. Rasale = {ras-alay} houses of relish, devoted ones.
(O Prabhu!) In truth only those men perform Your praise (that is, the praise they perform is fruitful) who are dyed in Your love and are Your devoted bhagats; those men alone seem dear to You.
They alone sing of You, who are pleasing to Your Will. Your devotees are imbued with Your Sublime Essence.
They also eulogise You, who are Your saints and are pleasing to You and are steeped (in Name) and your bliss impairing love.
Those who seem good to You, they alone sing of You. (Rasale) the house of love, or all the bhagats there are, they are dyed in You.
3407: Hori kete = countless other beings {the word 'hori' is the plural of 'hor'}. Mai chiti = in my mind. Mai chiti na avani = they do not come into my mind, I cannot number them, they are beyond my reflecting. Kia bichare = what reflection can he make?
Countless other beings are proclaiming Your greatness, whom I cannot number. (Indeed, about this numbering) what reflection can Nanak make? (Nanak is not capable of making this reflection.)
So many others sing of You, they do not come to mind. O Nanak, how can I think of them all?
Many others whom I cannot recollect within my mind, sing You. How can Nanak think of them.

Countless others too — the sense being, very many — sing of You. All these do not come within my contemplation. Sri Guru Ji says, (what reflection can I make of them?) — the sense being, they are past counting. Bibi Ji said, O brother, when was Parmeshvar, and of what kind is He? ☬ Upon that He spoke thus:
3MUK: Sachu = abiding. Nai = greatness {the Arabic word sana. This Arabic word has two forms in Panjabi: asnai, nai. 'Jo kichhu hoia sabhu kichhu tujh te, teri sabh asnai'} In the same way from Sanskrit words: sthan = asthan, than; snan = asnan, nhan; stambh = asthambh, thambh; sneh = asneh, neh; sthir = asthir, thir; sthal = asthal, tal, {see 'Gurbani Viakaran'}. {Note: the word 'sacha' is masculine and is the adjective of 'sahib'. The word 'sachi' is feminine and is the adjective of the word 'nai'. In reading this line the pauses are to be attended to.}
That Master-Prabhu is ever-abiding. His greatness is ever-abiding.
That True Lord is True, forever True, and True is His Name.
That and that Lord is ever True. He is True, and True is His Name.
The ever-true Master was in the past tense, and that same True One, possessed of true (nai) greatness, is now.
DG4Z: Hosi = will be, will abide. Jai na = is not born. Na jasi = nor will He die. Jini = by which (Prabhu). Rachai = has created.
That (Prabhu) who created this creation is present at this moment too, and is ever-abiding.
He is, and shall always be. He shall not depart, even when this Universe which He has created departs.
He, who created the creation is and shall also be. He shall not depart when the creation shall depart (disappear).
(Bhi) And again that same True One will always (hosi) be in the future, will exist. And the creation (jai) will pass away. And He who created it, (na jasi) He will not pass away.
52A7: Rangi rangi = of colours and colours, of many colours. Bhati = of many kinds. Jinsi = of many sorts. Jini = by which (Prabhu). Upai = has created.
That Prabhu who has fashioned Maya of many colours, kinds and sorts.
He created the world, with its various colors, species of beings, and the variety of Maya.
(God), who fashioned the world, has by divers contrivances created the creation of various colors and kinds.
He who has created, by way of Maya of countless colours and of every fashion, the sorts — the sense being, by the distinctions of beast and bird and the rest.
F8PK: Kari kari = having created. Dekhai = He takes care. Kita apana = His own created world. Jiu = as. Vadiai = will.
He, as is His will, having created the world, is also taking care of what He has created.
Having created the creation, He watches over it Himself, by His Greatness.
Having created the creation, He, as it pleases His Honour, beholds His handiwork.
Having fashioned and fashioned that expanse which is His own making, just as His (vadiai) desire is, so He watches over it — the sense being, He sustains it.
RMED: Tisu bhavai = seems good to Him. Karsi = He will do. Na karana jai = cannot be done.
Whatever seems good to that (Prabhu), that alone He does. No being can show defiance before Him (no being can say to Him, 'not thus, do it thus').
He does whatever He pleases. No one can issue any order to Him.
Whatever pleases Him He does that. (To Him) then no one can issue an order.
Whatever seems good to that Parmeshvar, that alone comes about in all three times. And again, no command can be laid upon Him by anyone.
K69L: Saha pati sahibu = the emperor and master of kings. Rahanu = to abide (befits). Rajai = within the will ||1||
That Prabhu is the emperor (of the whole world), the emperor of emperors too. O Nanak! It befits (beings) to abide within His will alone. ||1||
He is the King, the King of kings, the Supreme Lord and Master of kings. Nanak remains subject to His Will. ||1||
He is the king the Emperor of the kings Nanak remains subjects to (His) will.

He is the emperor of kings and emperors. Sri Guru Ji says, it is fitting to abide within the (rajai) command of that Parmeshvar. ||1|| ☬ At one time Baba Kalu Ji said, 'Son, that Master whose bhajan you perform — how great is He?' Then Sri Guru Ji, making supplication before Hari, gives the answer to His father:
G9XC: Hearing of Your greatness, everyone calls You great. Just how great You are is only known by seeing You. No price/value can be put on Him, He cannot be described. Those who speak of You remain absorbed in You. ||1|| O my great Master — You are like a deep ocean, great-hearted, of infinite virtue. No one knows how great Your expanse is. ||1||Pause||
6K1B: Suni = having heard. Sabhu koi = every being.
Every being says merely from hearsay (from others) that (O Prabhu!) You are great.
Hearing of His Greatness, everyone calls Him Great.
By hearing every one calls You great (O Lord!),
Hearing and hearing from the shastras, everyone says that He is great.
JP9V: Kevadu = how great. Ditha = only upon being seen. Hoi = can be (told), can be said.
But how great You are (how boundless You are?) — this can only be told upon having Your darshan (only upon seeing You can it be said that You are utterly boundless).
But just how Great His Greatness is-this is known only to those who have seen Him.
But One, who has seen You Knows, how great You are.
(Kevadu) How great is He? When someone has seen Him, then let him say that He is this great.
H5HB: Kimati = worth, a thing equal to it. Kimati pai na = the worth cannot be assessed, no being equal to Him can be named.
No other equal to You can be named; Your form cannot be described.
His Value cannot be estimated; He cannot be described.
Therefore neither is Your worth found, nor is Your limit spoken.
SVR1: Those who speak Your greatness (forgetting themselves) become absorbed within You alone. ||1||
Those who describe You, Lord, remain immersed and absorbed in You. ||1||
Yours describers remain absorbed in You.

Or, those sants who have found Your (kimati) measure — the sense being, who have known You as of the form of sat, chit and anand — to them You are reachable by direct experience. By the tongue You cannot be spoken of as a this. Those speakers who are Your sants, they have become undivided within You alone.
WL9H: Gahir = O deep One! Gambhira = O One of great heart! Guni gahira = O One deep by reason of virtues! O master of boundless virtues!
O my great Master! You are (as it were) a deep (ocean). You are of great heart, You are of boundless virtues.
O my Great Lord and Master of Unfathomable Depth, You are the Ocean of Excellence.
O My great Master of unfathomable depth, (You are) an ocean of excellences.
O my great Master! (Gahir gambhir) Deep, and an unfathomable ocean of virtues!
AX53: No being at all knows how great Your extent is. ||1|| Rahau ||
No one knows the extent or the vastness of Your Expanse. ||1||Pause||
None knows, how much and how great, Your expanse is. Pause.

No one can know this matter, of how much Your (chira) limit or register is. ||1|| Rahau. They speak of Rahau as the refrain, that is to say the pause; and some also give this meaning, that Rahau is the settling of the mind.
WC54: Sabhi mili = all together, all taking one another's help. Surti = surat. Surti surat kamai = surat kamai, surat kamai, again and again they fixed themselves in samadhi.
(To find out how great You are) many great and renowned jogis who fix themselves in samadhi made efforts to fix their attention, made efforts again and again.
All the intuitives met and practiced intuitive meditation.
All the contemplatives have met and practised contemplation.
All the (surti) shrutis of the Veds, or the pandit folk, joined together and earned their own (surati) attention — the sense being, applied it.

The meditators got together and meditated, trying to find You. The appraisers got together, tried to evaluate You. The wise ones and deep meditators (the great ones) — could not even describe a sesame-seed's worth of Your glory. ||2|| All truth, all austerities, all good deeds; all the Siddhas' powers were from Your greatness. Without You, none could attain that perfection. If You bless someone with Your grace, nothing can block them from receiving it. ||3||
TXLX: Sabh... pai = sabh mili kimati pai, kimati pai.
Great and renowned men of discernment (versed in the shastras), taking one another's help, tried to find some being equal to You,
All the appraisers met and made the appraisal.
All the appraisers, having met together, have appraises (Your) worth.
All the (kimati) jewellers — the sense being, the men of discernment — joined together and found Your worth; the sense being, they too pronounced You boundless.
YVTH: Giani = men of discernment, of high understanding. Dhiani = those who fix their attention. Gur = great. Gur hai = gur bhai, brothers of the great, some other such great ones. Gur gurhai = many great and renowned ones {these words 'gur gurhai' are the adjective of the words 'giani dhiani'}.
(the men of discernment and the men of meditation, many great and renowned ones)
The spiritual teachers, the teachers of meditation, and the teachers of teachers
The theologians, the visualisers and they, who are the preachers of preachers, (have described You.)
Giani, versed in the shastras; dhiani, those of pranayam; (gur gurhai) the gurus even of the gurus.
M65L: but they could not tell even a tila's worth of Your greatness. ||2||
-they cannot describe even an iota of Your Greatness. ||2||
They cannot tell even an iota of Your greatness.
The sense being, the greatest of the great — by these too not even a tila's measure of Your greatness can be told. ||2||
F7WM: Sabhi sat = all good deeds. Tap = hardship, austerities. Changiaia = good qualities.
(What of the men of discernment and what of the Siddh jogis? None at all could estimate Your greatness; but the men of discernment's) every good deed, every tap and every virtue,
All Truth, all austere discipline, all goodness,
All truths, all austerities all goodness
Every kind of virtue, such as being a speaker of truth, and every kind of tap, and all the (changiaia) good qualities there are —
M6TF: Sidh = the accomplished, men who have succeeded in life.
the great works (the riddhis and siddhis and the rest) of the Siddh folk —
all the great miraculous spiritual powers of the Siddhas
and the magnificences of the men of occult powers,
and the greatnesses in the form of the siddhis of the Siddh persons —
T68Y: this success has been obtained by no one at all without Your help.
without You, no one has attained such powers.
without You none has ever attained such power.
without Your grace, those siddhis of the aforesaid virtues have been obtained by no one.
0UHE: Karami = by (Your) mercy, by way of Your bounty. Thaki = having stopped, having blocked ||3||
(Whoever has obtained siddhi) has obtained it by Your mercy, and no other could put an obstacle in the way of that attainment. ||3||
They are received only by Your Grace. No one can block them or stop their flow. ||3||
With Your grace they are procured No one can obstruct and stop (their flow).
He to whom it comes by Your grace, from him no one's blocking can block it; or, without grace it remains blocked. ||3||
36YB: What standing has the being that he could describe these virtues?
What can the poor helpless creatures do?
What can the helpless creatures do?
If anyone should say, O Akal Purakh! I shall tell all Your glory — then what is the poor speaker, what a trifling being is he, that he could tell it?

What capacity does a mere speaker have to describe You? Your treasures are overflowing with Your praises. To whom You give (this gift), no one else has the power to grant it. O Nanak, the True Lord is the One who adorns/perfects all. ||4||2||
Q5BK: (O Prabhu!) The treasuries of Your virtues are (as it were) brimming full.
Your Praises are overflowing with Your Treasures.
Yours treasure are brimful with Your praises,
Because, O Akal Purakh! Your (bhandara) treasuries of (siphati) praises — the sense being, the hearts of the sants, or the Ved and Shastras — are brimming full.
3N6N: He to whom You grant the gift of performing Your praise — no one's strength can avail to put an obstacle in his way,
Those, to whom You give-how can they think of any other?
Why should he, whom. You givest, think of some other means?
He to whom You give the understanding to perform Your praise — against him what (chara) strength has anyone? That is to say, none.
R8CU: (because) O Nanak! (Say — O Prabhu!) You, the ever-abiding Prabhu, are Yourself the one who sets that (fortunate one) right. ||4||2||
O Nanak, the True One embellishes and exalts. ||4||2||
O Nanak! the True one Himself is the decorator.

Sri Guru Ji says: O You of the form of truth! You alone are the (savaran) maker of all. The sense being this, that whatever You wish, that alone You do, and that alone comes about. ||4||2|| ☬ Mata Tripta Ji said, O son! Perform the bhajan at some one time; why do you keep repeating the Nam at every moment? Upon that He uttered the shabad:
5ZH5: Speaking of God, I live; forgetting Him, I die (spiritually). It is hard to speak/focus on the True Name, yet I try. When one feels hunger for the True Name, that hunger consumes/removes deeper pain. ||1|| How can I forget Him, my mother! The True Lord dwells in the True Name — the more one meditates, the more it settles in the mind. ||1||Pause||
W829: Akha = akhan, (when) I utter (the Hari-Nam). Jiva = jivan, I come to life, spiritual life arises within me. Mari jau = mari jaun, I die, (because of the vices) my spiritual life comes to an end, my spiritual death takes place.
(As) I remember (Parmatma's) Nam, so spiritual life arises within me. (But when Prabhu's Nam) is forgotten by me, my spiritual death takes place.
Chanting it, I live; forgetting it, I die.
By repeating your Name, I live, by forgetting it I die.
O Mother Ji! So long as I (akha) speak — that is, repeat the Nam of Hari — just so long do I live. When the Nam is forgotten by me, then I die, that is to say I become miserable.
J2BJ: (Even knowing this) to remember the Nam of the ever-abiding Parmatma (seems a) hard (task).
It is so difficult to chant the True Name.
Difficult to utter is the True Name.
But this speaking of the True Nam is very hard. All cannot speak it — the sense being this, that when great merits earned in former births come to fruition, then love for the Nam arises.
15PS: (In that man within whom) the longing to remember the ever-abiding Prabhu's Nam arises,
If someone feels hunger for the True Name,
If man feels hunger for the True Name,
If the hunger for the True Nam should arise — the sense being, if the desire should be there —
S8J4: Utu = {instrumental of the word 'us'. From 'jis', 'jitu'}. Utu bhukhai = because of that hunger. Khai = having eaten (the food of the Nam). Chaliahi = are removed ||1||
by the grace of that longing, having eaten (the food of the Hari-Nam), all his sorrows are removed. ||1||
that hunger shall consume his pain. ||1||
that hunger shall consume his pains.

then, that hunger being present, having eaten up the sorrows — that is, having brought them to nothing — one departs to the next world. Or, when one eats the Nam which is the food of that hunger — the sense being, repeats it — then the sorrows depart. ||1||
2SET: Mai = O mother! Kiu visarai = may never be forgotten.
O my mother! (Make supplication that) that Parmatma may never be forgotten by me.
How can I forget Him, O my mother?
How can He be forgotten O my Mother?
O Mother Ji! Why should that Nam be forgotten by me — the sense being, it is not forgotten.
9T2G: Sachai nai = by way of the ever-abiding Hari-Nam, as we remember the ever-abiding Hari-Nam. Nai = by way of the Nam ||1|| Rahau ||
As we remember the Nam of that ever-abiding Prabhu, so that ever-abiding Master (comes to dwell within the mind). ||1|| Rahau ||
True is the Master, True is His Name. ||1||Pause||
True is the Lord and true His Name, O my Mother? Pause.
He is the True Master, and His Nams too are true. ||1|| Rahau ||
ZMHE: Even a tila's worth of the greatness of the ever-abiding Prabhu's Nam...
Trying to describe even an iota of the Greatness of the True Name,
Recounting the greatness of the True name,
Even a (tilu) little of the (vadiai) glory of the Sati Nam —

Even trying to describe the smallest bit of the True Name's greatness, people grow weary and still cannot capture its worth. Even if all got together to describe Him, He grows no greater, no less. ||2|| He does not die, nor is there grief for Him. He keeps giving, and we keep consuming, without end. This is His virtue: there is none like Him — no one has been, no one will be. ||3|| As great as You are, so great is Your gift; You who made the day, also made the night. Those who forget the Master are lowly. O Nanak, without the Name, one is lowly. ||4||3||
3PAD: (All beings) have wearied of describing (they cannot describe it). No one at all has been able to tell what being is equal to Parmatma.
people have grown weary, but they have not been able to evaluate it.
Men have grown weary but they have not been able to appraise even a jot of it.

Having spoken it, Shesh, Sarda, Vyas and the rest have wearied. But His worth — the sense being, His this-ness — was not found. (Having spoken the greatness of the Nam, now they speak the greatness of the Named.)
TM30: Sabhi = all beings. Apani pahi = should make the effort to speak {'akhani pai' is singular: 'je ko khaiku akhani pai'}.
If all the beings (of the world) should join together and make the effort to describe (Prabhu's greatness),
Even if everyone were to gather together and speak of Him,
If all men meet and glorify You,
If all the people of the world should join together and begin to perform the praise of the Named,
6VZM: then that Prabhu does not become greater (than His own reality); (and if none at all should praise Him), He does not become less (than before). (He has no craving for His own repute.) ||2||
He would not become any greater or any lesser. ||2||
You would neither grow greater nor lesser.
then by their praising He does not become great, and by slander He does not diminish. The sense being, hearing slander He does not become troubled in mind as these beings do. ||2||
D3SF: That Prabhu never dies, nor is there mourning (on His account).
That Lord does not die; there is no reason to mourn.
That Lord dies not, nor there is any mourning.
O Mother Ji! That True Master never dies. Because of this His bhagats never have the grief of separation from Him.
JCB0: Deda = giving. Na chukai = does not run out. Bhogu = the using.
He goes on giving (sustenance to beings) always; the use of the gifts He has given never runs out (His gifts never run out by being used).
He continues to give, and His Provisions never run short.
He continues to give; His provisions never run short.
That Parmeshvar keeps giving the world such food and drink as never (chukai) fails; He gives it to all having remembered them.
KSKR: Gunu eho = this very excellence. Ko = any (other).
His great excellence is this, that no other is like Him.
This Virtue is His alone; there is no other like Him.
This alone is His merit that none else is like Him.
Such an excellence as Parmeshvar's is in no other at all.
DEKT: Hoa = has come to be. Na hoi = nor will be ||3||
(None like Him has) come to be until now, nor will any ever be. ||3||
There never has been, and there never will be. ||3||
There has been none, nor there shall be any.
Because of this, none like Parmeshvar has been before, and none will be hereafter. ||3||
KAQZ: Jevadu = as great. Tevad = so great.
(O Prabhu!) As boundless as You are Yourself, so boundless is Your bounty.
As Great as You Yourself are, O Lord, so Great are Your Gifts.
As great as You are, O; Lord! so, great are Yours gift.
O Parmesar! As great as You Yourself are, so great is Your (dati) bounty.

CSBR: Jini = by which (You). Kari kai = having created.
(You are such) as has made the day and made the night.
The One who created the day also created the night.
(Yours is the personality) who makest the say and the night (too).

Of what kind are You! That having first made the day, You then made the night. That is to say, had there been no night, beings would have died in their toil alone. From this, the making of the night too is Parmeshvar's bounty.
PH3Z: Visarahi = they forget. Te = those (men) {plural}. Kamjati = of low birth.
Those who forget (such) a Master-Prabhu become men of low life.
Those who forget their Lord and Master are vile and despicable.
Vile are they who forget their Master.
O Parmeshvar! Those who forget such a (khasam) Master of Yours — that is, who let Him slip from mind — they are (kamjati), that is to say low.
ZTUC: Navai bajhu = without the Hari-Nam. Sanati = low ||4||
O Nanak! Those beings who have strayed from the Nam are the low ones. ||4||3||
O Nanak, without the Name, they are wretched outcasts. ||4||3||
O Nanak! without God's Name, men are out caste wretches.

Sri Guru Ji says: without the Nam they are (sanati) like ghosts. ||4||3|| ☬ Sri Guru Amar Das Ji, after the marriage of Bibi Bhani Ji, said to Guru Ramdas Ji, O Jetha Ji! It is the custom of our family that whatever the son-in-law asks of his own wish, that is given. Therefore you too ask something; being pleased with you, we shall give it. Then Sri Guru Ramdas Ji spoke this shabad:
LMBS: O servant of the Lord, the True Guru, the all-pervading God — I offer a humble prayer to the Guru. I, a mere worm/insect, have come for the True Guru's sanctuary; have mercy, and illuminate me with the Name. ||1|| O my friend, the divine Guru — enlighten me with the Lord's Name. The Name, received through the Guru's wisdom, is the true companion of my life; the Lord's praise is my life's provision/support. ||1||Pause||
2TNR: Hari ke jan = O servant of Hari! Satiguru = O Satigur! Sat purakha = O Mahapurakh Guru! Binau = {vinaya} supplication. Karau = karaun, I make. Gur pasi = O Guru! before You.

O Mahapurakh Guru! O Satiguru, bhagat of Prabhu! I, O Guru, make supplication before You. O Satiguru! I, the humble one, have come to Your shelter. Showing mercy, produce (within me) the light of Prabhu's Nam. ||1||
O humble servant of the Lord, O True Guru, O True Primal Being: I offer my humble prayer to You, O Guru.
O my Great Sat Guru, the accepted one of the Lord and the True Person, I make a supplication before You.
O Satiguru, Sat Purakh! (Gur) worshipful bhagat of Hari, this alone is my supplication before You.
NRC0: Satigur sarnai = O Guru! Your shelter. Kire kiram = humble, lowly beings. Pargasi = make manifest, make light.
O Satiguru! I, the humble one, have come to Your shelter. Showing mercy, produce (within me) the light of Prabhu's Nam. ||1||
I am a mere insect, a worm. O True Guru, I seek Your Sanctuary. Please be merciful, and bless me with the Light of the Naam, the Name of the Lord. ||1||
I, an insect and a worm, have sought Your shelter, mercifully bestow on me the light of God's Name, O True Guru!

We are (kire kiram) the smallest of the small beings. O Satiguru! We have come into Your shelter; showing mercy, make the light of the Nam within my antahkaran. ||1|| ☬ If you should ask, of which Nam shall He make the light? Upon that they say:
6C6N: Mo kau = to me, within me. Mit = O friend!
O my friend Guru! Grant me the light of Prabhu's Nam.
O my Best Friend, O Divine Guru, please enlighten me with the Name of the Lord.
O My friend, the bright Guru! Illumine me with the Name of the Omnipresent Lord.
O my friend Gurdev Ji! If You have been merciful to me, then make the light of the Ram Nam within my antahkaran.
V7G9: Gurmati = (obtained) by way of the Guru's teaching. Pran sakhai = companion of the life. Kirati = repute, praise. Rahrasi = the capital of the road, the provision for the journey of life ||1|| Rahau ||
May the Hari-Nam obtained by way of the Guru's teaching (remain) the companion of my life; may Prabhu's praise remain the capital for the journey of my life. ||1|| Rahau ||
Through the Guru's Teachings, the Naam is my breath of life. The Kirtan of the Lord's Praise is my life's occupation. ||1||Pause||
The Name revealed to me by Guru's instruction is the friend of my very life and God's praise is my life's vocation. Pause.

O Guru! The Nam repeated by Your (gurmati) instruction will be the (sakhai) companion of my pranas. Hearing this much, Sri Guru Amar Das Ji said, O beloved! Take the gift of the Nam, and ask also for that dealing which is the family custom. Upon that he says, O ocean of mercy! This alone is our (rahrasi) custom, or supplication, that of the Gurus the praise of Hari alone is to be asked; therefore give this very updesh. ||1||
QEHF: Those servants of Prabhu have very high fortune within whom there is faith in Prabhu's Nam, a longing for it.
The servants of the Lord have the greatest good fortune; they have faith in the Lord, and a longing for the Lord.
The greatest good fortune is of the people of God who have faith in the Lord Master and thirst for God.
O Guru Ji! I know only by Your grace: those who have faith in the Hari-Nam and the thirst to repeat Hari — those servants of Hari have the greatest of fortunes.

The Lord's servants who have deep faith and thirst for Him are truly fortunate. Getting the Lord's Name, they are satisfied; meeting the Sangat, their virtues are awakened. ||2|| Those who have not tasted the Name's essence are unfortunate, in the grip of spiritual death. Those who don't seek the True Guru's shelter and Sangat — cursed is their life and their hopes for life. ||3|| Those blessed to meet the True Guru's Sangat had it written on their forehead from the very start. Blessed, blessed is the Sat Sangat where the Lord's essence is obtained — meeting the Lord's humble servants, O Nanak, the Name is illuminated within. ||4||4||
TZFJ: Triptasahi = they are satisfied. Mili = having joined ||2||
When they obtain the Nam of Parmatma they are satisfied (from the craving of Maya); joining in the sadh sangat, (good) qualities arise (within them). ||2||
Obtaining the Name of the Lord, Har, Har, they are satisfied; joining the Sangat, the Blessed Congregation, their virtues shine forth. ||2||
By obtaining the Name of the Lord God they are satiated and by meeting the society of saints their virtues shine forth.
Because on obtaining the Hari Hari Nam they hold themselves satisfied, and joining in the sadh sangat the light of Hari's qualities arises. ||2||
J5YR: But those men to whom the relish of Parmatma's Nam has not come, who have not obtained Prabhu's Nam, are ill-fortuned; they are under the sway of the jams (understand that spiritual death rides upon their heads always).
Those who have not obtained the Sublime Essence of the Name of the Lord, Har, Har, Har, are most unfortunate; they are led away by the Messenger of Death.
They who have not gained God, God's elixir and God's Name are unfortunate and are near (handed over to) the minister of death.
Those who have not obtained the relish of the Hari Hari Nam of Hari — those ill-fortuned ones go to the city of Sanjamani, near the Jam. Or, they fall into the Jam's noose.
3B06: Dhrigu jive = a curse upon their living ||3||
Those men who do not come into the Guru's shelter, who do not sit in the sadh sangat — a curse upon their living; their living is worthy of reproach. ||3||
Those who have not sought the Sanctuary of the True Guru and the Sangat, the Holy Congregation-cursed are their lives, and cursed are their hopes of life. ||3||
Fie on the life and accursed the hope of living of those who have not sought the society and protection of the Sat Guru.

Those who have not come into the sadh sangat by way of the Satigurus' shelter — upon the living of those manmukhs too is reproach. And upon the hope of living that lies ahead for them, upon that too is reproach. ||3||
4174: Dhuri = from the very beginning, from Parmatma. Mastaki = upon the forehead. Likhasi = writ {the words 'jivasi' and 'likhasi' are altered from the words 'jive' and 'lekh' in order to complete the rhyme}.
Those servants of Prabhu who have been granted a seat in the Guru's sangat — (understand that) a good writ has been inscribed upon their forehead from the very beginning.
Those humble servants of the Lord who have attained the Company of the True Guru, have such pre-ordained destiny inscribed on their foreheads.
