The men of God, who have obtained the society of the True Guru, they have, on their fore-heads the pro-ordained writ.
Those hari jan, the gurmukhs, who have obtained the sangat of the Satiguru — upon their forehead is inscribed from the very beginning the (likhasi) writ of a record of grace.
H5GP: Jitu = in which, by way of which. Mili jan = having met the servants, having met Prabhu's servants ||4||

O Nanak! Blessed is the satsang! Blessed is the satsang! In which (being seated) the bliss of Prabhu's Nam is had, where on meeting the gurmukhs the Nam (of Parmatma) comes to dwell (within the heart). ||4||4||
Blessed, blessed is the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation, where the Lord's Essence is obtained. Meeting with His humble servant, O Nanak, the Light of the Naam shines forth. ||4||4||
Blest, blest is the saints congregation from where God's elixir is procured. By meeting God's own, O Nanak! manifest becomes Lord's Name.

Sri Guru Ji says: O Guru Ji! Such a satsangat of Yours as this is blessed and blessed. By which the hari-ras has been obtained, and to the servants the light of the Nam comes about. Therefore, O Lord, give me the Nam alone. ||4||4|| ☬ When Sri Guru Arjan Sahib Ji was seated upon the gaddi, at one time there came a shortage in the expenditure of the langar, because the wealth that came in was being taken in hand by Prithi Chand Ji. At that time Bhai Gurdas Ji came. Seeing the shortage of the langar, he made some effort himself and urged the Guru Maharaj Ji also to make effort. Then the Guru Ji, under the pretext of addressing the mind, gives the updesh and says:
9P2F: Why, mind, do you always worry and plan for yourself, when the Lord Himself is already engaged in that task for you? He who created beings within rocks and boulders already arranged their sustenance there. ||1|| O my dear Lord — those who meet the Sat Sangat are carried across. By the Guru's grace, one attains the highest state — like dry wood turning green again. ||1||Pause||
5PF1: Kahe = why? Chitavahi = you think. Chitavahi udamu = you brood upon effort, you fret {* Note: the difference between 'brooding upon effort' and 'making effort' is worth remembering. To make effort to earn a living is the duty of every man. The Guru Sahib has forbidden the wrong road of going on in anxiety and dread}. Ja ahari = in which business. Paria = is engaged.
O mind! That business in which Parmatma Himself is engaged (for your sake) — why do you keep worrying and fretting (always) about it?
Why, O mind, do you plot and plan, when the Dear Lord Himself provides for your care?
Why doest you, O Mind! think of enterprises, when Revered God Himself is engaged in your care?
O mind! Why do you brood upon effort, when Hari Ji Himself is fallen into the (ahari) effort — that is, the care — of all?
ZH72: Sail = rock. Ta ka = their. Agai = beforehand ||1||
Those beings whom Prabhu has created within rocks and stones — their sustenance too He has prepared beforehand (before creating them). ||1||
From rocks and stones He created living beings; He places their nourishment before them. ||1||
In the rocks and stones He has created beings. Their sustenance He puts before them.
Upon that, an illustration: within (sail) dry stone, or (sail) the stones of the mountains, whatever beings He has created — their food Hari has made ready beforehand. ||1||
C143: Madhau ji = O Prabhu Ji! O Husband of Maya! {madhau = ma-dhav. Ma = Maya. Dhav = husband}.
O my Prabhu Ji! Those men who sit together in the sadh sangat are saved (from useless anxieties and frets).
O my Dear Lord of souls, one who joins the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation, is saved.
O My venerable Lord of mammon! He, who mixes with the society of saints, is saved.
O my mind! That satsangat which is of Madhav Ji — whoever has joined it, he has crossed the ocean of the world.
WQNK: Parsadi = by grace. Param padu = the highest spiritual rank. Kasat = wood, timber ||1|| Rahau ||
That man to whom by the Guru's grace this high spiritual state (of poise) is given becomes, as it were, dry wood turned green. ||1|| Rahau ||
By Guru's Grace, the supreme status is obtained, and the dry wood blossoms forth again in lush greenery. ||1||Pause||
By the grace of the Guru, (he) obtains the supreme state (as) the dry wood blooms forth. Pause.

In what manner has he crossed? So they say: by the grace of the Gurus the param pad, moksh, has been obtained. Of what kind is that satsang? That it has made green a heart that was empty like dry wood. ||1|| Rahau ||
7L0M: Janani = mother. Sut = son. Banita = wife. Dharia = support. Kis ki = of anyone.
(O mind!) Mother, father, son, people, wife — none at all is the support of any other.
Mothers, fathers, friends, children and spouses-no one is the support of anyone else.
Of mother, father, people, son, (and) wife no one is the support of another.
Mother, father, son, wife and all related people — none at all is the (dhari) prop of any other from any side.

Mother, father, friends, children, spouse — none is the ultimate support of another. To every person, the Master delivers sustenance — why does the mind grow so afraid? ||2|| Birds fly hundreds of miles, leaving their young behind — who feeds them, who teaches them to peck at food? He remembers them in His mind. ||3|| All treasures and the eighteen powers of the Siddhas rest in the Master's palm. Servant Nanak is a sacrifice, forever a sacrifice — Your expanse has no end or limit. ||4||5||
HJQL: Siri = upon the head. Siri siri = upon every head, for every being. Sanbahe = {samvahaya} conveys. Man = O mind! ||2||
O mind! Why are you afraid? The sustaining Prabhu Himself conveys sustenance to every being. ||2||
For each and every person, our Lord and Master provides sustenance. Why are you so afraid, O mind? ||2||
To every individual the Lord reaches sustenance, why fearest (you), O My soul?
Therefore (siri siri) head by head — that is, as many beings as there are — having created them all, the Thakur then conveys their (rijaku) food. Then, O mind! Why do you fear? ||2||
TYVV: Ude = udi. Ude udi = udi udi, having flown. Sai = hundreds (plural of 'sau'). Tisu pachhai = behind that (kunj). Bachre = the little chicks. Chharia = are left behind.
(O mind! Look! The kunj) comes flying and flying hundreds of kos, and behind her the chicks are left (alone).
The flamingoes fly hundreds of miles, leaving their young ones behind.
The flamingoes come having flown over hundreds of miles, their youngling they leave behind.
The flock of kunj comes flying and flying for hundreds of kos. And those kunj have left their chicks behind.
59FL: Chugavai = gives the picking. Mani mahi = within (that kunj's) mind. Simranu = the thought (of those chicks). Khalavai = feeds. Kavanu khalavai = who feeds them? No one feeds them anything. ||3|| 'Jaisi gagani phiranti udati, kapre bage vali. Uh rakhai chitu pichhai bichi bachre, nit hirdai sari samali.' (Gauri Bairagani M:4).
There is no one to feed them anything, no one gives them their picking. That kunj keeps the thought of her chicks within her own mind (and this Prabhu makes the means of their sustenance). ||3||
Who feeds them, and who teaches them to feed themselves? Have you ever thought of this in your mind? ||3||
Who feeds them and who causes them to peck? (Have you ever) thought of it in your mind?

Who (khalavai) fondles them, or feeds them their picking as a hen does? And who gives them the picking, who puts it in their mouth as the sparrow and the rest do? The sense being, no one gives it. Whichever of those flocking kunj has a chick, she does the simran of her own chick, and by that simran alone the sustaining takes place. Then why do you fear? ||3||
F2Z9: Sabhi nidhan = all treasures. Asat = eight. Das asat = eighteen. Sidhan = siddhis. Padam = gold and silver. Maha padam = diamonds and jewels. Sankh = fine food and clothing. Makar = the attainment of the science of arms, honour in the royal court. Mukandu = the attainment of the gentle arts such as rag. Kund = trade in gold. Nil = trade in pearl and coral. Kachhap = trade in cloth and grain. Kar tal = upon the palms of the hands.
O sustaining Prabhu! All the treasures of the world and the eighteen siddhis are (as it were) laid upon the palms of Your hands.
All the nine treasures, and the eighteen supernatural powers are held by our Lord and Master in the Palm of His Hand.
All the nine treasure and the eighteen supernatural powers, the Lord holds on the palm of His hand.

All the (padam and the rest) nidhis of every kind, and the eighteen siddhis there are — the Thakur has laid all these upon the palm of His own hand; the sense being, in giving them to His bhagats He makes no delay.
URFH: Paravaria = par-avar, the far and the near shore ||4||
O servant Nanak! Be for ever a sacrifice to such a Prabhu, for ever devoted, (and say — O Prabhu!) the end of the near and far shores of Your greatness cannot be found. ||4||5||
Servant Nanak is devoted, dedicated, forever a sacrifice to You, Lord. Your Expanse has no limit, no boundary. ||4||5||
Slave Nanak is devoted, dedicated and ever a sacrifice (to You, O Lord!) To Your vastness there is no limit or bound.

Sri Guru Ji says: to such a Maharaj let us go daily as a sacrifice again and again, and let us make supplication in this manner: O Hari! There is no end to Your far shore and near shore — the sense being, You are boundless. ||4||5||
5Z1H: The bani 'So Purakhu' of Guru Ramdas Ji, in Rag Asa.
Raag Aasaa, Fourth Mehl, So Purakh ~ That Primal Being:
Asa Measure, Fourth Guru. That Lord.
XLBA: Akal Purakh is One, and He is met through the grace of the Satguru.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but one God, by the true Guru's grace He is obtained.
546S: So = that. Purakhu = {puri shete iti purushah} He who is pervasive within every body. Niranjanu = nir-anjanu. Anjanu = soot, the influence of Maya} He upon whom the influence of Maya cannot fall. Agam = unreachable {gam = reach}. Apara = a-par, He whose far shore cannot be found, boundless.
That Parmatma is pervasive within all beings, (and yet) is above the influence of Maya, is unreachable, and is boundless.
That Primal Being is Immaculate and Pure. The Lord, the Primal Being, is Immaculate and Pure. The Lord is Inaccessible, Unreachable and Unrivalled.
That Lord is pure, Lord God is sans stain, God is unapproachable unintelligible and unrivalled.

Purakh is the name of the Virat. So You, Niranjan Purakh, were in the past tense also beyond mind and speech, unreachable. So You, Hari Niranjan Purakh, are unreachable in the present tense also. So You, Hari Purakh, will in the future tense also remain (apar) unreachable.
7A3W: Sabhi = all beings {plural of the word 'jiu'}.
O ever-abiding Hari, creator of all beings! All beings remember You always, all fix their attention upon You.
All meditate, all meditate on You, Dear Lord, O True Creator Lord.
All meditate, all meditate on You, O Reverend God, the True Creator!

O true Creator Hari! (Tudh) You alone did all meditate upon formerly, and now too all meditate, and hereafter too they will meditate. Although here there are two words 'dhiavahi', still one is to be supplied by implication; or, by mind and speech all beings meditate upon You alone.
R0RP: O Prabhu! All beings are Your own creation; You alone are the sustainer of all beings.
All living beings are Yours-You are the Giver of all souls.
All the creatures are Yours, You are the Bountiful to the living beings.
O Hari Ji! All beings are created by You, and You alone are the giver of enjoyment and of moksh to all beings.
Y4GD: O sant jano! Keep fixing your attention upon that Parmatma; He is the destroyer of all sorrows.
Meditate on the Lord, O Saints; He is the Dispeller of all sorrow.
O you saints! meditate on God, the Dispeller of all the distresses.
And I give this updesh: O brother sant jano! He who is the forgetter of all sorrows — the sense being, who removes sorrow and gives happiness — meditate upon that Hari Ji.
RSG2: He (being pervasive within all beings) is Himself the Master and Himself the servant. O Nanak! (Apart from Him) what are the poor beings? (Apart from that Hari the beings have no existence of their own.) ||1||
The Lord Himself is the Master, the Lord Himself is the Servant. O Nanak, the poor beings are wretched and miserable! ||1||
God Himself is the Master and Himself the servant, How insignificant the man is, O Nanak!1
O sants! Hari Himself is the Thakur, that is the Master, and Hari Himself is the servant. Sri Guru Ji says: what am I, a poor trifling being, that I could describe His praise? ||1||
